**Design — a mini-POS popup launched from a class on the Schedule page:**
- Open a class → its **attendee roster**. Pick a person → a **mini-POS cart** opens for them, pre-loaded with their **class drop-in charge** as a line item.
- On that cart you can: **remove the drop-in line** (and instead **add a package** they buy, or settle with an existing package credit), **add merchandise**, apply a **manual discount**, enter a **promo code**, pick a **payment method**, then **Complete** — which takes payment and **checks them in**. Then move to the next person.
- It reuses the existing POS backend (invoice/payment creation, promo validation `/api/promotions/preview`, package sale, merch stock, walk-in check-in) — no new payment engine.

Two decisions shape the build:

questions.question: Should the mini-POS cart be per-person (one checkout at a time) or one shared cart for the whole class?

options.label: Per-person (recommended)
options.description: Click a person in the class → their own cart opens (their drop-in pre-loaded). Add their merch/package/discount/promo, take their payment, check them in, then do the next person. Matches how a front desk checks people out one at a time and keeps each person's receipt clean.

options.label: One shared class cart
options.description: A single cart for the whole class where you add everyone's drop-ins + items and take one combined payment. Faster for a group paying together, but mixes people on one receipt and complicates per-person package/credit.

questions.question: Where should the mini-POS live in the code?

options.label: New popup in the class panel
options.description: Build a dedicated mini-POS modal inside the schedule's class detail panel that calls the existing POS/invoice endpoints. Self-contained, doesn't disturb the full POS page. More code but cleaner separation.

options.label: Reuse full POS in a modal
options.description: Load the existing POS checkout UI inside a popup on the schedule, pre-scoped to the person/class. Less duplicate code, but the POS page wasn't built to embed and may need significant refactoring to work in a modal.

- The instructor portal uses that catalog instead of the admin-only endpoint.

So on her portal, the granted pages (Clients, Bookings) will now appear under **Studio pages** (and Menu on mobile), and they'll stay put whether she's on Schedule, Earnings, or an admin page.

Once both deploy I'll confirm health. Then Nhi should refresh — she'll consistently see Schedule, Earnings, **and** her granted pages in every view.

# Soul Pilates — PRODUCTION Stack
#
#  Assumes you've copied soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz and
#  soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz onto the host and loaded them with:
#    docker load < soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz
#    docker load < soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz
#
#  Then:
#    cp prod.env.sample prod.env  # edit secrets
#    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
#
#  External access (mongosh / redis-cli from your dev machine):
#    MongoDB → host:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 27117)
#    Redis   → host:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 6479)
#    Both are auth-protected. Restrict access at the firewall to trusted IPs:
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 27117
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 6479
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port so the operator can run mongosh
      # from a dev machine. Auth is mandatory (MONGO_USER / MONGO_PASSWORD).
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27117}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port for direct redis-cli access.
      # Protected by REDIS_PASSWORD via --requirepass.
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6479}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6324:9000"      # S3 API — exposed so the public can fetch images
      - "127.0.0.1:6325:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s

  # One-shot that creates the soulpilates-public bucket (idempotent).
  # Runs after rustfs is healthy so it never races the S3 API startup.
  # Sets anonymous download policy so the frontend can fetch images directly.
  rustfs-bucket-init:
    image: minio/mc:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-bucket-init
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 $$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY $$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY &&
        mc mb --ignore-existing rustfs/soulpilates-public &&
        mc anonymous set download rustfs/soulpilates-public &&
        echo 'Bucket soulpilates-public ready.'
      "
    depends_on:
      rustfs:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    image: soulpilates/backend:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8391:8080"
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Production
      ASPNETCORE_URLS: http://+:8080
      MongoDbSettings__ConnectionString: "mongodb://${MONGO_USER}:${MONGO_PASSWORD}@mongo:27017/?authSource=admin"
      MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName: soulpilates
      JwtSettings__Secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
      # P4-S12 — optional previous-key slot for the rotation grace window.
      # Empty string is interpreted by Program.cs as "no previous key" (single-key mode).
      JwtSettings__PreviousSecret: ${JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET:-}
      StorageSettings__Endpoint: "http://rustfs:9000"
      StorageSettings__AccessKey: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      StorageSettings__SecretKey: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      StorageSettings__PublicBucket: soulpilates-public
      StorageSettings__PublicUrlBase: ${PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE}
      StorageSettings__ForcePathStyle: "true"
      StripeSettings__SecretKey: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}
      StripeSettings__PublishableKey: ${STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY}
      StripeSettings__WebhookSecret: ${STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET}
      StripeSettings__Enabled: ${STRIPE_ENABLED}
      # ───── SMTP / Email ─────
      SmtpSettings__Host: ${SMTP_HOST}
      SmtpSettings__Port: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      SmtpSettings__Username: ${SMTP_USERNAME}
      SmtpSettings__Password: ${SMTP_PASSWORD}
      SmtpSettings__FromEmail: ${SMTP_FROM_EMAIL}
      SmtpSettings__FromName: ${SMTP_FROM_NAME:-Soul Pilates Da Nang}
      SmtpSettings__Enabled: ${SMTP_ENABLED:-true}
      SmtpSettings__EmailRegisterVerificationEnabled: ${SMTP_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ENABLED:-true}
      # ───── Web Push (VAPID) ─────
      WebPush__Enabled: ${WEBPUSH_ENABLED:-true}
      WebPush__Subject: ${WEBPUSH_SUBJECT:-mailto:admin@soulpilates.com.vn}
      WebPush__PublicKey: ${WEBPUSH_PUBLIC_KEY}
      WebPush__PrivateKey: ${WEBPUSH_PRIVATE_KEY}
      # ───── Seed & CORS ─────
      AdminSeed__Enabled: "true"
      AdminSeed__Email: ${ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL}
      AdminSeed__Password: ${ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD}
      AdminSeed__Name: "Soul Pilates Admin"
      # CORS — single origin in path-split deployment
      CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      # ───── Public site (customer-facing absolute URLs in emails) ─────
      # EmailService builds verify-email, reset-password and "view account"
      # links against this base. Must match the host VestaCP serves publicly.
      PublicSite__BaseUrl: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      # ───── Timezone ─────
      TZ: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
      # ───── Observability ─────
      SentrySettings__Dsn: ${SENTRY_DSN}
    volumes:
      - ./data/soulpilates-api-logs:/var/log/soulpilates-api
    depends_on:
      mongo:
        condition: service_started
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      rustfs-bucket-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]

  frontend:
    image: soulpilates/frontend:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3719:80"
    networks: [public]


  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # GlitchTip (Sentry-compatible self-hosted error tracker) — P4-S10
  #
  # ALL FOUR SERVICES ARE INTERNAL-ONLY. There is no `ports:` mapping on the
  # `glitchtip` web service — the operator reaches the UI by SSH-tunneling
  # port 8000:
  #
  #     ssh -L 8000:localhost:8000 prod-host
  #     # then open http://localhost:8000 in a browser
  #
  # This matches the studio's existing security posture: admin surfaces are
  # tunneled, not internet-facing.
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  glitchtip-postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-glitchtip-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: glitchtip
      POSTGRES_USER: glitchtip
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${GLITCHTIP_POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/glitchtip-postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks: [internal]

  glitchtip-redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-glitchtip-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./data/glitchtip-redis:/data
    networks: [internal]

  glitchtip:
    image: glitchtip/glitchtip:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-glitchtip
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://glitchtip:${GLITCHTIP_POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@glitchtip-postgres:5432/glitchtip
      REDIS_URL: redis://glitchtip-redis:6379/0
      SECRET_KEY: ${GLITCHTIP_SECRET_KEY}
      PORT: "8000"
      GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN: ${GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN}
      # 30-day event retention — aligned with B2 Object Lock (P4-S11) so the
      # forensic window for both operational systems matches.
      GLITCHTIP_DEFAULT_EVENT_LIFETIME_DAYS: "30"
      EMAIL_URL: ${GLITCHTIP_EMAIL_URL:-consolemail://}
      DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL: ${GLITCHTIP_FROM_EMAIL:-glitchtip@soulpilates.com.vn}
    # NO ports: mapping — SSH tunnel only.
    depends_on: [glitchtip-postgres, glitchtip-redis]
    networks: [internal]

  glitchtip-worker:
    image: glitchtip/glitchtip:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-glitchtip-worker
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ./bin/run-celery-with-beat.sh
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://glitchtip:${GLITCHTIP_POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@glitchtip-postgres:5432/glitchtip
      REDIS_URL: redis://glitchtip-redis:6379/0
      SECRET_KEY: ${GLITCHTIP_SECRET_KEY}
      GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN: ${GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN}
      GLITCHTIP_DEFAULT_EVENT_LIFETIME_DAYS: "30"
      EMAIL_URL: ${GLITCHTIP_EMAIL_URL:-consolemail://}
      DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL: ${GLITCHTIP_FROM_EMAIL:-glitchtip@soulpilates.com.vn}
    depends_on: [glitchtip-postgres, glitchtip-redis]
    networks: [internal]

networks:
  internal:
    driver: bridge
  public:
    driver: bridge

content.text:
Building. Here's the safety net I built so you can test freely without any real customer getting test emails:

**Email test mode** (a single chokepoint — every email in the system routes through it):

- When **`SMTP_TEST_MODE=true`**, **no real customer receives mail**. Every message is either:
  - **redirected** to `SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO` (your inbox), with the intended recipient shown in the subject as `[TEST → customer@email]`, so you see exactly who *would* have gotten it, or
  - **dropped** entirely if no redirect address is set (logged for a trace).
- Addresses in **`SMTP_TEST_ALLOWLIST`** are exempt — they still get the real email (so your own account behaves normally).

I've pre-configured it in `prod.env`:
```
SMTP_TEST_MODE=true
SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO=haxkodi@gmail.com
SMTP_TEST_ALLOWLIST=haxkodi@gmail.com
```

So right now, once this deploys, **all outgoing emails will land in your inbox** (with the intended recipient in the subject) instead of reaching customers — perfect for testing booking confirmations, receipts, reminders, etc.

**When you're done testing:** set `SMTP_TEST_MODE=false` and redeploy the backend, and emails resume going to real recipients.

Two things to confirm once it's up:
1. Is `haxkodi@gmail.com` the right test inbox? If not, tell me and I'll change it.
2. Note `SMTP_ENABLED=true` already — so email *is* on; just make sure the SMTP credentials are valid (the password was a placeholder at one point) or nothing will send at all. Want me to check whether SMTP is actually configured to send?

I'll confirm health after deploy.

content.text:
## What a PTR record is

Regular DNS is **forward**: name → IP (e.g. `mail.soulpilates.com.vn` → `72.62.240.50`).

A **PTR record** (also called **reverse DNS / rDNS**) is the opposite: **IP → name** (`72.62.240.50` → `mail.soulpilates.com.vn`).

**Why it matters for email:** when your server connects to Gmail/Yahoo to deliver mail, they look up the reverse DNS of your IP and check that it's a real hostname that points back to that same IP. If the PTR is a generic host name (yours is currently `srv1782021.hstgr.cloud`) or doesn't match, they treat you as a suspicious/unconfigured sender and are far more likely to junk or reject your mail. Setting the PTR to your actual mail hostname is one of the strongest deliverability signals.

**Important:** PTR is **not** set in Cloudflare. Reverse DNS for an IP is controlled by whoever *owns the IP* — in your case, **Hostinger** (your VPS provider). So this one is done in the Hostinger panel, not Cloudflare.

## What you need to do (Hostinger VPS)

1. Log in to **hpanel.hostinger.com**
2. Go to **VPS** → select this server (the one at `72.62.240.50`)
3. Look for **IP Address / Networking**, and find the **rDNS** or **Reverse DNS / PTR** setting for `72.62.240.50`
   - It's often under: VPS dashboard → **Settings** → **IP address** (there's an edit/pencil icon next to the IP, or a "PTR record" field)
4. Change the value from `srv1782021.hstgr.cloud` to:
   ```
   mail.soulpilates.com.vn
   ```
5. Save.

That's it. It usually takes effect within a few minutes to an hour.

## One prerequisite to know

For the PTR to be valid ("forward-confirmed reverse DNS"), `mail.soulpilates.com.vn` must resolve **back** to `72.62.240.50` — which it already does (I verified it earlier). So you're good; just set the rDNS to `mail.soulpilates.com.vn`.

If you can't find the rDNS option in the panel, Hostinger sometimes requires you to submit it via **support chat** — just ask them to "set reverse DNS (PTR) for 72.62.240.50 to mail.soulpilates.com.vn." They'll do it.

Once it's set, tell me and I'll verify the PTR (and the DKIM/SPF records once you've added those) so we can confirm mail is authenticating cleanly before you go live.

Here's the honest picture, because there's one important catch:

## What BIMI needs
1. **DMARC enforced** — your record must be `p=quarantine` or `p=reject` (currently it's `p=none`, which BIMI won't accept).

Logo is live at **`https://new.soulpilates.com.vn/soulpilates-public/bimi/logo.svg`** (HTTP 200, correct `image/svg+xml` type). Now the two DNS records to add in Cloudflare:

## 1. Upgrade DMARC (required for BIMI)
BIMI won't work with `p=none`. **Edit** your existing `_dmarc.soulpilates.com.vn` TXT to:
```
v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:postmaster@soulpilates.com.vn
```
*(Safe now — you only send from this one authenticated server, and your mail passes SPF+DKIM. This just tells receivers to quarantine anything that fails, which your real mail won't.)*

## 2. Add the BIMI record
Create a new **TXT** record:
- **Name:** `default._bimi`

```
v=BIMI1; l=https://new.soulpilates.com.vn/soulpilates-public/bimi/logo.svg;
```
*(No `a=` certificate tag — that's the free, no-VMC version.)*

   - MongoDB C# driver throws on UNMAPPED fields; entities need matching properties (RoleModuleDefinition needed a `[BsonId]` Id).
   - Deployment: prebuilt Docker images; build backend `docker build -q -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .`; frontend `docker build -q --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://new.soulpilates.com.vn -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro`; deploy `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend`.

content.text:
Everything is built, deployed, and the core flow is verified. Here's where the account-activation migration stands.

## What I built

**Backend**
- `SendActivationEmailAsync` in [EmailService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/EmailService.cs) — welcome/activation copy (EN + VI subtitle), links to `/reset-password?token=…&activate=1`, "valid for 30 days".
- `ResetPasswordAsync` now also sets `EmailVerified = true` and clears the verification token — so setting a password via the emailed link **activates** the account. ([CustomerAuthService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/CustomerAuthService.cs))
- `SendActivationInvitesAsync(onlyClientId, onlyEmail, resend)` — creates a portal account (unverified, unusable random password, 30-day token) for each client with an email and no account, and emails the invite. Idempotent: existing accounts are skipped unless `resend` re-issues a fresh token to still-unverified ones. Single-target params for testing.
- Admin-only endpoint `POST /api/customer-migration/send-invites` ([CustomerMigrationController.cs](SoulPilates.API/Controllers/CustomerMigrationController.cs)).

**Frontend**
- [reset-password.astro](SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/reset-password.astro) shows activation copy ("Activate your account", "Activate my account", "Account activated") when `?activate=1`.
- New **"Account Activation Invites"** card in Settings → Emails tab: optional single-client test email, a "resend to unactivated" checkbox, confirm dialog, and a result summary (created / re-sent / skipped / no-email).

## What I verified end-to-end
Using a seeded account matching exactly what the invite creates, against the real public endpoints:
- ✅ `POST /api/customer/reset-password` with the 30-day token succeeded
- ✅ Account flipped to `EmailVerified: true`, token cleared
- ✅ Login with the new password succeeded (`emailVerified: true`)

Current DB state: **412 clients with an email, 2 existing accounts** — so a full run would create ~410 accounts.

## One thing I couldn't test, and why
Firing the actual admin endpoint (which sends the real activation *email*) needs an admin login. The seeded `ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD` in `prod.env` no longer works — the admin password was changed after deploy. I deliberately did **not** forge an admin token from `JWT_SECRET` (that's an auth bypass) or reset your production admin password.

**To finish the real-email test yourself:** log in as admin → **Settings → Emails → Account Activation Invites**, put your own address in the test field, and click send. In test mode all mail routes to haxkodi@gmail.com, so no real client gets anything. You'll get the activation email; click it, set a password, and confirm login. Once you're happy, leave the test field blank to run the full migration (remember to flip `SMTP_TEST_MODE=false` and redeploy before the real send, or invites will all land in your inbox instead of clients').

Want me to add a quick stats line to that card (e.g. "410 clients not yet invited") so you can see the scope before clicking?

Found it. Your click **did** reach the backend and returned success — but it created nothing and sent nothing (the response came back in 24ms; a real send would take much longer). Right now there are still only 2 accounts and **0 pending activations**.

The reason: the "send a test to one client first" field matches against **existing client records**, not arbitrary addresses. You almost certainly typed your own email (haxkodi@gmail.com) — but you're not a *client* in the system, so the filter matched zero people and the run did nothing. No client matched → no account → no email.

Two ways forward:

**Option A — test right now, no code change.** Because test mode redirects *all* mail to haxkodi@gmail.com anyway, enter a **real client's email** in that field. For example `jjujju928@hotmail.com` (client "Jeong Eun"). That creates their new-system account, and the activation email gets redirected to *your* inbox with a `[TEST → jjujju928@hotmail.com]` subject. You click it, set a password, and confirm the whole round-trip. No real customer is emailed. I'll clean up the test account afterward.

**Option B — I make the test field smarter.** I change it so that when you type an address that *isn't* a client, it still sends a real, working activation email to that address (a standalone test account) — so you can test with your own email directly. 3	namespace SoulPilates.Core.Entities;
4	
5	/// <summary>
6	/// An editable transactional email template (SPM-76). Stored as an embedded
7	/// sub-document inside <see cref="GlobalSettings.EmailTemplates"/> so the studio
8	/// owner can re-word any email from the admin Settings → Email Templates tab
9	/// without a code change.
10	///
11	/// <para>
12	/// Substitution convention: <c>{VariableName}</c> tokens (PascalCase) inside
13	/// <see cref="Subject"/> and <see cref="BodyHtml"/> are replaced at send-time by
14	/// <c>EmailService</c> with the live, HTML-encoded values for that send. The set
15	/// of tokens a template supports is fixed in code (the built-in defaults) — the
16	/// admin can move/remove/duplicate them but cannot invent new ones, because the
17	/// service only supplies the known dictionary keys.
18	/// </para>
19	///
20	/// <para>
21	/// SAFE-FALLBACK CONTRACT: when a stored template's <see cref="Subject"/> or
22	/// <see cref="BodyHtml"/> is blank (or the whole record is missing), the service
23	/// falls back to the hardcoded built-in default for that <see cref="Id"/>, so a
24	/// half-configured or never-touched template can never break a live email.
25	/// </para>
26	/// </summary>
27	public class EmailTemplate
28	{
29	    /// <summary>
30	    /// Stable template key — matches the constants in <c>EmailTemplateIds</c>
31	    /// (e.g. "booking-confirmation"). Used to look the template up at send-time
32	    /// and to backfill built-in defaults on read.
33	    /// </summary>
34	    public string Id { get; set; } = "";
35	
36	    /// <summary>
37	    /// Human-readable label shown in the admin list (e.g. "Booking Confirmation").
38	    /// Informational only — not used for substitution.
39	    /// </summary>
40	    public string Name { get; set; } = "";
41	
42	    /// <summary>
43	    /// The email subject line. May contain <c>{Token}</c> placeholders. Blank →
44	    /// service uses the built-in default subject for this <see cref="Id"/>.
45	    /// </summary>
46	    public string Subject { get; set; } = "";
47	
48	    /// <summary>
49	    /// The inner body HTML fragment (the per-template content — NOT the shared
50	    /// chrome, which <c>EmailTemplateHelper.Layout</c> still wraps around it).
51	    /// May contain <c>{Token}</c> placeholders. Blank → service uses the built-in
52	    /// default body for this <see cref="Id"/>.
53	    /// </summary>
54	    public string BodyHtml { get; set; } = "";
55	
56	    /// <summary>
57	    /// Tokens (without braces, e.g. "ClientName") that MUST appear — referenced as
58	    /// <c>{ClientName}</c> — somewhere in <see cref="Subject"/> + <see cref="BodyHtml"/>
59	    /// combined for the template to be considered valid. The update path rejects a
60	    /// save that drops any of these so an admin can't accidentally strip a critical
61	    /// field (e.g. a reset link) out of the email.
62	    /// </summary>
63	    public List<string> RequiredVariables { get; set; } = new();
64	
65	    /// <summary>
66	    /// All tokens the service can substitute for this template (superset of
67	    /// <see cref="RequiredVariables"/>) — surfaced in the admin UI as the
68	    /// "available variables" reference list. Informational; not persisted-critical.
69	    /// </summary>
70	    public List<string> AvailableVariables { get; set; } = new();
71	
72	    /// <summary>
73	    /// When false, the studio system will not auto-send this email. Staff can still
74	    /// trigger it manually. Defaults to true (all emails active).
75	    /// </summary>
76	    public bool IsEnabled { get; set; } = true;
77	
78	    // ── SPM-76 follow-up — transient fields for the admin editor (API response only) ──
79	    // [BsonIgnore] keeps these OUT of the stored document, so the "blank stored field =
80	    // use built-in default at send-time" contract (and future-default tracking) is preserved;
81	    // GetEmailTemplatesAsync fills them so the editor can show the default, support
82	    // "Reset to default", and render the Customised badge.
83	
84	    /// <summary>Built-in default subject — lets the editor's "Reset to default" restore it.</summary>
85	    [BsonIgnore] public string DefaultSubject { get; set; } = "";
86	
87	    /// <summary>Built-in default body HTML — for "Reset to default".</summary>
88	    [BsonIgnore] public string DefaultBodyHtml { get; set; } = "";
89	
90	    /// <summary>True when a stored non-blank override exists (drives the "Customised" badge).</summary>
91	    [BsonIgnore] public bool IsCustomised { get; set; }
92	}

Both features are built, compiled, and deployed. Here's the summary.

## 1. Review-request email (2h after first class)
- **New template** `review-request` — bilingual (EN/VI), with a ⭐ button linking to your Google page (`https://share.google/GXuGXXVZ3RIcQJ2KK`). It shows up in **Settings → Emails** like the others, so you can edit the wording or toggle it off. ([EmailTemplateDefaults.cs](SoulPilates.Core/Entities/EmailTemplateDefaults.cs))
- **Delivery logic** — a new hourly background job ([ReviewRequestService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/ReviewRequestService.cs)) finds classes that ended **2–24h ago** and emails a review request, but **only if it's that client's first-ever attended class**. Long-standing clients are never emailed (their first class is in the past, outside the window). Each attendance is tagged once handled, so nobody gets it twice — same durable, idempotent pattern as your existing class reminders.

## 2. Google Maps link in confirmations & reminders
- Added a **"📍 Get directions / Chỉ đường đến studio"** button (linking `https://maps.app.goo.gl/DKeX1rQVHAMSMy4j7`) to both the **booking confirmation** and **class reminder** default templates.

## Two things to know
- **Test mode is still on.** While `SMTP_TEST_MODE=true`, all of these — review requests and confirmations — redirect to haxkodi@gmail.com, so no real client gets them yet. They'll go out for real once you flip test mode off before launch.
- **The maps/review links are baked into the default template bodies.** If you later customize those templates in the editor, the links carry into what you edit — just don't delete them. (The review link is also a `{ReviewUrl}` token, so it's protected as a required variable there.)

content.text:
Temp endpoint gone (404), production is running the clean build. Done on all three fronts.

## 1. Full email redesign — premium, on-brand
Rebuilt the shared chrome ([EmailTemplateHelper.cs](SoulPilates.Services/Email/EmailTemplateHelper.cs)) and **all 10 templates** ([EmailTemplateDefaults.cs](SoulPilates.Core/Entities/EmailTemplateDefaults.cs)) to match the customer site's theme (`customer.css`):
- **Palette swap** — dropped the old Stripe-blue/`#635bff` + slate-navy look for the site's warm system: ivory canvas `#FAFAF8`, soft-charcoal header `#2C2C2C`, **orange brand accent `#EA6A24`**, hairline borders `#E8E5E0`, warm text greys. Success/danger now use the site's `#3D8C5C`/`#C44B4B`.
- **Premium touches** — rounded 18px card with a proper shadow, a "Soul·Pilates" wordmark header with an orange separator + accent rule, refreshed detail panels (`#F5F4F0` with row dividers and orange monospace reference codes), redesigned notice cards (grip-socks, cancellation, waitlist), consistent pill buttons, a real footer with address/link, and table-based layout for email-client compatibility.
- Reworked the code-built fragments too (receipt balance-owed row, generic-email CTA, cancelled-email heading) so nothing was left off-palette.

## 2. Unsubscribe — tested, works
The unsubscribe exists for the **retention check-in emails** (the "we miss you" nudges). I tested it end-to-end against the live public endpoint:
- Valid token → flips `RetentionRemindersOptedOut` to **true**, shows the confirmation page ✓
- Unknown token → same neutral 200 page, no crash, no account-enumeration ✓

Note: transactional emails (bookings, receipts, reminders) intentionally have **no** unsubscribe — only the retention nudges do, which is the correct pattern.

## 3. Sent test emails
Fired **5 samples** to haxkodi@gmail.com — booking confirmation, 24h class reminder, waitlist promoted, password reset, and the new review request. All five **delivered to Gmail** (`status=sent, 250 OK`), each subject-tagged `[TEST → …]` since test mode is still on. Check your inbox to eyeball the new design.

One thing worth flagging: **customized templates keep their old styling.** The redesign lives in the built-in defaults, so any template you've already edited in Settings → Emails still uses your saved HTML. If you'd edited any, hit "Reset to default" on those to pick up the new look. Want me to check whether any are currently customized?

content.text: I've mapped the funnel. The customer site is an Astro app: most funnel pages (`index`, `booking`, `checkout`, `account`, `packages`, `my-bookings`) share `CustomerLayout`, and `checkout.astro` completes every booking through a single `showConfirmation()` point — a clean place to fire the conversion. Before I build, two decisions shape what I write and what you'll set up:

questions.question: How deep do you want the tracking? This determines how well Meta can optimize (and how much setup is on your side).

options.label: Pixel + Conversions API
options.description: Browser Pixel AND server-side events sent directly from your backend to Meta, with deduplication. Best attribution and ad performance — survives iOS/ad-blockers/cookie loss. Needs a Meta access token from you and a bit more backend work.
options.preview:
Browser Pixel (client) + Conversions API (server)
• Recovers ~10-30% of conversions lost to blockers
• Meta's current best-practice for lead/booking ads
• You provide: Pixel ID + a system-user Access Token

options.label: Browser Pixel only (for now)
options.description: Standard client-side Pixel firing PageView, ViewContent, InitiateCheckout, Purchase, etc. Faster to ship; you only provide the Pixel ID. Can add Conversions API later.
options.preview:
Browser Pixel only
• Quick to launch — just needs your Pixel ID
• Some conversions lost to ad-blockers / iOS
• CAPI can be layered on afterwards

questions.question: Should booking conversions report a monetary value to Meta (enables value/ROAS optimization), or just count bookings?

options.label: Send booking value (recommended)
options.description: Each booking's price + currency (VND) is sent with the Purchase event, so you can optimize ads for revenue/ROAS, not just booking count. Package-credit bookings report the class's equivalent value.
options.preview:
Purchase event → value: 500000, currency: 'VND'
Unlocks Value Optimization & ROAS reporting

options.label: Count bookings only
options.description: Fire the conversion event with no value. Simpler; Meta optimizes for number of bookings only. You can't do ROAS/value bidding.
options.preview:
Purchase event → (no value)
Optimizes for booking count only

<!-- 
  GA4 Dynamic Loader & Funnel Tracker (Standalone pages)
  Include this partial in pages that DON'T use CustomerLayout.astro
  (e.g. index.astro, login.astro, register.astro).
  Pages using CustomerLayout already get this automatically.
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initGA4Standalone() {
    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch(e) {}

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/analytics/ga-config')
      .then(function(res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function(cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.measurementId) return;
        var gaId = cfg.measurementId;
        var enableEvents = cfg.enableEventTracking !== false;

        var s = document.createElement('script');
        s.async = true;
        s.src = 'https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=' + gaId;
        document.head.appendChild(s);

        window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
        function gtag() { window.dataLayer.push(arguments); }
        window.gtag = gtag;
        gtag('js', new Date());
        gtag('config', gaId, {
          page_path: window.location.pathname,
          send_page_view: true,
        });

        window.spTrackEvent = function(eventName, params) {
          if (!enableEvents || typeof gtag !== 'function') return;
          gtag('event', eventName, params || {});
        };

        window.addEventListener('popstate', function() {
          gtag('config', gaId, { page_path: window.location.pathname });
        });
      })
      .catch(function() {});

    if (!window.spTrackEvent) {
      window.spTrackEvent = function() {};
    }
  })();
</script>

input.content:
<!--
  Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel + Conversions API loader.
  Include in every customer-facing page's <head>. Pages using CustomerLayout get
  it automatically; standalone pages (login/register/onboarding/…) include it too.

  Exposes window.spMetaTrack(eventName, customData, userData):
    • fires the browser Pixel with a fresh eventID, AND
    • relays the same event (same eventID) to /api/meta/event so the backend
      forwards it to Meta's Conversions API — de-duplicated by eventID.
  Safe no-op until a Pixel ID is configured (Events Manager → env).
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initMetaPixel() {
    // Default to a no-op so callers never crash before config resolves.
    window.spMetaTrack = window.spMetaTrack || function () {};

    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch (e) {}

    function getCookie(name) {
      var m = document.cookie.match('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;]*)');
      return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null;
    }

    function uuid() {
      try { if (crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {}
      return 'e-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(16).slice(2);
    }

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/config')
      .then(function (res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.enabled || !cfg.pixelId) return;
        var pixelId = cfg.pixelId;

        // ── Meta Pixel base code ──
        !(function (f, b, e, v, n, t, s) {
          if (f.fbq) return; n = f.fbq = function () {
            n.callMethod ? n.callMethod.apply(n, arguments) : n.queue.push(arguments);
          };
          if (!f._fbq) f._fbq = n; n.push = n; n.loaded = !0; n.version = '2.0';
          n.queue = []; t = b.createElement(e); t.async = !0; t.src = v;
          s = b.getElementsByTagName(e)[0]; s.parentNode.insertBefore(t, s);
        })(window, document, 'script', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js');

        fbq('init', pixelId);
        fbq('track', 'PageView');

        // ── Dual Pixel + CAPI tracker ──
        window.spMetaTrack = function (eventName, customData, userData) {
          customData = customData || {};
          userData = userData || {};
          var eventId = uuid();

          try { fbq('track', eventName, customData, { eventID: eventId }); } catch (e) {}

          // Synthesize fbc from an ?fbclid= param if the cookie isn't set yet.
          var fbc = getCookie('_fbc');
          if (!fbc) {
            try {
              var p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('fbclid');
              if (p) fbc = 'fb.1.' + Date.now() + '.' + p;
            } catch (e) {}
          }

          var payload = {
            eventName: eventName,
            eventId: eventId,
            eventSourceUrl: window.location.href,
            email: userData.email || null,
            phone: userData.phone || null,
            fbp: getCookie('_fbp'),
            fbc: fbc,
            value: (customData.value != null) ? customData.value : null,
            currency: customData.currency || null,
            contentName: customData.content_name || null,
            contentCategory: customData.content_category || null,
            contentIds: customData.content_ids || null,
          };

          try {
            fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/event', {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify(payload),
              keepalive: true,
            }).catch(function () {});
          } catch (e) {}
        };
      })
      .catch(function () {});
  })();
</script>

Everything is built, compiles, deployed, and sitting dormant until you add your Pixel credentials. Here's the complete picture.

## ✅ My side (done)

**Server-side (Conversions API):**
- `MetaConversionsService` — hashes email/phone (SHA-256), attaches the visitor's IP + user-agent + `_fbp`/`_fbc` cookies, and posts events to Meta's Graph API.
- `GET /api/meta/config` (public — returns only Pixel ID, never the token) and `POST /api/meta/event` (first-party relay on *your* domain, so ad-blockers that kill `facebook.com` can't stop it).
- Config via env (like your SMTP secrets), not the DB — token never leaks.

**Browser Pixel + funnel events** (each fires the Pixel *and* the CAPI relay with a shared `eventID`, so they deduplicate):

| Event | Fires when | Value sent |
|---|---|---|
| `PageView` | every customer page | — |
| `ViewContent` | opens a class detail | class price |
| `InitiateCheckout` | reaches payment step | quote amount |
| **`Purchase`** | **booking confirmed** | **amount + VND + email/phone match** |
| `CompleteRegistration` | account created | + email/phone match |

The Pixel loads on all 7 customer pages (via `CustomerLayout` + the standalone auth pages). Right now `/api/meta/config` returns `enabled:false` — the whole thing is a safe no-op until you fill in the credentials.

## 📋 Your side (in Meta — ~15 min)

1. **Events Manager → Connect Data Source → Web** → create a **Pixel/Dataset**. Copy the **Dataset (Pixel) ID** (a long number).
2. In that dataset → **Settings → Conversions API → Generate access token.** Copy it.
3. **Verify your domain:** Business Settings → **Brand Safety → Domains** → add `new.soulpilates.com.vn`. Easiest method is the **DNS TXT** record in Cloudflare (you already manage DNS there). *(Or tell me and I'll drop Meta's verification `<meta>` tag into the site head instead.)*
4. **Aggregated Event Measurement:** Events Manager → your dataset → **Aggregated Event Measurement → Configure Web Events** → add & drag **Purchase to the top** priority. (Critical for iOS conversions.)
5. **When you run ads:** set the optimization event to **Purchase** — that's your booking conversion with value, so you can use Value/ROAS optimization.

## 🔑 To go live

Send me the **Pixel ID** and **Access Token** and I'll put them in `prod.env` (alongside your existing secrets) and redeploy — or you can set `META_PIXEL_ID` / `META_CAPI_TOKEN` there yourself. Then we **test together**: you open **Events Manager → Test Events**, give me the test code, I set it temporarily, and we watch a real booking fire both the browser + server event and confirm they deduplicate. Then I clear the test code.

Want me to add the domain-verification `<meta>` tag now (option 3), or will you do the DNS TXT route in Cloudflare?

content.text:
I've audited the whole system end to end. The good news: the app is almost entirely config-driven, so there's **only one hard-coded domain reference in code**. The migration is mostly infrastructure + a database rewrite. Here's the complete picture.

## What actually references `new.soulpilates.com.vn`

| Layer | Reference | Action needed |
|---|---|---|
| **DNS** | apex `soulpilates.com.vn` → **`72.62.69.9` (a different server!)**; `new.` → Cloudflare → this box (`72.62.240.50`) | Repoint apex to this server |
| **TLS** | Cert exists for `new.` only; **no apex cert** | Issue LE cert for apex + www |
| **nginx** | `/etc/nginx/sites-available/soulpilates`: `server_name new.`, cert paths, 2× `proxy_redirect` | Rewrite for apex + add `new.`→apex 301 |
| **Backend env** (`prod.env`) | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `PUBLIC_API_URL`, `PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE` | Point to apex → recreate backend |
| **Frontend** | `PUBLIC_API_URL` is **baked at build time** | Rebuild image with apex |
| **Database** | **1,639** `CalendarSessions` + **13** `ClassBlueprints` + **5** `Equipment` store absolute `ImageUrl`s with `new.` | Bulk-rewrite to apex |
| **Code** | `EmailTemplateHelper.cs` email-footer link (only hardcode) | Change + rebuild backend |
| **External** | BIMI DNS logo URL, Meta Pixel domain verification | You update in Cloudflare/Meta |

## What needs NO action (verified)
- **Mail** — SMTP is already `smtp.soulpilates.com.vn`, from `noreply@soulpilates.com.vn`, with DKIM/SPF/DMARC on the apex. Web move doesn't touch deliverability.
- **CORS** — follows `PUBLIC_APP_URL` (and appsettings already whitelists the apex).
- **PWA manifest / service worker** — relative scope/paths, no change.
- **Web Push subscriptions** — endpoints aren't domain-bound; keep working.
- **Stripe** — disabled, no webhook to update.
- **VisitorEvents.Referrer** (162) — historical analytics, harmless.

## Migration plan (sequenced for zero downtime)

**You (Cloudflare/Meta) — the gating step:**
1. Point apex `soulpilates.com.vn` (+ `www`) A-record to **`72.62.240.50`** (this server). Decide: keep Cloudflare proxy (orange) or DNS-only. ⚠️ It currently points to a *different* machine (`72.62.69.9`) — presumably your old site.
2. Leave `new.` DNS as-is so it can 301-redirect (protects the **30-day activation/reset links already emailed**, which point at `new.`).
3. After cutover: update the **BIMI** DNS record's logo URL to apex, and **re-verify the apex domain in Meta** + redo Aggregated Event Measurement (Purchase on top).

**Me (server) — once apex DNS resolves here:**
4. Issue Let's Encrypt cert for apex + www.
5. Update nginx: serve apex/www, add `new.`→apex 301 redirect.
6. Update `prod.env` (3 URLs) + fix the email-footer hardcode → recreate & rebuild backend.
7. Rebuild frontend with `PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn`.
8. Bulk-rewrite the 1,657 stored image URLs `new.` → apex.
9. Verify: apex loads, images render, booking→checkout→confirm, email links, Meta test event, login.

## One decision worth making now
Instead of rewriting stored image URLs to the apex (which would break again on any *future* domain change), I can make them **relative** (`/soulpilates-public/...`) — domain-agnostic forever. Slightly more involved but future-proofs you. Otherwise I'll just swap `new.` → apex.

Full-codebase review of Soul Pilates CRM ([[project_soul_pilates]]) on 2026-07-03.

**FIXED — Security (was live/exploitable):** `BookingController` had a class-level `[AllowAnonymous]` that overrode every method-level `[Authorize]` (Roslyn ASP0026). `GET /api/booking/session/{id}/waitlist` (Admin-only) leaked client name/phone/email to the public (confirmed 200 anon → now 401), and 4 `[Authorize(Roles="Customer")]` endpoints (client-context, waitlist join/me/leave) were unenforced. Fix: removed class-level `[AllowAnonymous]`, added it explicitly to the 9 public funnel actions. **Why the pattern is dangerous:** in ASP.NET Core `[AllowAnonymous]` ALWAYS wins over `[Authorize]` regardless of level — never put it at class level on a controller that also has protected actions. Other controllers use the safe inverse (class `[Authorize]` + method `[AllowAnonymous]`).

**FIXED — Meta tracking value bugs** ([[meta-pixel-tracking]]): Purchase/InitiateCheckout used `amountDueNow` (=0 for PACKAGE_CREDIT / PAY_AT_STUDIO) → now uses `sessionFee × quantity` (full class value). **PARTIALLY FIXED — Test suite (`SoulPilates.Tests`) does not compile.** Fixed the parts my work broke (added `SendActivationEmailAsync`/`SendReviewRequestAsync` to all IEmailService test doubles; backfilled ISettingsService/IInvoiceService/IWalletService stub members). REMAINING pre-existing rot (NOT yet fixed): ~10 integration-test files construct `SettingsService(ctx)` and `AccountingService(...)` with outdated ctor signatures (now need `IConfiguration`, `IPayrollService`, `IReceptionistKpiService`) and require a live Mongo. The suite has been non-compiling for a while → no automated safety net. Needs a dedicated repair pass.

**FLAGGED (not fixed) — dependency CVEs** from build: SixLabors.ImageSharp 3.1.5 (high), Snappier 1.0.0 (high), Microsoft.OpenApi 2.4.1 (high), SharpCompress 0.30.1 (moderate), AWSSDK.Core (low).

**Domain migration ([[project_soul_pilates]]):** extra item beyond the main audit — `build-images.bat` also defaults `PUBLIC_API_URL` to new.soulpilates.com.vn.

Double-check done, and the codebase review turned up real issues — including a live security hole. Here's the full report.

## Migration double-check — one item missed
- **`build-images.bat`** also defaults `PUBLIC_API_URL` to `new.soulpilates.com.vn`. Add it to the migration checklist. Everything else from before stands.

## Errors & discrepancies found

### 🔴 Live security vulnerability — FIXED & verified
`BookingController` had a **class-level `[AllowAnonymous]`** that silently overrode every method-level `[Authorize]` (compiler flagged it: ASP0026). Impact:
- `GET /api/booking/session/{id}/waitlist` — marked **Admin-only**, but was **publicly readable**, leaking **client names, phones, and emails** for any session. I confirmed it returned `200` to an anonymous request in production.
- 4 `[Authorize(Roles="Customer")]` endpoints (client-context, waitlist join/me/leave) were also unenforced.

Fixed by removing the blanket attribute and marking the 9 genuinely-public funnel actions explicitly. **Verified:** the Admin endpoint now returns `401`, while public schedule/class endpoints still return `200`/`404`. Guest checkout unaffected (`client-context` is only called with a token).

### 🟠 Meta tracking value bugs — FIXED
- **Purchase/InitiateCheckout** were sending `amountDueNow`, which is **0** for package-credit and pay-at-studio bookings — exactly the ROAS-skewing mistake I'd promised to avoid. Now sends `sessionFee × quantity` (true class value).
- **ViewContent** referenced `session.dropInPrice`, which **wasn't in the API response** (so it always sent 0). Added `DropInPrice` to the class-detail endpoint.

### 🟠 Test suite doesn't compile — PARTIALLY FIXED
- My two new `IEmailService` methods weren't implemented on 6 test doubles → **fixed** (plus backfilled other missing stub members).
- But this exposed **extensive pre-existing rot**: ~10 integration-test files build `SettingsService`/`AccountingService` with outdated constructor signatures (now needing `IConfiguration`, `IPayrollService`, `IReceptionistKpiService`) and a live Mongo. **The suite has been un-runnable for a while — no automated safety net.** Needs a dedicated repair pass (I didn't silently balloon into it).

### 🟡 Email-template test drift — FIXED
My redesign broke 2 `EmailTemplateHelper` assertions; I resolved it by making the design **more email-client-safe** (literal `DA NANG STUDIO`, kept the 📍) rather than weakening the tests.

### 🟡 Dependency CVEs — FLAGGED (not fixed)
Build reports known vulnerabilities: **SixLabors.ImageSharp 3.1.5 (high)**, **Snappier 1.0.0 (high)**, **Microsoft.OpenApi 2.4.1 (high)**, SharpCompress 0.30.1 (moderate), AWSSDK.Core (low). Worth a `dotnet` package bump.

## What I deployed this pass
Backend + frontend rebuilt and live with: the security fix, the Meta value fixes, `DropInPrice` in the API, and the email-chrome tweaks. All test-double fixes are in the repo (not deployed — test project only).

**Two things worth your decision:**
1. Want me to do the **test-suite repair** as a focused follow-up so you have a working safety net before the domain migration?

The standouts to scrutinize: `DevSeedController` (`[AllowAnonymous]` in prod?!), `SchedulingController`, `PaymentController`, `PackagePurchaseController`, `ClassBlueprintController`, `EquipmentController`, `PromotionController`.   echo "===================== $c ====================="
  grep -nE "\[Http(Get|Post|Put|Delete|Patch)|\[Authorize|\[AllowAnonymous|public.*Task.*Async\(|public IActionResult" "$f" | sed 's/^/  /'
done 2>/dev/null | head -120

content.text: `SchedulingController`, `PaymentController`, `PackagePurchase`, `ClassBlueprint`, `Equipment`, `Promotion` all use the **safe** per-method pattern (only intended public reads are anonymous). But **`DevSeedController` is `[AllowAnonymous]` with `seed-demo` and `purge-demo` (data-destroying) endpoints** — if that's compiled into production, anyone could wipe/inject data. This is the top priority:

`DevSeedController` gates every method behind an `X-Dev-Key` header that must equal the JWT secret — so it's not wide open. But two things matter: (1) does that config key actually resolve (if not, the gate may be accidentally disabled or accidentally locked), and (2) does `purge-demo` only delete demo-tagged data? Let me verify both:

input.command:
cd /opt/soulpilates && echo "=== how is the JWT secret actually configured/read elsewhere? ==="; grep -rnE "JwtSettings:Secret|JwtSettings__Secret|Jwt:Secret|Jwt__Secret|\"Jwt\"|JwtSecret|Jwt:Key|GetJwtSecret|jwtSecret =|_jwtSecret =" SoulPilates.API/Program.cs SoulPilates.API/appsettings.json | head
echo "=== does DevSeed's key config path resolve? (compare to what Program uses) ==="; grep -rn "config\[\|Configuration\[\|GetValue\|GetSection" SoulPilates.API/Program.cs | grep -i "jwt\|secret" | head
echo; echo "=== purge-demo: is the delete filtered to DEMO markers? ==="; sed -n '321,400p' SoulPilates.API/Controllers/DevSeedController.cs | grep -nE "DeleteMany|DeleteOne|Filter|MARK|REF_PREFIX|Regex|Authorised|Empty|FilterDefinition" | head -30

`DevSeedController` is gated by the JWT secret (same key Program.cs uses, so the gate is active) and `purge-demo` only deletes `DEMO_SEED`-marked rows — so it's not a wide-open hole, but shipping a data-purge tool in prod behind a hand-rolled header check is a hygiene risk worth flagging. Auth is now thoroughly mapped.

Let me pivot to **money correctness** — you previously flagged that POS package sales may create a PAID invoice without a `Payment` record, which would skew revenue. Let me trace how payments are recorded vs how revenue is reported:

content.text: Revenue-by-category comes from **Invoices**, but revenue-by-**method** uses Payment records. So a PAID invoice with no `Payment` doc wouldn't lose total revenue, but would desync the payment-method breakdown. Let me see how `ComputeRevenueByMethodAsync` handles invoices lacking payments:

content.text:
Full-system audit complete. I went well beyond recent changes — systematically sweeping auth, money, secrets, and concurrency across the whole codebase.

## What I audited & found

### 🔴 Auth / data exposure — swept all 40 controllers
- **`BookingController` PII leak** — found and **fixed/verified** last turn (Admin waitlist endpoint was public).
- **Every other controller checks out**: they use the safe pattern (class-level `[Authorize]` + method-level `[AllowAnonymous]`). Only intended public reads (schedule, class detail, quote, checkout-settings, promo preview, retention unsubscribe) are anonymous.
- **`DevSeedController` (low-med)** — `seed-demo`/`purge-demo` are compiled into production and `[AllowAnonymous]`, gated only by an `X-Dev-Key` header equal to the JWT secret. The gate *is* active (same config key Program.cs uses) and `purge` only deletes `DEMO_SEED`-tagged rows, so the blast radius is limited — but shipping a data-purge tool in prod behind a hand-rolled, secret-reusing header check is a hygiene risk. **Recommend env-gating to Development or removing.**

### 🟠 Concurrency — overbooking race (real, not yet fixed)
All three booking paths (`ReserveSpotAsync` online, walk-in, admin-add) do **check-then-act** on capacity: read `CurrentBookings`, validate, then unconditionally `Inc(CurrentBookings)`. Two customers racing for the **last seat** both pass the check and both increment → **overbooking**. The code comment even claims the guard prevents this, but it only holds single-threaded. Tellingly, merch **stock** already uses an atomic `FindOneAndUpdate` — capacity is the inconsistent one. **Fix:** atomic guarded increment (`filter: CurrentBookings <= Capacity - qty`), insert attendance only if it succeeds.

### 🟢 Money correctness — verified clean (good news)
Your long-standing worry that POS package sales create PAID invoices without `Payment` records: I measured it directly. Of **746** invoices, only **13** lack a Payment — and all 13 are **zero-value comps**. Total revenue reconciles with the payment-method breakdown. **This suspected bug does not exist in your data.**

### 🟡 Secrets — no leaks found
`User`/`CustomerAccount` (password hashes, tokens) are never returned raw — all endpoints use projections. `Staff` (which holds salary + bank account number) is returned raw only by the **Admin-only** controller. No exposure to lower roles.

## Honest scope note
I can't claim I read every line of a system this size — but I systematically covered the categories where real bugs hide (authorization, PII exposure, revenue math, concurrency, secret handling) and empirically validated the money path against the live DB.

## Open items (ranked)
1. **Overbooking race** — fix the 3 booking paths to atomic capacity guards (I recommend doing this before the domain migration/launch push).
2. **DevSeedController** — env-gate or remove.
3. **Test suite repair** (from last turn) — so these fixes can be regression-tested.
4. **Dependency CVEs** — bump ImageSharp/Snappier/OpenApi.

Want me to **fix the overbooking race** (carefully, atomic `FindOneAndUpdate` on all three paths) and **env-gate DevSeed** now? Those two are the most launch-critical.

Straight answer: **no — not literally every line with real comprehension, and I won't pretend otherwise.** The system is **~110,000 lines** (47K backend C# across 310 files + 62K frontend across 85 files). Anyone claiming a reliable line-by-line read of that in one pass is overselling — it'd degrade into skimming, and skimming is how you *miss* the subtle bugs while sounding thorough.

aiTitle: Soul Pilates CRM bug fixes and premium redesign

content.text:
Both option-C fixes are done, deployed, and verified in production.

## ✅ Overbooking race — fixed across every booking path
Added two helpers to `SchedulingService`:
- **`TryClaimSessionCapacityAsync`** — an atomic `FindOneAndUpdate` with `$expr: CurrentBookings + seats <= Capacity` (and `Status = SCHEDULED`). One DB round-trip claims the seat(s) or fails — no check-then-act gap.
- **`ReleaseSessionCapacityAsync`** — compensating release for rollback.

Applied to **all six claim sites**: online `ReserveSpotAsync` (fresh reserve + quantity-increase re-reservation), `BookClientAsync`, `WalkInCheckoutAsync` (with credit-refund rollback if the insert fails), `AdminAddStudentAsync`, and `AdminRescheduleBookingAsync` (target session, reordered after validations). Each pairs the atomic claim with rollback so capacity/credits never drift.

**Validated:** compiles, deployed, and I ran the exact `$expr` guard against all **1,020 live sessions** — it matched the manual has-room/full computation exactly (1011 vs 9). Two customers racing for the last seat can no longer both win.

## ✅ DevSeedController — fixed
Now injects `IWebHostEnvironment`; `seed-demo` and `purge-demo` return **404 outside Development** (verified 404 in prod). The JWT-secret header gate remains as a second layer. The data-purge surface no longer exists on the live studio.

Public booking reads still return 200 — nothing user-facing broke.

---

Per your **C** choice, that was "fix these two first, **then** audit." I've done the fixes. The deeper audit is still open — I've so far covered auth, PII exposure, revenue reconciliation, secret handling, and concurrency. The big remaining areas I haven't gone deep on:

- **Accounting/payroll engine** (`AccountingService`, commission tiers, washout splits, owner distributions) — money math, rounding, double-counting.
- **Wallet/credit ledger** (`WalletService`) — refund/forfeit correctness, negative-balance guards.
- **Stripe payment/webhook** dedup and idempotency (disabled now, but pre-launch).
- **Frontend funnel** logic beyond tracking.

Want me to continue into the **accounting + wallet** money paths next (highest business risk), or a different area?

message.content: give me a step by step guide on creating the meta pixel and ads for it to maximize bookings for the pilates studio in da nang vietnam mostly targeting foreign travellers

content.text:
Here's a complete, practical playbook — tailored to your studio, the Pixel+CAPI system I already built into the site, and specifically to reaching **foreign travelers in Da Nang**.

---

# Part 1 — Create the Meta Pixel (Dataset)

1. Go to **business.facebook.com** → **Business Settings**. If you don't have a Business Portfolio yet, create one (name it "Soul Pilates Da Nang").
2. **Events Manager** (left menu) → **Connect data sources** → **Web** → **Connect**.
3. Name the dataset **"Soul Pilates Web"** → enter your site URL `https://soulpilates.com.vn` (or `new.` for now).
4. When asked how to install, choose **"Do it manually" / "Use a partner or code"** — you don't need their code snippet, because the Pixel is *already installed on your site*. Just **copy the Dataset (Pixel) ID** (a ~15-digit number).
5. Skip the "add code" step — click through to finish.

# Part 2 — Get the Conversions API token & plug both into your system

1. In Events Manager → your dataset → **Settings** tab.
2. Scroll to **Conversions API** → **Generate access token** → copy it (long string). Treat it like a password.
3. Send me both the **Pixel ID** and **Access Token**, or set them yourself in `prod.env`:
   ```
   META_PIXEL_ID=<your pixel id>
   META_CAPI_TOKEN=<your access token>
   ```
   Then redeploy the backend. The site immediately starts firing PageView, ViewContent, InitiateCheckout, **Purchase** (with booking value), and CompleteRegistration — both browser Pixel *and* server-side CAPI, deduplicated. Nothing else to install.
4. **Verify it's live:** Events Manager → **Test Events** tab → it gives a test code; I set `META_CAPI_TEST_CODE` temporarily, you do one test booking, and we watch the events land + dedupe. Then I clear the code.

# Part 3 — Domain verification & Aggregated Event Measurement (do this before spending)

1. **Verify your domain:** Business Settings → **Brand Safety → Domains** → add `soulpilates.com.vn` → verify via **DNS TXT** in Cloudflare (easiest — you already run DNS there).
2. **Aggregated Event Measurement:** Events Manager → your dataset → **Aggregated Event Measurement → Configure Web Events** → drag **Purchase to priority #1**, then InitiateCheckout, ViewContent, etc. *(This is what makes conversions still count for iPhone users — and a lot of Western travelers are on iPhone.)*

---

# Part 4 — Build the campaign

1. **Ads Manager** → **Create** → objective **Sales** (this is the one that optimizes for purchases/bookings).
2. **Conversion location:** Website. **Dataset:** your Pixel. **Conversion event:** **Purchase**.
3. Structure: **1 campaign → 1–2 ad sets → 2–3 ads each.** Keep it simple at first; don't fragment a small budget.
4. Turn on **Advantage+ campaign budget** so Meta shifts spend to the winning ad set.

⚠️ **Reality check on volume:** Meta's algorithm wants ~**50 Purchase conversions per week** per ad set to optimize well. A boutique studio may not hit that at first. So:
- **Weeks 1–3:** optimize the ad set for **"Initiate Checkout"** or **"View Content"** (far more frequent) to gather signal and let the pixel learn.
- **Once you're getting steady bookings,** switch to optimizing for **Purchase**. This two-stage ramp avoids the ad set getting "stuck in learning."

---

# Part 5 — Targeting foreign travelers in Da Nang (the important part)

This is where most studios get it wrong — they target everyone in Da Nang and burn budget on locals who won't book English-language Pilates. Do this instead:

**Location**
- Set location to **Da Nang** (drop a pin on your studio area — An Thượng / My Khe beach / Son Tra, where tourists cluster — and set a **radius of ~10–15 km**).
- Critical: change the location dropdown from "People living in or recently in this location" to **"People traveling in this location"** (or "Recently in this location"). This is the single most important setting for reaching tourists rather than residents.

**Language**
- Set **Language = English** (and add **Korean** and **Russian** — Da Nang's biggest tourist groups). This alone filters out most Vietnamese locals.

**Age / gender**
- Pilates travelers skew **female, 25–55** — but don't hard-exclude men; start **all genders, 25–55** and let the data narrow it.

**Detailed targeting (interests) — layer these**
- **Travel:** "Traveling", "Frequent international travelers", "Digital nomad", "Expats", "Vietnam travel".
- **Wellness:** "Pilates", "Yoga", "Reformer", "Physical fitness", "Wellness", "Healthy lifestyle", "Meditation".
- Meta's **Advantage+ detailed targeting** will expand beyond these once it finds bookers — leave it on.

**Two ad sets worth A/B testing**
- **Ad set A — "Traveling in this location" + wellness interests** (tourists actively in Da Nang now — highest intent, book this week).
- **Ad set B — Expats/digital nomads living in Da Nang + English/Korean** (longer-term members, retarget-able).

**Retargeting (add after ~2 weeks of pixel data)**
- Create a **Custom Audience** from your Pixel: "ViewContent or InitiateCheckout, last 14 days, no Purchase." Show them a "Still deciding? First class special" ad. Travelers have short windows — retarget fast.
- Build a **Lookalike (1–3%)** off your Purchasers once you have ~100 bookings.

---

# Part 6 — Creative that converts travelers

- **Video/Reels win** for this audience — a 10–20s clip of a bright class, the reformer, ocean/Da Nang vibe, smiling international clients.
- **Lead with the traveler angle:** "Keep your practice while you travel — drop-in Reformer Pilates in Da Nang." "English-speaking instructors. Book online in 60 seconds."
- **Reduce friction / urgency:** "First-timer drop-in," "No membership needed," "Book your spot tonight."
- **Show the booking is easy** — a screen of your booking page. Travelers won't call or DM; they want to tap and book.
- Run ads on **Instagram + Facebook + Reels** placements (Advantage+ placements on). Instagram over-indexes with this audience.
- Put a clear **CTA button = "Book Now"** linking straight to `https://soulpilates.com.vn/booking`.

---

# Part 7 — Budget & timeline

- **Start:** ~**$10–20/day** total for 1–2 weeks to gather signal. Don't judge results in the first 3–4 days (learning phase).
- Once an ad set is producing bookings profitably, **scale ~20% every few days** — big jumps reset learning.
- Kill ads with high cost-per-InitiateCheckout and no bookings after ~$30–50 spent; double down on winners.

# Part 8 — Measure & iterate

- In Ads Manager, add columns for **Purchases, Cost per Purchase, Purchase ROAS** (these come from the Pixel/CAPI I wired up — Purchase carries the real class value, so ROAS is meaningful).
- Watch **Events Manager → your dataset** for event volume and the **Event Match Quality** score (CAPI + hashed email/phone from checkout should keep this "Good/Great").
- Every 1–2 weeks: cut the worst ad, clone the best with a new creative, refresh the retargeting audience.

---

## What's blocking go-live
Everything on the **technical side is already built and deployed** — it's dormant until you paste the **Pixel ID + Access Token**. Send me those (Part 2), tell me whether you want the **DNS TXT** domain-verification route or for me to add Meta's `<meta>` tag, and we'll do a live Test-Events booking together to confirm tracking before you spend a dong on ads.

Want me to (a) drop the domain-verification `<meta>` tag in now so that step's ready, and (b) write the 2–3 starter ad copy variations (EN + KR) you can paste straight into Ads Manager?

Smart to split them — private (therapeutic) and group are very different buyers. But **the therapeutic angle has a real Meta-policy trap** you need to know before writing a single word, so let me cover that first, then give you compliant copy for both.

## ⚠️ Read this first — health-ad rules (this gets ads rejected or worse)

1. **Meta's "Personal Attributes" policy** bans ads that *imply you know the viewer's condition.* So **"Do you suffer from back pain?"**, **"Struggling with scoliosis?"**, **"Your chronic pain…"** → **rejected**. You must use general, benefit-led language: *"Pilates for a stronger, healthier back."*
2. **No medical/cure claims.** Don't say Pilates **treats / cures / heals** scoliosis or back pain. Safe verbs: **support, strengthen, improve mobility/posture, adapt to your body.**
3. **Put the specifics on the landing page, not the ad.** You *can* name scoliosis, disc issues, post-injury, posture etc. on your **booking page / class description** — that's informational and fine. Keep the *ad* general to get it approved.
4. **Make sure it's true.** Only run the therapeutic angle if you have an instructor genuinely qualified for rehab/clinical Pilates. Consider a "not a substitute for medical advice — consult your doctor" line on the page.

content.text:
Great question — and there's an important distinction here that's worth understanding, because it explains what you're seeing on other sites.

## What's controlled where
- **The embedded card fields you're looking at** (the "Payment Element") are styled by **our code**, via Stripe's `appearance` API — *not* the Stripe Dashboard. That's what I just modernized. Changing settings in the Stripe Dashboard won't restyle those specific fields.
- **The Stripe Dashboard *does* control** the look of Stripe's **own hosted pages** (the full-page Checkout, Payment Links, invoices, receipts, and the "Link" experience) — via **Settings → Branding** (your logo, brand color, accent, icon). Worth setting regardless.

## The "nicer forms" you've seen are almost always one of these
Most premium-looking Stripe checkouts aren't a *differently styled card form* — they're using extra Stripe features:

1. **Express Checkout buttons** — **Apple Pay / Google Pay / Link** one-tap buttons sitting *above* the card fields. This is the single biggest "modern & trustworthy" upgrade, and it's huge for your audience: **foreign travelers pay in one tap with the card already in their phone's wallet** — no typing card numbers. Enabled in Dashboard (turn on the wallets) + a small code addition.

2. **Stripe-hosted Checkout** — instead of an embedded form, you redirect to Stripe's own beautifully-designed page (`checkout.stripe.com`), fully branded from the Dashboard. It's the most polished with the least code, handles wallets automatically — the trade-off is it's a **redirect away** from your site (or an embedded iframe version).

3. A well-tuned **Payment Element** (what we have) with wallets on — often what people *think* is a custom form.

## My recommendation
Do **both** of these:
- **In the Dashboard now:** Settings → **Branding** → upload your logo + set brand color to your orange `#EA6A24`. And **Settings → Payment methods** → enable **Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Link**.
- **In code:** I add an **Express Checkout Element** (the Apple/Google Pay/Link buttons) above the card form. Quick change, and it's the biggest visual + conversion upgrade.

---

Which direction do you want?

- **(A)** Keep the embedded form + **add Apple Pay / Google Pay / Link buttons** (recommended — modern, one-tap, stays on your site). I wire it up; you enable the wallets in the Dashboard.
- **(B)** Switch to **Stripe-hosted Checkout** (most polished, least custom, but redirects off-site). I convert the flow.
- **(C)** Just keep refining the **embedded form's** styling further (spacing, single-line layout, etc.).

I'd go **A**. Want me to build it?

content.text:
You're right, and here's the honest reason why: **Shopify's checkout isn't Stripe's form at all.** Shopify built their *own* checkout UI (Stripe/Shopify Payments runs underneath as the processor, but the clean form you see is Shopify's proprietary interface, refined over a decade). So you literally can't get "that exact look" out of Stripe's embedded element — no amount of CSS gets you Shopify's checkout, because it isn't Stripe's.

What you *can* get that's genuinely **clean and smooth** falls into two buckets:

## 1. Stripe Checkout (hosted or embedded) — the closest to that Shopify feel
This is **Stripe's own** full checkout page — the polished, single-column, animated, conversion-optimized one Stripe designed themselves. It's what a lot of "nice" Stripe sites actually use. Two flavours:
- **Embedded Checkout** — Stripe's clean form dropped into *your* page (an iframe), so it still feels on-site. Smooth, wallets built in, brandable from the Dashboard.
- **Hosted Checkout** — redirect to `checkout.stripe.com`, then back. Most polished, least code, but it leaves your page.

Both are branded from **Dashboard → Branding** (logo + your orange), and they handle Apple Pay / Google Pay / Link automatically. This is the realistic way to get "Shopify-clean."

## 2. Keep the embedded Payment Element, but declutter + add wallets
The current form's biggest "not clean" offenders are the **"Secure, fast checkout with Link" bar** cluttering the top and the tighter spacing. I can strip Link out, open up the spacing, and add the Apple/Google Pay buttons. It gets meaningfully cleaner — but it still won't *match* Shopify, because it's a fundamentally different (more compact) component.

---

## My honest take
If "clean and smooth like Shopify" is the goal, **go with Embedded Stripe Checkout** (option 1, embedded flavour). It's Stripe's best-looking form, stays on your domain, and it's what actually gets you that feel — the embedded Payment Element will always be the more compact, utilitarian one no matter how I style it.

The trade-off: it's a real integration change (backend creates a Checkout Session instead of a PaymentIntent, frontend mounts the embedded checkout, plus webhook wiring). Since Stripe's still disabled and you're pre-launch, now's the right time to do it.

Done — the card step is now **Stripe's Embedded Checkout** (their own clean, branded form), deployed. Here's the important context.

## What changed
- **Backend:** the real-Stripe path now creates a **Checkout Session** (`ui_mode: embedded`) instead of a bare PaymentIntent. Crucially, it puts the same booking metadata on the underlying PaymentIntent, so your **existing webhook + confirmation finalization is completely reused** — I didn't touch the proven money-finalizing logic, which keeps the blast radius small.
- **Frontend:** when Stripe returns an embedded session, the checkout mounts Stripe's embedded form (`initEmbeddedCheckout`) with its own pay button; on completion it fires your confirmation screen (and the Meta Purchase event). The old Elements form stays as a fallback for the dev/mock path.

## Two things you need to know

**1. The look now comes from Stripe's Dashboard, not our CSS.** Embedded Checkout is Stripe's own UI — that's *why* it's cleaner. To brand it:
- **Dashboard → Settings → Branding** → upload your logo, set the **brand/accent color to `#EA6A24`**, background/icon. That styling flows straight into the embedded form.
- **Dashboard → Settings → Payment methods** → enable **Apple Pay / Google Pay / Link** — they'll appear automatically as one-tap buttons (huge for travelers).

**2. I could NOT test the live payment flow — Stripe is currently disabled** (`STRIPE_ENABLED=false`), so right now checkout still shows the dev mock stub. The embedded form only appears once you turn Stripe on with real keys. **This must be tested with Stripe TEST keys before you go live.** Both the backend and frontend compile and deploy cleanly, but the actual card flow needs a real Stripe session to exercise.

## To test it (recommended before launch)
1. In the admin **Settings → Payments**, enable Stripe with your **test** publishable + secret keys (and set the webhook secret; the webhook endpoint is already `/api/payment/webhook`).
2. Set the **Branding** in the Stripe Dashboard.
3. Do a test booking that requires payment (deposit or full) → you'll see the embedded form → pay with Stripe's test card `4242 4242 4242 4242` → confirm the booking finalizes and the confirmation screen shows.

## Direct link (fastest)

content.text:
Deployed. The review-request email now has three gates before it goes out:

## Who gets the review email now
A customer receives it **only if all** are true:
1. **Checked in** — status is `CHECKED_IN` (they physically turned up and were marked in at the desk). No-shows (still `BOOKED` / `NO_SHOW`), cancellations, and late-cancels are all excluded.
2. **Paid / settled** — nothing owed (`AmountDueAtStudio` is 0 or null). This covers package-credit, fully-paid-online, and pay-at-studio once collected on check-in. Anyone who attended but still owes money is skipped.
3. **It's their first checked-in class** — and it's ~2h+ after that class ended.

So a cancellation or no-show can never trigger it, and neither can an unpaid booking.

## One thing worth knowing
This now **depends on your team actually marking check-ins**. If a customer attends but the receptionist never marks them `CHECKED_IN`, no review email goes out. That's the correct trade-off (better to miss one than email a no-show) — just make sure check-in is part of your desk routine.

Also, a minor timing note: the check-in + payment need to be recorded within ~24h of the class (the send window). Since both normally happen live at class time, that's not an issue in practice.

Everything else about it is unchanged — still test-mode-safe (routes to your inbox until you flip `SMTP_TEST_MODE=false`), still one-per-customer, bilingual, links to your Google page.

content.text:
Fixed and cleaned up. This-month revenue dropped from ₫11,400,000 → **₫7,075,000** — the ₫4,325,000 of voided test transactions is gone.

## What was wrong
Voiding an invoice only set its status to `VOIDED` — it **left the payment records untouched**. Your dashboard "Monthly Revenue" is calculated from **payments** (money received), not invoice status, so the voided invoices' payments kept counting. The P&L/washout had a related gap (it summed all invoices, including voided).

## What I fixed (deployed)
1. **`VoidInvoiceAsync` now reverses the payments** — when you void an invoice, its linked payment records are removed, so revenue drops immediately. The audit log (original `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` events + the `VOID` event) preserves the full history, so nothing is lost from the record.
2. **P&L/washout now excludes voided invoices** from revenue and the per-method breakdown.

## Cleaned up your test data
Removed the 2 orphaned payments (₫500,000 booking + ₫3,825,000 package) that your earlier voids left behind. Your dashboard revenue is now correct.

## One thing to check
- The **dashboard revenue KPI** recalculates live — it's already correct.
- If you have a **saved P&L / monthly washout** for July that you generated earlier, **re-run/refresh it** so it picks up the exclusion (stored washouts don't auto-recompute).

Going forward, voiding any invoice will automatically pull its revenue back out — no manual cleanup needed.

All three are live. Here's what you now have:

## 1. Lifetime value in the profile view
The regular client profile (not just edit mode) now shows **💰 Lifetime value: ₫X** right under the name.

## 2. Automatic VIP badge
Any client whose lifetime spend reaches **₫10,000,000** gets a **👑 VIP** badge on their profile — computed automatically, no manual tagging. **20 clients already qualify** from your historical data.

## 3. VIP tab on the clients page
A new **👑 VIPs** tab sits next to Packages, listing all VIP clients (highest spender first) with their lifetime value. Click any row to open their profile.

## Bonus: lifetime value is now kept live
This was important — `LifetimeValue` was previously a **frozen snapshot from your data import** and never updated. So "spends 10M or more" would have been stuck at import values forever. I fixed that:
- **Every payment** now adds to the client's lifetime value (all booking/package/POS payments flow through one path).
- **Refunds and voids** subtract from it.

So VIP status updates **automatically as customers spend** — a client who crosses ₫10M in the new system becomes a VIP without any manual step. (This also ties into the void fix from earlier — voided sales now correctly reduce lifetime value too.)

## Two notes
- The automatic **👑 VIP** (badge + tab, spend-based) is **separate** from the manual **"VIP" tag** preset you already had — they don't interfere. If you'd rather the manual tag drive it, or want both, tell me.
- The threshold is **₫10,000,000** as you specified. If you ever want it adjustable from the admin Settings screen rather than fixed in code, I can wire that up.

Want me to also show a small 👑 next to VIP clients in the **main Clients list** (not just the VIP tab)?
