Done — all deployed and validated against your real data: **16 VIP + 4 Super VIP** clients right now.

## What you now have

**Tiers (auto, spend-driven):**
- **👑 VIP** — lifetime spend ≥ **₫10M** (gold chip)
- **💎 SUPER VIP** — spend ≥ **₫20M** *and* ≥ **20 checked-in classes** (purple chip)

**The VIP chip shows next to the name everywhere:**
- Main **clients list** rows
- **Client profile** (next to their name)
- The **👑 VIPs tab** (now shows the tier + classes attended, Super VIPs listed first)

**Settings (Admin → Settings → Integrations → 👑 VIP Program):**
- **Enable/disable** the whole VIP program
- **VIP minimum spend**
- **Super VIP minimum spend** + **minimum classes attended**
- Saves via a dedicated update so it never disturbs other settings, and the thresholds are preserved across any other settings save.

**Everything stays live** — since lifetime value now updates on each payment (and drops on refund/void), and class counts come from actual check-ins, a client is promoted to VIP/Super VIP automatically the moment they cross the thresholds. No manual step.

## One design note
I implemented the "VIP tag next to their name" as an **automatic derived chip** (always accurate, updates itself) rather than writing a literal `"VIP"` entry into the client's manual **Tags** list. This avoids stale/conflicting tags. Your existing manual **"VIP" tag** preset still works independently.

If you'd rather I *also* auto-write an actual `VIP` / `Super VIP` **tag** into each qualifying client's tags (so it flows into tag-based filters/exports), I can add that — just say the word. Want me to?

content.text:
All done and deployed. Here's everything:

## Clients page
- **Pagination: 12 → 25** per page.
- **"Member since"** column added (month + year).
- **"Credits"** column — shows remaining **Group / Mat / Private** credits as color-coded pills (only the ones they have; "—" if none). Fetched efficiently via one aggregation.
- **Search autofill** — added `autocomplete="off"` plus the anti-autofill tricks (search type, non-email field name, LastPass/1Password ignore hints). This should stop the email dropdown; Chrome is occasionally stubborn about it, but this is the standard fix and works in the large majority of cases.

## Calendar light mode
- **Gray bar fixed** — the header bands (title + toolbar) had no background, so the page's off-white showed through as a gray strip. They're now explicitly white, matching the grid.
- **Cards more readable** — each class card now has a **full hairline border + soft shadow** (so they separate cleanly from the white grid and each other) and a **firmer color tint**, while keeping the thick colored left border for format. Dark, high-contrast text.

## "Users & Access" page — I did NOT remove it
It was **hidden**, not deleted. The sidebar only shows a page if its module is in your role's enabled-modules list — and `user-access` had been dropped from your admin role. The real cause: `user-access` was never in the **module catalog**, so the last time Role Access was saved through the UI, it silently got dropped. I fixed it two ways:
1. **Re-enabled** `user-access` for admin/superadmin/owner (it's back now).
2. **Added it to the module catalog** so it now appears as a real toggle in Settings → Roles & Access and won't get dropped again.

**Refresh the page** and "Users & Access" will be back in the sidebar (it's also always at `/admin/access`).

content.text:
I now have the complete picture. Here's the full migration audit.

## Current architecture (verified)

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| **DNS zone** | `soulpilates.com.vn` nameservers = Cloudflare (`jonah`/`zara.ns.cloudflare.com`) — whole zone is in Cloudflare |
| **`new.soulpilates.com.vn`** | Cloudflare-proxied (orange cloud) → origin = **this** server's nginx → Let's Encrypt cert for `new.` |
| **`soulpilates.com.vn` + `www`** | Point to **`72.62.69.9`** — a *different* server running the **old** "Da Nang Pilates Studio" marketing site (nginx, DNS-only/grey cloud) |
| **This server nginx** | Only has a server block for `new.`; routes `/api/` + `/hubs/` → backend `:8391`, `/soulpilates-public/` → storage `:6324`, `/` → frontend `:3719` |
| **App config** | `prod.env`: `PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `PUBLIC_API_URL`, `PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE` all = `https://new.soulpilates.com.vn`; these feed `CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0` and `PublicSite__BaseUrl` |
| **Frontend** | `PUBLIC_API_URL` is **baked into the JS bundle at build time** (Astro inlines `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_API_URL`) — app makes **absolute** API calls to `new.` |

**The core reality:** the apex isn't free — it's actively serving a *different* live website on another server. Migration = repoint apex/www to this CRM **and** retire the old site.

---

## What needs to change

### 1. DNS — Cloudflare (you must do; I have no access)
- Change the **`soulpilates.com.vn`** (apex) and **`www`** records from `72.62.69.9` to **this server's IP**, set to **Proxied** (orange cloud) — matching how `new.` is set up.
- Keep **`new.`** as-is for now (needed for the redirect + already-sent email links — see §8).

### 2. TLS cert — nginx origin (this server)
- Issue a Let's Encrypt cert covering `soulpilates.com.vn` **and** `www.soulpilates.com.vn`. Because apex will be Cloudflare-proxied, use **DNS-01** challenge (Cloudflare token) or temporarily grey-cloud during HTTP-01 issuance. A **Cloudflare Origin Certificate** is the cleanest alternative.

### 3. nginx — new server block (this server)
- Add a server block for `soulpilates.com.vn` + `www` that mirrors the existing `new.` block (same `/api/`, `/hubs/`, `/soulpilates-public/`, `/` proxy_pass targets) with the new cert.
- Add a `www → apex` 301 redirect.

### 4. App config — `prod.env` (this server)
Change these three to the apex:
```
PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn
PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn
PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE=https://soulpilates.com.vn/soulpilates-public
```
These propagate to CORS (`CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0`) and email base URL (`PublicSite__BaseUrl`). **Recommend adding `new.` as a second allowed CORS origin** during the transition so nothing breaks mid-cutover.

### 5. Frontend — **must rebuild** (this is the critical one)
The API base is compiled into the bundle. Rebuild with the apex:
```
docker build -q --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro
```
Then redeploy backend + frontend. Without this, pages served at the apex would still fire API calls at `new.` (cross-origin/CORS + hard dependency on `new.` staying alive).

### 6. Data migration — stored absolute media URLs
Image URLs are persisted absolute in the DB (they'll 404 if `new.` is ever removed):
- `CalendarSessions.ImageUrl` — **1,639 docs**
- `ClassBlueprints.ImageUrl` — 13 docs
- `Equipment.ImageUrl` — 5 docs

Fixed and deployed. Here's what happened and what you need to do:

## What went wrong
Your Stripe keys were **wiped by a settings save**, not by anything payment-related. The general Settings save does a full-document replace and is supposed to carry forward fields it doesn't manage (email templates, VIP, and Stripe keys). The guard for Stripe (`PreserveStripeKeysIfAbsent`) **existed but was never actually called** — so the moment any General/Payments setting got saved, it reset `StripeEnabled=false` and blanked the encrypted keys. That's why the first transaction worked and the next one dropped into "Development mode."

**This was a latent bug, not something you did wrong.**

## The fix (live now)
I wired `PreserveStripeKeysIfAbsent` into `UpdateAsync` and deployed it. Now any settings save carries the Stripe keys + enabled flag forward — they won't be wiped again.

## What you need to do — re-enter the keys
The keys are currently blank in the DB, so payments are in mock mode until you re-enter them:

**Admin → Settings → Stripe Gateway Configuration** → paste Publishable / Secret / Webhook Secret → enable → **Save**.

This is the ideal moment to use a **freshly rolled `sk_live_`** (Stripe → Developers → API keys → Roll), since the earlier one was exposed in this chat. Enter the rolled secret + your `pk_live_` + the `whsec_`.

Once you've saved, tell me and I'll re-verify from the server (enabled + keys present) and confirm a real create-intent returns a live publishable key — then the "development mode" message is gone for good. With the fix in place, it'll stay put through future settings changes.

Both changes are built and deployed. Here's what changed:

## Req 1 — Online fee (VAT) now applies to packages
Package purchases were charging the bare package price with **no** online fee. Now the same **5% VAT (online only)** surcharge is applied, consistent with class bookings:
- `PackagePurchaseController` computes the fee from `OnlinePaymentFeePercentage` and stamps it on the invoice's `OnlineFeeAmount` → `CreateInvoiceAsync` folds it into `TotalNet`, so the customer is billed **base + VAT** and it shows on the receipt as a "VAT (online only)" line.
- Example — 10 Group Class Pack: `4,250,000` + 5% (`212,500`) = **`4,462,500`** charged.
- The package payment page now **itemizes** it: package price, VAT line, then Pay Now total.

## Req 2 — Class options page no longer bundles the fee
On the option-selection page (your screenshot), the prices now show the **base amount** with no "(incl. 5% VAT)" note:
- Guarantee Your Spot → **₫150,000** (was ₫157,500)
- Pay in Full → **₫500,000** (was ₫525,000)
- Pay at Studio → ₫500,000 (unchanged, never had a fee)

The VAT is then applied and **itemized on the payment page** (which already breaks out Session Fee + VAT + total), so the customer sees the fee at the point of payment rather than bundled into the selection list.

Both frontend and backend rebuilt and deployed; containers healthy.

## Two things to note
1. **This raises what customers pay for packages** by 5% (now base + VAT). That's the intent of "make the fee apply," just flagging it's a real price change. Existing/old invoices are unaffected — only new purchases.
2. ⚠️ **Payments are still in mock mode until you re-enter the Stripe keys** (they were wiped by that earlier settings bug, and the preservation fix is now deployed). Once you re-enter them in **Settings → Stripe Gateway Configuration** and save, do a real low-value **class booking** and a **package purchase** to confirm both the new base-price display and the VAT totals look right end-to-end. Tell me when the keys are back in and I'll verify from the server.

Found it — and it's **not** a code-logic bug in the sum itself; it's **orphan test payments**. (`AmountPaid` is Decimal128, not a string — that was just mongosh display.)

## The July dashboard breakdown
| Amount | Method | Linked invoice | Legit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **₫3,825,000** | CASH | **(invoice missing)** | ❌ orphan test |
| **₫2,250,000** | CASH | **(invoice missing)** | ❌ orphan test |
| ₫500,000 | Card | Studio collection (PAID) | ✅ |
| ₫500,000 | Card | Studio collection (PAID) | ✅ |
| ₫500,000 | Card | Studio collection (PAID) | ✅ |
| ₫150,000 | Stripe | Online booking (PARTIAL) | ✅ |

**Dashboard shows ₫7,725,000. Real cash is ₫1,650,000.** The ₫6,075,000 gap is **two CASH payments from Jul 3 whose invoices no longer exist** — leftovers from your Stripe testing where the invoice was deleted/voided but the payment record wasn't cleaned up.

## Why the dashboard shows them
`AnalyticsService.ComputeRevenueAsync` sums **every** payment in the month with no cross-check — it never verifies the payment's invoice still exists or isn't voided. So these orphans get counted.

## Fix — two parts
1. **Delete the 2 orphan payments** (₫3,825,000 + ₫2,250,000, invoices missing). Immediate — drops the dashboard to the correct ₫1,650,000.
2. **Harden the code** so the dashboard only counts payments tied to a **live (non-voided, existing) invoice** — then voided/deleted invoices can never inflate revenue again. (I'd apply the same invoice cross-check the washout now uses.)

Deleting payment records is a financial-data change, so I want your go-ahead. Want me to:
- **(a)** delete just those 2 orphan payments now (quick fix), and
- **(b)** also harden `ComputeRevenueAsync` so it's robust going forward?

Both, or just one? And should I scan the whole Payments collection for any **other** orphans (payments whose invoice is missing/voided) while I'm at it, since they'd be skewing other periods too?

Both addressed. Here's where things stand:

## ✅ Class analytics — done & deployed
The "classes this week" metric now counts **only COMPLETED sessions that had at least one checked-in attendee**. Verified on this week's real data:
- Old metric (scheduled + completed): **11**
- **New metric (completed *with* attendees): 6**

So scheduled-but-not-yet-held classes, and empty/no-show sessions, no longer inflate the count. (The occupancy/attendance analytics already used COMPLETED, so those were fine.)

## ❓ Changing `/admin` to a secret path — assessment
**Short answer: it won't break the system if done thoroughly, but it's a big mechanical change with low real security value.**

What it touches:
- Rename the `src/pages/admin/` directory → new path.
- Update **~161 hardcoded `/admin` references** (nav links, `window.location` redirects, the post-login redirect).
- No nginx/backend changes needed — `/admin` is served by the frontend SPA (nginx just proxies `/`), and the **API stays at `/api/*`**.

The real caveats:
- **It's security-through-obscurity.** Your actual protection is already solid: admin pages require a logged-in JWT with an admin role, and every API endpoint is `[Authorize(Roles=...)]`. Someone who finds `/admin` without a token just bounces to the login screen — they can't do anything. Renaming the path only stops casual URL-guessing; it does **not** protect the API (an attacker probes `/api/...`, not `/admin`).
- It breaks any **bookmarks** your staff have.
- Risk is missing one of the 161 refs → a broken link/redirect (fixable, but why introduce it).

**If your goal is genuinely harder access,** these add real security where obscurity doesn't:
- **IP allowlist** on nginx for the admin UI + sensitive API routes (restrict to studio/office IPs).
- **fail2ban / rate-limit** on the login endpoint.
- **2FA** for admin logins (larger feature).

My recommendation: skip the rename as a security measure — it's a lot of churn for obscurity. If you want defense-in-depth, an nginx IP allowlist is far stronger and ~5 lines. That said, if you still want the rename (some people like it purely to reduce bot noise), I can do it safely — full find-replace + rebuild + verify zero stray `/admin` refs and that login redirects land correctly. Just say the word.

Deployed — `renotify` is live in the served `sw.js`.

## What this fixes
Repeated notifications with the same `tag` (like pressing Test multiple times, or two bookings) now **re-alert with a fresh banner** instead of silently updating the existing one. That was very likely why your first test showed but the rest didn't.

## Important — you must update the service worker on your device
The browser caches the old service worker. To get the fix:
1. **Fully close and reopen** the PWA/tab on `soulpilates.com.vn` (or hard-refresh `Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-R`). The app has a skip-waiting handler, so the new SW should activate on reload.
2. Then press **Test** again — you should get a banner each time now.

## If it *still* only lands in the notification center (not a top banner)
That part is an **OS setting**, not something the web app controls — the browser can request a banner, but the OS decides banner vs. notification-center list:
- **macOS:** System Settings → Notifications → **[your browser]** → set style to **"Alerts"** (persistent) or **"Banners"** (auto-dismiss), and make sure "Allow Notifications" is on. If it's set to "None," nothing shows.
- **Windows:** Settings → System → Notifications → **[your browser]** on; turn **Focus Assist / Do Not Disturb** off; enable "Show notification banners."
- **Chrome itself:** `chrome://settings/content/notifications` → `soulpilates.com.vn` = Allow.

Once you've reloaded to pick up the new SW, hit Test and tell me — I'll confirm from the server that it delivered, so we know for certain whether any remaining issue is the OS notification style (which only you can toggle on that device).

That was the missing piece. Backend is serving and stable (the startup exception was a transient Mongo/Redis race on restart — it recovered and is healthy).

## Why "nothing changed" before
The schedule's **per-class commission display** (the Financials tab on a class — what you're actually looking at) is computed by a **completely separate method** in `SchedulingService`, not the monthly payroll I'd fixed. It had the *same* bug in its own copy of the logic: line 405 defaulted to `DropInPrice` and never overrode it for package bookings. So my earlier fixes to `PayrollService` didn't touch what you were seeing.

## Now fixed in both places (identical rule)
The schedule's per-class commission now resolves the base exactly like payroll:
1. **`PACKAGE_CREDIT`** → the package's per-class rate (price ÷ credits).
2. **Actually paid** → what they paid (genuine full-price drop-in stays drop-in).
3. **Unpaid but client holds an active package for that format** → package rate (catches the `PAY_AT_STUDIO` package members).
4. Otherwise → drop-in.

So a private-package class now shows **722,500** (not 850,000), a group-package class **425,000** (not 500,000), and discounted packages show their actual per-class price.

**Open the class on the schedule and check the Financials/commission section** — it should now reflect the package rate. If it still looks wrong, tell me exactly which class and instructor and I'll trace that specific number.

I've noted in memory that there are **two** commission code paths (`PayrollService` + `SchedulingService`) so this rule gets applied to both from now on.

## Fixed
The schedule's per-class **tier count** (`monthClassCount` in `SchedulingService`) was counting a class if it had any `BOOKED` attendee — including not-yet-arrived and empty classes. It now only counts a class once someone has **CHECKED_IN / ARRIVED**. So:

- A class with **no check-ins** (empty, all no-shows, or only future bookings) → **does not count** toward the instructor's class total.
- A class counts as soon as **≥1 attendee actually checks in**.

The monthly **payroll** aggregation was already correct here (it skips any class with zero arrived attendees), so this was purely the schedule/class-detail view showing an inflated count and, with it, potentially the wrong commission tier.

Let me record this rule alongside the commission rule:

For instructor **% commission** on a class booking, the commission base depends on how the client paid:
- **Package-credit redemption** → base = the **per-class rate within the package** = (package sale price ÷ credits). Stored on `ClientPackage.FractionalValuePerClass`. NOT the full drop-in rate.
- **Regular drop-in** (client paid the full drop-in price) → base = the drop-in rate.

**Why:** a client on a 10 Group pack (₫4,250,000/10 = ₫425,000/class) did NOT pay the ₫500,000 drop-in rate, so commissioning on drop-in overpays instructors. The user has emphasized this repeatedly.

Per-class value MUST be the **actual amount the package sold for** (net of discounts), NOT the product list price — the user was explicit: some packages are discounted and list price would overpay commission.

**How to apply:** the base resolver is `PayrollService.ResolveAttendeeRevenueAsync` (2026-07-05: loads the `ClientPackage` via `Attendance.PackageInstanceId` and returns `FractionalValuePerClass × qty` for `PACKAGE_CREDIT`; falls back to `session.DropInPrice` only when the per-class value is unknown/0). Package creation sets `FractionalValuePerClass = line.LineTotal ÷ units ÷ credits` — the **actual net** — in `InvoiceService.ProvisionPackagesFromInvoiceAsync` (line ~534), so upcoming purchases are correct including discounts. WalletService comp-grants set 0. On 2026-07-05 backfilled 95 legacy packages by matching each to its **actual purchase invoice line** (same client + parsed "<credits> <Group|Private> Class Pack" description + nearest date), net÷credits — script at scratchpad `backfill-actual-perclass.js`. content.text:
Both fixes are live and verified.

## What caused the 500
Clicking the notification opened `/admin/client-profile`… no — it opened **`/admin/clients/{id}`**, a route that **doesn't exist**. On any unknown route, the frontend's nginx fell back to `/404.html`, but that file **wasn't in the build**, so nginx looped (`redirect cycle → /404.html`) and returned **500** instead of a 404. Two bugs stacked.

## Fixes (deployed)
1. **Notification URL corrected** — the "New client" push now links to `/admin/client-profile?id={id}` (the real route). Verified it resolves `200`.
2. **Also fixed the "Low stock" push** — it pointed to `/admin/merchandise` (nonexistent) → now `/admin/products`.
3. **Added a real 404 page** (`404.astro` → `/404.html`) so the nginx fallback resolves to a file instead of looping. **Any** unknown route now shows a friendly "404 – Go to dashboard" page instead of a 500 — this also fixes the `/robots.txt` and bot-probe 500s you had.

## Good news for existing notifications
Even the notifications **already sitting on your device** (which still carry the old bad URL) will now open the **404 page** instead of crashing with a 500 — and any new "New client" notification opens the correct client profile.

Verified: `/admin/client-profile?id=…` → `200` through the apex, unknown routes → 404 page (no more 500), backend healthy.

The other notification types (`/admin/calendar?session=…`, `/admin/washout`) point to routes that exist, so they're fine. Give it a try from the PWA — a fresh "new client" notification should open straight to that client's profile.

content.text:
**Found the real cause of the spam** — it's not just reputation, it's a **DNS misconfiguration**:

## The problem: broken reverse-DNS (FCrDNS)
- Your server's reverse DNS (PTR) for `72.62.240.50` → **`mail.soulpilates.com.vn`** ✓
- But `mail.soulpilates.com.vn` is **Proxied** (orange cloud) in Cloudflare, so it resolves to **Cloudflare's IPs** (`104.21.32.40`…), **not** `72.62.240.50`.
- So when Gmail checks "does the sending IP's hostname point back to it?" → **it fails**. Forward-Confirmed Reverse DNS mismatch is a **strong spam signal** — and it also **breaks incoming email** (mail can't flow through Cloudflare's proxy).

Cloudflare **cannot proxy email** anyway — SMTP isn't HTTP.

## Fix — you do this in Cloudflare (2 clicks)
1. **`mail.soulpilates.com.vn`** → click Edit → set **Proxy status to "DNS only"** (grey cloud) → Save.
2. **`smtp.soulpilates.com.vn`** → same → **"DNS only"** (grey cloud) → Save.

That's it. After this, `mail.` resolves to `72.62.240.50`, matching the PTR → FCrDNS passes → a big deliverability jump, and incoming mail works again.

*(The Cloudflare warning about "revealing an IP" is expected and fine here — mail servers **must** expose the real IP; you can't hide a mail server behind Cloudflare. Keep the apex, `www`, and `new` proxied as they are.)*

## Secondary cleanup (optional but recommended)
- The **`_domainkey`** TXT record `"t=y; o=~;"` — the **`t=y`** flag means "DKIM in **testing** mode," which tells receivers not to fully trust your DKIM. Either **delete that record** (your real key lives at `mail._domainkey`, which is fine) or change `t=y` to `t=s`.
- Your SPF ends in `~all` (softfail). Once mail is flowing cleanly you could tighten to `-all`, but leave it for now.

## Do this before any bulk send
Un-proxying `mail.` is the single biggest fix here — it likely explains the spam more than reputation does. After you change it, tell me and I'll **re-send the test** to confirm it lands in the inbox. Then we warm up gradually.

Make those two records "DNS only" and let me know.

Great choice. Here's the setup — a few of these are yours (Brevo dashboard + the secret key), then I flip the app over and test.

## Step 1 — Get your Brevo SMTP credentials
In Brevo → **SMTP & API → SMTP** tab:
- **Server:** `smtp-relay.brevo.com` **Port:** `587`
- **Login:** the value Brevo shows (looks like `8xxxxxx@smtp-brevo.com` or your account email)
- **Password:** click **Generate a new SMTP key** and copy it (this is the secret)

## Step 2 — Authenticate your domain in Brevo (critical for inbox placement)
Brevo → **Senders, Domains & Dedicated IPs → Domains → Add a domain** → `soulpilates.com.vn`. It'll give you **2–3 DNS records** (a `brevo._domainkey` DKIM, a `brevo-code` TXT, maybe a DMARC). Add each in **Cloudflare as "DNS only"** and hit Verify in Brevo. This lets Brevo sign mail as *your* domain so it passes DMARC and lands in inboxes.

## Step 3 — Add Brevo to your SPF (Cloudflare)
Edit your existing SPF TXT record on `soulpilates.com.vn` to include Brevo:
```
v=spf1 mx a ip4:72.62.240.50 include:spf.brevo.com ~all
```

## Step 4 — Point the app at Brevo (you run this — keeps the key yours)
On the server, paste your login and key into these:
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates
sed -i 's#^SMTP_HOST=.*#SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.brevo.com#' prod.env
sed -i 's#^SMTP_USERNAME=.*#SMTP_USERNAME=YOUR_BREVO_LOGIN#' prod.env
sed -i 's#^SMTP_PASSWORD=.*#SMTP_PASSWORD=YOUR_BREVO_SMTP_KEY#' prod.env
```
(Leave `SMTP_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@soulpilates.com.vn` and `SMTP_PORT=587` as-is.)

## Step 5 — Tell me "done"
I'll restart the backend and send a test through Brevo to confirm it delivers (and lands in the inbox, not spam). Then I'll resend to the **24 that got stuck** and we can pace out the rest — Brevo's 300/day free tier comfortably covers your 221 over a day or two.

Confirmed — the sync **does** cover equipment (it sets `EquipmentTypes`/`EquipmentType` on future sessions). So this was a workflow thing, not a bug.

## Fixed
The 51 future Core Balance sessions now carry **Reformer + Ladder Barrel**. **Refresh the booking page** (hard-refresh if needed for cache) and the equipment will show.

## Why it happened & how to avoid it next time
Editing a blueprint updates the *template*, but classes already on the calendar keep the equipment they were created with — **unless you tell it to update them**. When you save a blueprint, a **"Save" dialog pops up** with an option like **"update existing future sessions."** You most likely saved without ticking that, so only the blueprint changed and the already-scheduled Core Balance classes stayed empty.

**Next time:** after editing a blueprint, in that save dialog **check "update existing future sessions"** — it'll push equipment (and name, time, price, image, etc.) to all upcoming classes automatically. That's the same thing I just did manually.

This is by design (it lets you change a template without disturbing classes already booked), but if you'd rather equipment changes **always** auto-propagate without the dialog, I can wire that up — just say the word. Otherwise you're all set: refresh the booking page and Core Balance will show its equipment.

All fixed and verified:

- **Booking schedule works again** — 110 sessions load (was 500-erroring).
- **Days with classes:** Mon Jul 6 → Sat Jul 11… **no Sunday** (matches what you saw). So the auto-skip will now correctly jump from today (Sunday) to **Monday Jul 6**.

When I fixed the Core Balance equipment earlier, I also wrote an **`EquipmentIds`** field onto those 51 sessions — but `CalendarSession` has no such property. The MongoDB driver **throws on any unknown field**, so as soon as the booking schedule query hit one of those sessions it **crashed with a 500**. That broke class-loading entirely, and the auto-skip (which reads that endpoint) silently fell back to "today" — which happened to be Sunday. So the feature wasn't gone; the data behind it was crashing.

The fix: removed the stray `EquipmentIds` from all 51 sessions. Kept `EquipmentType` + `EquipmentTypes` (what actually drives the equipment display).

**Refresh the booking page** — it should now load Monday's classes and show Core Balance's equipment. Sorry about that — it was affecting all customers' booking, so good catch.

## Worth hardening
This class of bug (one stray field crashing a whole endpoint) is avoidable — I can add `[BsonIgnoreExtraElements]` to `CalendarSession` (and key entities) so an unexpected field is ignored rather than 500-ing the booking system. Want me to add that safety net? It's a small, low-risk change that would've turned this outage into a no-op.

Done — deployed and healthy.

## What's added
Now when your team edits a **client's email** in the admin client editor, the change **automatically propagates to that customer's login account** — so they can immediately sign in with the new email. No more "invalid login" after an email edit.

**Safety guards built in:**
- Skips if the new email is **blank**.
- Skips if that email already belongs to a **different** account (prevents duplicate-login conflicts) — in that rare case the login email is left unchanged rather than clobbering someone else's.
- The change is audited (the existing PII-update audit log already records email changes).

Your own `soul@pilates.com` account is already synced from earlier, so you're good to log in with it now. And going forward, this keeps the CRM email and login email in lockstep for all real customers automatically.

<!--
  Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel + Conversions API loader.
  Include in every customer-facing page's <head>. Pages using CustomerLayout get
  it automatically; standalone pages (login/register/onboarding/…) include it too.

  Exposes window.spMetaTrack(eventName, customData, userData):
    • fires the browser Pixel with a fresh eventID, AND
    • relays the same event (same eventID) to /api/meta/event so the backend
      forwards it to Meta's Conversions API — de-duplicated by eventID.
  Safe no-op until a Pixel ID is configured (Events Manager → env).
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initMetaPixel() {
    // Default to a no-op so callers never crash before config resolves.
    window.spMetaTrack = window.spMetaTrack || function () {};

    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch (e) {}

    function getCookie(name) {
      var m = document.cookie.match('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;]*)');
      return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null;
    }

    function uuid() {
      try { if (crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {}
      return 'e-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(16).slice(2);
    }

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/config')
      .then(function (res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.enabled || !cfg.pixelId) return;
        var pixelId = cfg.pixelId;

        // ── Meta Pixel base code ──
        !(function (f, b, e, v, n, t, s) {
          if (f.fbq) return; n = f.fbq = function () {
            n.callMethod ? n.callMethod.apply(n, arguments) : n.queue.push(arguments);
          };
          if (!f._fbq) f._fbq = n; n.push = n; n.loaded = !0; n.version = '2.0';
          n.queue = []; t = b.createElement(e); t.async = !0; t.src = v;
          s = b.getElementsByTagName(e)[0]; s.parentNode.insertBefore(t, s);
        })(window, document, 'script', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js');

        fbq('init', pixelId);
        fbq('track', 'PageView');

        // ── Dual Pixel + CAPI tracker ──
        window.spMetaTrack = function (eventName, customData, userData) {
          customData = customData || {};
          userData = userData || {};
          var eventId = uuid();

          try { fbq('track', eventName, customData, { eventID: eventId }); } catch (e) {}

          // Synthesize fbc from an ?fbclid= param if the cookie isn't set yet.
          var fbc = getCookie('_fbc');
          if (!fbc) {
            try {
              var p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('fbclid');
              if (p) fbc = 'fb.1.' + Date.now() + '.' + p;
            } catch (e) {}
          }

          var payload = {
            eventName: eventName,
            eventId: eventId,
            eventSourceUrl: window.location.href,
            email: userData.email || null,
            phone: userData.phone || null,
            fbp: getCookie('_fbp'),
            fbc: fbc,
            value: (customData.value != null) ? customData.value : null,
            currency: customData.currency || null,
            contentName: customData.content_name || null,
            contentCategory: customData.content_category || null,
            contentIds: customData.content_ids || null,
          };

          try {
            fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/event', {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify(payload),
              keepalive: true,
            }).catch(function () {});
          } catch (e) {}
        };
      })
      .catch(function () {});
  })();
</script>

That's a strong, clean creative — the icon column and branding look great. Before you run it, though, one **important heads-up on Meta ad policy**, then ready-to-use copy.

## ⚠️ Meta will likely reject this as-is (two policy issues)
1. **Before/After images are prohibited.** Meta's advertising policy explicitly bans "before-and-after" images and content implying transformation of the body. This exact format (BEFORE/AFTER + the yellow alignment lines showing a "corrected" spine) is one of the most commonly auto-rejected ad types — and repeated rejections can get your **ad account restricted**, which you really don't want right at launch.
2. **Medical claims.** "Realign your spine," treating scoliosis, "reduce pain" — health-outcome claims are heavily scrutinized and often disallowed.

**Fix:** keep the beautiful design, but swap the before/after for **one aspirational lifestyle image** (someone confidently practicing/standing tall), and **soften the claims** to supportive language ("may help," "support," "feel"). You can still target scoliosis interest — you just can't *promise* a fix or show a transformation.

## Ready-to-use ad copy (compliant framing)

**Primary text (EN):**
> Living with scoliosis or back tension? Personalised Pilates in Da Nang can help you build a stronger, more balanced body. 🧘‍♀️
> Our reformer and private sessions focus on posture, deep-core strength, and gentle mobility — so you feel taller, looser, and more at ease in your body.
> Book a private session with our specialist instructors. Your spine. Your strength. Your best self.

**Headline:** Feel Stronger, Straighter, More Balanced
**Description:** Personalised Pilates in Da Nang · Private & Reformer
**CTA button:** Book Now

**Short versions for foreign travelers:**
- 🇰🇷 척추측만증이나 허리 긴장이 있으신가요? 다낭의 맞춤 필라테스로 더 강하고 균형 잡힌 몸을 만들어보세요. 자세·코어·유연성에 집중하는 프라이빗 세션 — 지금 예약하세요.
- 🇷🇺 Сколиоз или напряжение в спине? Персональный пилатес в Дананге поможет стать сильнее и более сбалансированным. Осанка, глубокие мышцы кора, мягкая подвижность. Записывайтесь на приватную сессию.

Yes — that's almost certainly it. In Meta, the Pixel is now called a **"dataset,"** and it has to be **assigned to your ad account** as a shared asset before it shows up when you build an ad. Right now your dataset (`Soul Pilates Da Nang`, ID `1330301812103697`) exists but likely isn't connected to the ad account you're creating the ad in.

## Fix — connect the dataset to the ad account (Business Settings)
1. Go to **[business.facebook.com/settings](https://business.facebook.com/settings)** (Business Settings).
2. Left menu → **Data sources → Datasets** (older UIs: **Data sources → Pixels**).
3. Select **Soul Pilates Da Nang**.
4. Click the **"Connected assets"** (or **"Add assets"** / **"Assign partners/accounts"**) tab.
5. **Add your ad account** and give it access.

Or from the other direction: **Accounts → Ad accounts → [your ad account] → Connected assets → add the dataset.**

## Things to double-check
- **Same Business Portfolio:** the **dataset** and the **ad account** must live in the **same** Business Manager. If the pixel was created in one business and the ad account is in another (or a personal account), they won't see each other — you'd move/re-share one of them.
- **Your access level:** you need **admin** rights on *both* the dataset and the ad account to link them.
- After linking, **refresh** the Ads Manager tab — the dataset should now appear in the ad's tracking/conversion section.

Once it's connected, when you set the ad up you'll be able to pick the dataset for **conversion tracking** and choose the events (PageView, ViewContent, InitiateCheckout, Purchase) we wired up.

If it *still* doesn't appear after connecting, tell me what you see in **Business Settings → Data sources → Datasets → Connected assets** (which ad accounts are listed) and I'll help you narrow it down. This is all on Meta's side — nothing to change on the server.

The dataset is connected now — and all four events (**Complete registration, View content, Initiate checkout, Purchase**) show the green **"Conversions API"** badge, which confirms our server-side tracking is registered correctly. Nice.

## About that greyed-out event
The tooltip *"This conversion event is only available with sales objective"* means **Purchase** is disabled because your campaign's **objective isn't set to "Sales."** Purchase = an actual booking/payment, so Meta only lets you optimize for it under the **Sales** objective. If you want the algorithm to chase real bookings, restart the campaign with the **Sales** objective, then Purchase becomes selectable.

## Which event should you pick? (this matters a lot)
It depends on your **volume**, and as a brand-new studio you have very little yet:

- **Purchase** — the *ideal* signal (real bookings), **but** Meta needs roughly **~50 conversions/week** to optimize well. With low early booking volume, it'll stay stuck in "learning" and spend inefficiently.
- **Initiate checkout** — someone started a booking. More volume than Purchase, still high-intent. **Good middle ground to start.**
- **View content** — someone viewed a class. Highest volume, lowest intent — useful only if the above are too sparse.

## My recommendation for launch
1. **Start with a Sales campaign → optimize for `Initiate checkout`** (or even `View content`) while volume is low — you'll get out of learning phase faster and feed the algorithm data.
2. **Once you're getting ~30–50 bookings/week**, switch a campaign to optimize for **Purchase** directly.
3. Alternatively, run a cheaper **Traffic** campaign to your booking page first to build audiences + pixel data, *then* layer a Sales/Purchase campaign on top.

So: **set the campaign objective to Sales**, pick **Initiate checkout** for now, and move to **Purchase** as bookings grow.

Fixed and deployed. 

## Root cause
Marking a class completed goes through the **session-update** endpoint, which was locked to **Admin/Manager only** — so your receptionist account got a permission denial (403). Now **Receptionist is allowed**, so they can mark classes completed (and edit sessions).

**No re-login needed** — the role is already in their token; the endpoint just now accepts it. Have them retry marking the class completed.

## Note on the specific class
The June-6 sessions in the data (around that time) already show status **COMPLETED**, so if that's the one, it may already be done — but regardless, receptionists can now perform this action on any class going forward.

## One scope decision for you
This change lets receptionists **edit sessions** in general (status, and technically also reschedule/rename/capacity/price via the edit modal), not *only* mark-completed. For a small front-desk setup that's usually fine, but if you'd rather receptionists could **only mark classes completed** (and not reschedule or reprice), I can add a dedicated "status-only" permission so they get exactly that and nothing more.

Want me to tighten it to status-only, or is full session-edit access for receptionists fine?

content.text:
Both fixes are live. Here's what was actually going on — it was **two** things:

## Root causes
1. **Session update was Admin/Manager only** → receptionist got a 403 marking a class completed. (Fixed in the earlier deploy.)
2. **The instructor dropdown loaded from `/api/staff`, which is Admin-only** → blank for receptionists. Saving a session with a blank instructor then failed → *"failed to update session."* This was the remaining blocker.

## What I did
- Added a **lightweight instructor directory** (`GET /api/scheduling/instructors`) that returns only **id / name / role / active** — **no salaries, rates, or bank details** — accessible to Admin, Manager, **Receptionist**, and Instructor.
- Pointed the calendar's instructor dropdown at it, so it now populates for receptionists (in both the calendar and the class-edit modal).
- Kept the full `/api/staff` (with sensitive pay data) **Admin-only**, so receptionists get what they need without seeing payroll info.

## Receptionists can now do the full class-management job
✅ Create classes · ✅ Edit / **mark completed** · ✅ Check people in · ✅ Add walk-in students · ✅ Change booking status · ✅ See/assign instructors.

**Have the receptionist hard-refresh the calendar page** (Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-R for the new bundle) — no re-login needed — and retry. The instructor dropdown should populate and the save should go through.

The only class actions still restricted to Admin/Manager are **deleting** classes and **blocking** time slots (higher-impact). If you want receptionists to have those too, say so and I'll add them — but marking completed, editing, check-in, and adding students all work for them now.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
This is a continued session developing the Soul Pilates CRM (.NET 10 + Astro 6 + MongoDB at /opt/soulpilates, deployed via prebuilt Docker images on a VPS, IP 72.62.240.50, domain soulpilates.com.vn). The user made many sequential requests:
- Send test activation + birthday emails.
- Execute the domain migration from new.soulpilates.com.vn → apex soulpilates.com.vn (audited earlier, now executed).
- Rename "Online Fee" → "VAT (online only)" in customer-facing displays.
- Make the online fee (VAT) apply to package purchases (was only on class bookings).
- Don't bundle the fee into the class-options-page price — show base, put fee on payment page.
- Change revenue to cash-basis (only count money actually received, not invoiced) to avoid counting unpaid packages/deposit balances.
- Class analytics should only count "completed classes with attendees."
- Analytics page should default to current month (was showing previous month).
- Update Meta domain-verification tag to the apex value provided.
- Fix PWA notifications (not showing; and a 500 error on notification click).
- Add searchable country-code selector to client-creation forms (clients page + calendar popup).
- Fix commission %: for package bookings, base commission on the package per-class rate (package sale price ÷ credits), NOT drop-in rate — UNLESS a regular drop-in class paid full rate. Later refined: use ACTUAL sale price (with discounts), not list price. Then: also handle classes where the person is on a package but booked non-PACKAGE_CREDIT. Correct all class commissions from July 2 onward.
- A class with no checked-in attendees shouldn't count toward instructor's class total.
- Fix "jump to next available day" booking feature (was stuck on Sunday) — turned out to be a 500 caused by a stray EquipmentIds field I'd added.
- Remove internal tag "SP_INFOGRAPHIC" leaking into customer-facing ad/class display.
- Fix new account iwizardhax2.1 wrongly showing a past booking (linked to wrong client via placeholder phone).
- Add contact-details/phone handling; make client-email edits propagate to login account.
- Create VIP and Super VIP achievement email templates that send when customers reach those tiers.
- Rename instructor "Nhi" to "Nakko" everywhere including existing classes.
- Create a full system backup (DB + code + media) as a zip.
- Reset/refresh visitor and funnel stats (test data → live).
- Turn SMTP live and send activation emails to filtered customers (package OR attended in last 3 months); set up Brevo SMTP relay after self-hosted port-25 throttling.
- Continue Meta Pixel work (PageView dedup fix, ad copy, dataset connection, conversion event selection).
- Give receptionist permissions to manage classes (mark completed, check-in) — CURRENT TASK.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- Clean Architecture: SoulPilates.API (controllers), .Core (entities/DTOs/interfaces), .Services, .Infrastructure (MongoDbContext).
- Deploy: backend `docker build -q -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .` then `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend`; frontend `docker build -q --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro` then `up -d frontend`. Backend on 127.0.0.1:8391, frontend on 127.0.0.1:3719.
- Mongo access: `docker exec soulpilates-prod-mongo mongosh -u admin -p "$(grep '^MONGO_PASSWORD=' prod.env|cut -d= -f2)" --quiet --eval '...'`.
- **CRITICAL: IDs (ClientId, InstructorId, CalendarSessionId, etc.) are `string` in C# with [BsonRepresentation(ObjectId)], stored as ObjectId in Mongo.** mongosh queries must use ObjectId() or match will fail (string vs ObjectId). This caused several bugs.
- Denormalized/snapshotted fields: CalendarSession snapshots InstructorName, EquipmentType, EquipmentTypes, DropInPrice, ImageUrl from ClassBlueprint at materialization; editing the blueprint doesn't update existing sessions unless the "Save dialog → update existing future sessions" sync (SyncBlueprintSessionsAsync) is used.
- **Mongo driver throws FormatException on unknown fields** (CalendarSession lacks [BsonIgnoreExtraElements]) — adding a field the entity doesn't have crashes deserialization.
- Email templates system: EmailTemplateIds constants, EmailTemplateDefaults.All(), ResolveTemplateAsync, IsTemplateEnabledAsync, auto-backfill. Editable in Admin → Settings → Emails.
- Background service pattern (BackgroundService, periodic tick, scoped service resolution) — used for birthday, review, VIP emails.
- Meta Pixel + CAPI: dual pixel+CAPI with shared eventID for deduplication; /api/meta/event endpoint → MetaConversionsService; fbp/fbc for match quality.
- Role-based [Authorize(Roles=...)] on endpoints; class-level and method-level Authorize attributes AND together (method can't loosen class-level).

- **SoulPilates.API/Controllers/SchedulingController.cs** (CURRENT WORK):

Also `monthClassCount` query (~line 385) changed to require CHECKED_IN/ARRIVED (removed BOOKED). `TryClaimSessionCapacityAsync` (~1519) status filter changed to `In(Status, ["SCHEDULED","COMPLETED","NO_SHOW"])` to allow booking past classes for backfill.

- **SoulPilates.Core/Interfaces/IEmailService.cs**: Added SendVipEmailAsync, SendSuperVipEmailAsync.

<!--
  Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel + Conversions API loader.
  Include in every customer-facing page's <head>. Pages using CustomerLayout get
  it automatically; standalone pages (login/register/onboarding/…) include it too.

  Exposes window.spMetaTrack(eventName, customData, userData):
    • fires the browser Pixel with a fresh eventID, AND
    • relays the same event (same eventID) to /api/meta/event so the backend
      forwards it to Meta's Conversions API — de-duplicated by eventID.
  Safe no-op until a Pixel ID is configured (Events Manager → env).
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initMetaPixel() {
    // Default to a no-op so callers never crash before config resolves.
    window.spMetaTrack = window.spMetaTrack || function () {};

    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch (e) {}

    function getCookie(name) {
      var m = document.cookie.match('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;]*)');
      return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null;
    }

    function uuid() {
      try { if (crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {}
      return 'e-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(16).slice(2);
    }

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/config')
      .then(function (res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.enabled || !cfg.pixelId) return;
        var pixelId = cfg.pixelId;

        // ── Meta Pixel base code ──
        !(function (f, b, e, v, n, t, s) {
          if (f.fbq) return; n = f.fbq = function () {
            n.callMethod ? n.callMethod.apply(n, arguments) : n.queue.push(arguments);
          };
          if (!f._fbq) f._fbq = n; n.push = n; n.loaded = !0; n.version = '2.0';
          n.queue = []; t = b.createElement(e); t.async = !0; t.src = v;
          s = b.getElementsByTagName(e)[0]; s.parentNode.insertBefore(t, s);
        })(window, document, 'script', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js');

        fbq('init', pixelId);

        // ── Dual Pixel + CAPI tracker ──
        window.spMetaTrack = function (eventName, customData, userData) {
          customData = customData || {};
          userData = userData || {};
          var eventId = uuid();

          try { fbq('track', eventName, customData, { eventID: eventId }); } catch (e) {}

          // Synthesize fbc from an ?fbclid= param if the cookie isn't set yet.
          var fbc = getCookie('_fbc');
          if (!fbc) {
            try {
              var p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('fbclid');
              if (p) fbc = 'fb.1.' + Date.now() + '.' + p;
            } catch (e) {}
          }

          var payload = {
            eventName: eventName,
            eventId: eventId,
            eventSourceUrl: window.location.href,
            email: userData.email || null,
            phone: userData.phone || null,
            fbp: getCookie('_fbp'),
            fbc: fbc,
            value: (customData.value != null) ? customData.value : null,
            currency: customData.currency || null,
            contentName: customData.content_name || null,
            contentCategory: customData.content_category || null,
            contentIds: customData.content_ids || null,
          };

          try {
            fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/event', {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify(payload),
              keepalive: true,
            }).catch(function () {});
          } catch (e) {}
        };

        // Fire the initial PageView through the dual path so it carries a shared
        // eventID (deduplicated with the server) AND is sent via the Conversions
        // API — not browser-pixel-only. Sends fbp/fbc for better match quality.
        try { window.spMetaTrack('PageView'); } catch (e) {}
      })
      .catch(function () {});
  })();
</script>

The receptionist's "mark completed" / edit-class save calls **`PATCH /api/scheduling/session/{id}/override`** (the endpoint that changes a session's status, instructor, capacity, times). - Confirmed the `settings/schedule` 403 in the logs is harmless — the calendar wraps it in try/catch and falls back to default hours, so it doesn't block anything.

Combined with the earlier fixes, receptionists now have the full front-desk toolkit (all already Receptionist-authorized, verified in the controller):
✅ Mark classes completed / edit sessions (override) · ✅ Create classes · ✅ Check-in (`check-in/{id}`) · ✅ Booking status · ✅ Add students · ✅ Collect payment · ✅ Reschedule · ✅ Instructor dropdown.

content.text:
Yes, it's possible — and the sidebar dropdown is genuinely the easy part. The hard part is that **your entire system is single-tenant today**: I checked all 69 entities and ~40 collections, and there's no concept of a store/branch/franchise anywhere. Every Client, CalendarSession, Invoice, Staff, Payroll run, etc. currently belongs to one implicit studio. To support franchises you have to introduce data isolation, and that touches nearly everything.

Here's the honest lay of the land.

## The three ways to do it

**1. One database, `StoreId` on every record (shared-schema multi-tenancy)** ← recommended for you
- Add a `Store` entity and stamp a `StoreId` on every tenant-scoped collection (Clients, Sessions, Invoices, Staff, Packages, Payments, Expenses, Payroll…).
- The sidebar dropdown sets an "active store," and **every query gets filtered by `StoreId`**.
- Reporting across stores (total revenue, HQ dashboards) is trivial — it's all one DB.
- This is the standard SaaS approach and fits your Mongo model well.

**2. One database per store**
- Strongest isolation, simplest per-store queries, but cross-store reporting becomes painful (you query N databases and merge), migrations run N times, and connection routing gets complex. Overkill unless franchisees legally demand separated data.

**3. Separate deployments per store**
- Just run the whole app N times. Zero code change, but no unified admin, N× hosting/ops, and no cross-store view. Fine for 2 stores, miserable at 5+.

## What option 1 actually requires

The dropdown (~a day of work) is dwarfed by:

1. **`Store` entity + `StoreId` on ~30 collections** and a backfill migration stamping all existing data with your current store's ID.
2. **Query filtering everywhere** — this is the big one. Every `.Find()`, aggregation, and report in the Services layer must scope by the active store. Miss one and Store A sees Store B's data. Best handled centrally (a tenant-context injected into the data layer) rather than editing hundreds of call sites by hand.
3. **User↔store access model** — which admins/receptionists/instructors belong to which store(s); the JWT carries the active store; server *enforces* it (never trust the dropdown alone).
4. **Cross-cutting decisions** you'll need to make per feature:
   - Are **clients** shared across stores or per-store? (Someone books at two locations.)
   - Are **staff** shared? Payroll is per-store but a trainer might work at two.
   - **Packages/credits** — usable at any branch or only where purchased?
   - **Blueprints, promos, email templates, settings** — global (HQ-defined) or per-store?
   - **Meta Pixel, Stripe, SMTP** — one account or per-franchise?
5. **Reporting** — per-store views plus an HQ roll-up.

## My recommendation

Go with **option 1**, but treat it as a planned migration, not an incremental patch — the risk is a cross-tenant data leak from one un-scoped query, so the filtering needs to be enforced in one central place. The right time to do it is **before** you actually onboard a second store, while all data legitimately belongs to one tenant and the backfill is a no-op.

If you want, I can:
- **Draft a concrete migration plan** — the `Store` entity, which collections get `StoreId`, the central tenant-scoping mechanism, and the auth/JWT changes — sized in phases, or
- **Prototype the sidebar dropdown + store-switching** against a `Store` entity so you can see the UX,

before committing to the full data-isolation work. Which would be more useful — the full plan, or the visible prototype first?

Want me to answer the cross-cutting questions above with a recommended default for a pilates franchise (shared clients, per-store staff/payroll, etc.)? That's usually where the real design decisions live.

content.text:
Yes — and there's a lot of low-hanging fruit here. I audited the public site; here's the state of things.

## What you have ✅
- Static build served by nginx (fast, crawlable — good foundation)
- Per-page `<title>` + `<meta description>`
- `lang="en"`, favicon, PWA manifest, theme-color
- Real server-rendered content on the homepage (crawlers see the hero/copy, not an empty shell)

## What's missing ❌ (this is where the SEO wins are)
| Gap | Impact |
|---|---|
| **No `robots.txt`** | Crawlers have no directives; admin/account pages may get indexed |
| **No `sitemap.xml`** | Google has to discover pages on its own; slower/incomplete indexing |
| **No canonical tags** | Risk of duplicate-URL dilution (apex vs trailing-slash, query params) |
| **No Open Graph / Twitter cards** | Links shared on FB/IG/Zalo/WhatsApp show no image or title preview |
| **No JSON-LD structured data** | ← **biggest local-SEO miss.** A `LocalBusiness`/`HealthClub` schema with address, geo-coordinates, opening hours, price range, and phone is what drives Google Maps/Knowledge-Panel results for "pilates Da Nang" |
| **English only** | A big chunk of Da Nang local search is in Vietnamese |

## What I can implement
**Technical foundation (safe, ~all additive, no behavior change):**
1. `robots.txt` — allow public pages, disallow `/admin`, `/account`, `/my-bookings`, etc., link the sitemap
2. `sitemap.xml` — via the official `@astrojs/sitemap` integration (auto-generated on build)
3. `<link rel="canonical">` on every page (driven off the apex domain)
4. Open Graph + Twitter Card tags in `CustomerLayout` (title, description, image, url, type)
5. **JSON-LD `HealthClub` schema** — NAP (name/address/phone), geo, opening hours, price range, sameAs (your IG/FB) → the single highest-value item for a local studio
6. Tighten per-page titles/descriptions (keyword-focused: "Reformer Pilates Da Nang", etc.) and add an OG share image

**Bigger scope (optional, separate):** Vietnamese localization (`hreflang`), a blog/content section for ranking on informational queries, and image `alt`/`loading="lazy"` sweeps.

One thing to note: `booking` and `packages` pull their content from the API at runtime (client-side), so crawlers see mostly empty shells there. The homepage is the real ranking asset, so I'd focus structured data and copy there — that's fine for a studio site.

To scope it right:

content.text:
Happy to — but one important guardrail first, because it directly affects whether this ad gets **approved and whether it's safe to run**:

**Meta will reject ads that claim to "treat," "cure," or "fix" a medical condition like scoliosis**, and health regulators treat that as a medical claim a Pilates studio isn't licensed to make. So we frame it around what Pilates genuinely and defensibly offers people *living with* scoliosis — **posture, mobility, core strength, moving with confidence, and working with trained instructors** — not a cure. This is also just more credible to the reader.

Here's compliant, high-converting copy you can drop straight in:

---

### Option A — Empowering / lifestyle angle (recommended)
**Primary text:**
> Living with scoliosis doesn't mean living with limits. 🌿
>
> At Soul Pilates Da Nang, our instructors guide you through mindful, low-impact movement designed to build core strength, improve posture, and help you move through your day with more ease and confidence.
>
> Every body is different — that's why we start with *you*. Book your first session and feel the difference of movement made for your spine.

**Headline:** Mindful Pilates for a Stronger, More Confident You
**Description:** Boutique studio in Da Nang · Small groups & private sessions

---

### Option B — Curiosity / question hook
**Primary text:**
> Struggling with posture or back discomfort? 🧘‍♀️
>
> Pilates is one of the most gentle, controlled ways to strengthen your core and support better alignment — guided every step by our trained Soul Pilates instructors.
>

content.text:
Here's the stuff that actually moves the needle for a **local boutique studio** — in priority order. I'll be specific to your situation (Da Nang, physical location, the pixel + CAPI you already wired up).

## 1. The single biggest lever: location targeting
You sell a service people physically come to. This matters more than any interest targeting.

- **Set location to a radius around the studio**, not "Vietnam" or "Da Nang" city-wide. In the ad set, drop a pin on 120A Nguyễn Văn Thoại and set a **radius of ~10–15 km** (covers Ngũ Hành Sơn, Sơn Trà, Hải Châu — realistic commute distance).
- Change the dropdown from "People living in or recently in this location" to **"People living in this location"** — you don't want tourists passing through who'll never come back.
- This one change alone stops you burning budget on people who can't attend.

## 2. Detailed targeting: go broad, let the pixel work
You already have the Pixel + Conversions API sending events. That's your targeting engine now — Meta's algorithm finds converters better than manual interests for a small local audience.

- **Recommended:** leave detailed targeting **empty (broad)** + rely on the radius. Meta's note in your screenshot ("broad audiences can improve performance") is right *when you have a conversion signal feeding it*, which you do.
- **If you want a safety rail:** add a broad interest layer like *Pilates, Yoga, Physical fitness, Wellness, Back pain* with **Advantage detailed targeting ON** (so Meta can expand beyond it). Don't stack 15 narrow interests — that fights the algorithm.
- **Age:** 25–55. **Gender:** consider **women only** if that's 80%+ of your clientele — but test broad first; men with back/posture issues convert too.

## 3. Fix the conversion event (this is currently working against you)
Your ad set optimizes for **Initiate Checkout**. For a **cold** scoliosis/posture audience with a small daily budget, that event is too deep and too rare — Meta needs **~50 conversions per week per ad set** to exit the learning phase, and you won't hit that on checkouts early.

- Start optimizing for a **mid-funnel event** you fire more often — **Lead**, **Contact**, or **View Content** — to give the algorithm volume to learn from.
- Once you're consistently getting 50+/week, graduate the campaign to Initiate Checkout / Purchase.
- (Worth confirming your funnel actually fires a Lead/Contact event — you have the CAPI plumbing; if it doesn't fire one at "booking started," that's a quick add on the site.)

## 4. Placements: Advantage+ Placements ON
- **Turn on Advantage+ Placements** (automatic). For a small budget, manually restricting placements just raises your costs.
- **One caveat:** design your creative **vertical/square (9:16 and 1:1)** so it looks native in Reels and Stories, where most cheap impressions are. A landscape-only image gets letterboxed and ignored.
- After ~2 weeks, check the placement breakdown; if Audience Network is spending with zero results, *then* exclude it — not before.

## 5. Budget & structure
- **Keep it simple: one campaign, one ad set, 2–3 ad creatives.** Don't split into many ad sets on a small budget — you'll starve each one below the data it needs.
- **Starting budget:** for Da Nang, **200,000–300,000 VND/day** is a realistic test level. Run it **at least 7 days untouched** — do not edit the ad set daily; every edit resets the learning phase.
- Let Meta distribute across the 2–3 creatives (that's your real A/B test — different hooks/images, same audience).

## 6. Creative = 70% of your result
The audience and placements only matter if the creative stops the scroll.

- **3 variations to test:** (a) the empowering/lifestyle angle, (b) the question hook ("Struggling with posture?"), (c) a short **founder/instructor talking-to-camera Reel** — video massively outperforms static for local wellness.
- **First 3 seconds and the on-image text carry it.** Keep text overlay short.
- **Compliance still applies** (no "treat/cure," no before/after X-rays) — a rejected ad kills momentum.

## 7. After launch — what to actually watch
Ignore vanity metrics. Watch, in order:
1. **Cost per result** (per Lead, then per booking) — your north star.
2. **CTR (link)** — under ~1% means the *creative* is weak, not the targeting.
3. **Frequency** — if it climbs past ~2.5–3 in a small radius, your audience is fatigued; refresh creative.
4. **Placement & age/gender breakdowns** after a week — cut what clearly wastes spend.

---

### Your concrete action list
1. Radius targeting ~10–15 km, "living in this location" ✅
2. Detailed targeting broad (or one broad interest + Advantage expansion) ✅
3. Switch optimization event to **Lead/Contact/View Content** ← most important fix ✅
4. Advantage+ Placements ON, creative in 9:16 + 1:1 ✅
5. One ad set, 2–3 creatives, ~250k VND/day, 7 days untouched ✅

Two things I can do right now to support this:
- **Draft the 3rd creative** — a script for a 15–20s instructor talking-to-camera Reel (EN + VN), which is usually the top performer for local studios.

content.text:
Good instinct — Da Nang genuinely has a big nomad/expat + affluent-local market, and those people **pay premium prices without blinking**. But there are two realities about Meta targeting you need to know up front, because they change the *how*:

1. **Meta has gutted income/wealth targeting.** Direct "household income" targeting only exists in the **US**. In Vietnam you **cannot** directly target "rich people" — you target *proxies* for wealth (luxury interests, iPhone users, business travel). Anyone selling you "income targeting in Vietnam" is guessing.
2. **These are 3 different people who need 3 different messages** — a short-stay traveller wants a drop-in class, a 6-month nomad wants a package, an affluent local wants private sessions. So this is really a **2–3 ad-set** structure, not one.

Here's how to actually reach each.

## 1. Digital nomads & expats (living in Da Nang 1–12 months)
This is your best segment — they're here long enough to buy packages and have disposable income.

- **Location:** Da Nang, **"People living in this location"** (they're residents while they're here).
- **Language:** set language to **English** (and optionally Korean/Russian — big Da Nang expat groups). ← This is the strongest nomad filter Meta gives you. It auto-excludes most locals.
- **Behaviors → find these:** `Frequent Travellers`, `Frequent International Travellers`, and under **"Expats"** the `Lived in [country] – now in Vietnam` options (still available in some accounts).
- **Interests:** `Digital nomad`, `Remote work`, `Coworking`, `Expat`, plus wellness (`Pilates, Yoga, Wellness`).
- **Creative:** **English**, angle = *"New to Da Nang? Find your studio."* / community + wellness.

## 2. Short-stay travellers (days–weeks)
Lower value — they won't buy a 10-class pack. Only worth it if you sell **drop-in / class passes**.

- **Location:** Da Nang, but switch to **"People recently in this location"** (catches tourists currently here).
- **Language:** English + Korean.
- **Creative:** a **drop-in / single-class offer** ("Visiting Da Nang? Drop into a class"), *not* package promotion. Send them to a drop-in booking, not checkout for a pack.
- Honestly: I'd **start with #1 and #3 and only add this if you have drop-in pricing to promote.**

## 3. Affluent Vietnamese (this is the proxy game)
You can't target income directly, so you stack **wealth signals**:

- **Location:** Da Nang radius, "living in this location," **language = Vietnamese**.
- **Wealth-proxy interests** (layer several with Advantage expansion ON): luxury/premium brands — `Chanel, Dior, Gucci, Apple, Mercedes-Benz, BMW`; `Business class / First class travel`; `Fine dining`; `Luxury goods`; `Spa & wellness`; `Private members clubs`.
- **Device targeting (underrated):** in Placements → device, target **iOS / iPhone & iPad only**. iPhone ownership is a strong affluence proxy in Vietnam and instantly skews the audience upscale.
- **Behavior:** `Engaged Shoppers` (people who click "shop now" — higher purchase intent).
- **Creative:** **Vietnamese**, premium/aspirational tone — private sessions, boutique, exclusivity. Lead with **private/1-on-1** pricing, not group.

## How to structure it (important)
Don't cram all three into one ad set — the messages and languages conflict. Use **separate ad sets**:

| Ad set | Location setting | Language | Key targeting | Creative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nomads/Expats** | Living in Da Nang | English (+KR/RU) | Frequent travellers, expat, digital nomad | EN, community/wellness |
| **Affluent locals** | Da Nang radius | Vietnamese | Luxury interests + iPhone-only + Engaged Shoppers | VN, private/premium |
| *(optional)* Travellers | Recently in Da Nang | English/KR | Frequent travellers | EN, drop-in offer |

## The honest caveat
Stacking iPhone-only + luxury interests + a small radius can shrink your audience so much that Meta can't optimize (you'll see the audience bar go deep into **"Narrow"** and costs spike). Watch the **estimated audience size** — if any ad set drops below ~**30,000–50,000 people**, loosen it (drop the narrowest interest, or widen radius). On a small local market, **language + location does 80% of the work**; the luxury/device layers are the fine-tuning.

And **budget per ad set**: if you run 2–3 ad sets, each still needs enough to learn — I'd want **~200k VND/day *each***, or run them one at a time rather than starving all three.

content: should i do campaign budget or adset

message.content: should i do campaign budget or adset

content.text:
Short answer: **for your situation, use Ad Set budget (ABO) — at least to start.** Here's the reasoning, because it depends on what you're doing.

## Why ABO for you
You're running **ad sets with deliberately different audiences and languages** (English nomads vs. Vietnamese affluent locals). That's exactly when ABO wins:

- **CBO (campaign budget) chases cheapest results.** It'll dump most of the money into whichever ad set gets cheap clicks — usually the broad English one — and **starve your Vietnamese/premium ad set** before it ever gets enough data to prove itself. You'd never learn if the affluent-local segment works.
- **ABO lets you guarantee each audience a fair test.** You *decide* the nomad set gets 200k/day and the local set gets 200k/day, so both get enough volume to exit the learning phase and give you real cost-per-result numbers.

On a small local budget, **control beats optimization** — you don't have enough spend for CBO's algorithm to distribute intelligently across segments; it just picks a favorite.

## When you'd switch to CBO later
Once you've run ABO for 2–3 weeks and **know which audience/creative actually converts**, consolidate the winners into a CBO campaign and let Meta optimize *within proven winners*. CBO is great for scaling things that already work — bad for discovering what works.

## The rule of thumb
| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Testing different audiences/languages, small budget | **ABO** ← you |
| Scaling proven winners, want max efficiency | CBO |
| One audience, one message | Either (CBO fine) |

## One caveat
If you truly only run **one ad set** (say, just nomads to start), it doesn't matter — CBO and ABO are identical with a single ad set, so pick whichever the UI defaults to.

**Practical move:** Turn **off** Advantage campaign budget, set the budget at the **ad set level**, give each audience ~200k VND/day, run 7 days without touching it, then read the cost-per-result per ad set. That tells you where to put the money next.

I've now got the full picture, and there's an important design constraint you should weigh in on before I build it.

## What I found (good news)
- The attendee data already carries **`quantity`** (seats) and **`amountDueAtStudio`**, so the POS can tell which bookings are multi-person.
- Splitting is clean on capacity: a 2-seat booking already counts as 2 in the class, so peeling it into two 1-seat rows **doesn't change capacity** — no overbooking risk.

## The one real constraint
Every attendance row **must be attached to a client record** (`ClientId` is required — the system has no "name-only" attendee). So to split Ruan's booking into *two separate people*, the second seat needs to point at a client:
- **an existing client** (search & pick — reuses the client search already in the panel), or
- a **quick walk-in client** created on the spot.

That's the fork that shapes the UI.

## Proposed build
**Backend** — `POST /api/scheduling/booking/{id}/split`:
- Guard: only unpaid, pay-at-studio bookings with `quantity ≥ 2` (can't split something already paid or settled by credit).
- Reduce the original row to 1 seat (due = 1× drop-in), create N−1 new 1-seat rows for the assigned people (each due = 1× drop-in). Capacity untouched.

**Frontend** — in the POS popup, when `quantity ≥ 2` and unpaid, show a **"Split into separate people"** button → for each extra seat, pick/search the client (or quick-add a walk-in) → confirm → roster now shows each person as their own row, each with its own **Collect payment** so they can pay separately (cash/card, or their own package credit if linked).

Done — the full feature is live. Here's what you've got now:

## 1. The bug is fixed (the root cause)
"Book for N" was **already a real feature** — one booking with a seat `Quantity`. The checkout just wasn't accounting for it. Now the expected amount = **drop-in × seats**, so:
- **Ruan's 2-seat / 1,000,000 booking checks out cleanly with no note required.** Reopen his checkout and hit Complete — it just works.
- The note field still guards *genuine* custom amounts (discounts, part-payments).

## 2. Split into separate people (new)
In the checkout popup, any **multi-seat unpaid booking** now shows:
> 👥 This is a booking for **2** people. Want each to pay separately? **[Split into separate people]**

Clicking it:
1. Closes the popup and drops you into the roster's client search in **"Splitting a booking"** mode.
2. **Search an existing client** or **quick-add a walk-in** (the `+` button) for the person that seat belongs to.
3. That seat is peeled off into **its own booking** (500,000), and the original drops to 1 seat.
4. Now each person has their **own Checkout button** — they can pay separately, different methods, or their own package credit if linked.

For a 3-person booking, repeat once more. Capacity never changes (the seats were already counted).

**Hard-refresh** the calendar (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) to load it.

## Guardrails I built in
- Can't split a booking that's already **paid** or settled by **package credit** (those have invoices/credits tied to them) — you'll get a clear message.
- Only unpaid pay-at-studio bookings are splittable.

One thing worth testing live before relying on it at a busy desk: do **one real split** on a test 2-seat booking and confirm both rows collect correctly. Want me to record the seats/split model in memory so it's documented, and is there anything about the split UX you'd like adjusted (e.g. a per-person split-all-at-once form instead of one-at-a-time)?

All three are live. Here's what shipped:

## 1. Notch cutoff — fixed
The class drawer header now respects the iOS safe area (`env(safe-area-inset-top)`), so the **✕ close button clears the notch/status bar** when running as an installed PWA.

## 2. Tap an attendee → contact + limited profile
Each attendee row is now tappable (shows a **"ⓘ tap for info"** hint). Tapping opens a modal with:
- **📞 phone** (tap-to-call) and **✉️ email** (tap-to-email)
- a **"👤 View full profile"** button that loads the **instructor-safe** profile: total visits, last visit, member-since, DOB, referral, tags, and **⚕ medical/health notes** — **no financial data** (per your choice).

## 3. Remove attendee — added
The modal has a **🗑 Remove from class** button (shown only on classes the instructor owns). It confirms, frees the seat, and refreshes the roster.

## Security built in
- Remove and profile go through the **`/api/instructor/*`** controller with **ownership checks** — an instructor can only remove attendees from **their own** sessions (verified server-side, and the booking must actually be on that session). I deliberately did **not** loosen the admin `/api/scheduling` endpoints.
- The profile endpoint returns a **financials-free** DTO, so instructors never see payments/balances.

## To test
Have the instructor **fully close and reopen the PWA** (PWAs cache hard — a plain refresh may not pull the new bundle). Then: open a class → tap an attendee → confirm contact, "View full profile", and a test **Remove** on one of her own classes.

content.text: Line 1456 fetches bookings per-session — let me see if that's a per-session loop (N+1) or lazy:

Here's the honest answer: **10-second polling won't melt your server at your scale — but your calendar's current fetch pattern makes each refresh ~40× heavier than it needs to be, and polling multiplies that waste.**

## What one calendar refresh actually costs
I checked — it's an **N+1 pattern**:
1. `GET /api/scheduling?start&end` — **1** request (all sessions for the week)
2. Then `batchFetchAttendees()` fires **one `/session/{id}/bookings` request per visible session** (batched 8 at a time)

So a week view with ~40 classes = **~41 requests per refresh**, not 1.

## The math at 10s
| Staff with calendar open | Requests/refresh | Per 10s | Sustained |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~41 | 41 | ~4 req/s |
| 3 | ~41 each | ~123 | ~12 req/s |
| 5 | ~41 each | ~205 | ~20 req/s |

~12–20 req/s of simple indexed Mongo reads is **not** going to strain the .NET backend or MongoDB on your VPS in throughput terms. So: **not harsh in the "server will fall over" sense.**

**But** two real problems:
1. **It's wasteful** — you re-pull every booking for every class every 10s even when nothing changed. That's ~40 pointless Mongo round-trips per idle refresh.
2. **It scales badly** — cost grows with (classes × staff), and if the PWA keeps polling while backgrounded, phones hammer it 24/7.

## What I'd actually do (in order of value)

1. **Collapse the N+1 first.** Add one batch endpoint (`/api/scheduling/bookings?sessionIds=...`) or fold booking counts into the main `/api/scheduling` response. Then a refresh = **1 request instead of 41**, and 10s polling becomes trivial.
2. **Pause polling when the tab is hidden** (`document.hidden`) — otherwise every idle device keeps fetching. Easy, big win.
3. **Loosen the interval to 20–30s.** For "did a new booking arrive," 10s rarely matters and it cuts load 2–3×.
4. **Best option: push-driven refresh.** You now have the new-booking push system we just built — reuse that signal so the calendar refreshes **only when something actually changes**, giving near-zero idle load and *instant* updates instead of up-to-10s-stale ones.

## My recommendation
Don't turn on 10s polling against the current N+1 — you'd be doing ~40× the necessary work on a timer. **Do #1 (batch endpoint) + #2 (pause when hidden) first**, then either poll at 20–30s or (better) drive refreshes off the push you already have. That's cheaper *and* fresher than naive 10s polling.
