Done — deployed and verified in the bundle. You picked the best option, and it directly solves your original concern: this is **fresher *and* cheaper than 10s polling**.

## How it works now
1. Whenever a booking push fires — **new booking (from any source now), cancellation, or reschedule** — the service worker (`sw.js`) broadcasts a `sp-data-changed` signal to every open tab.
2. The calendar hears it and **refreshes in place** — no page reload, no flicker.
3. Built-in efficiency:
   - **Coalesced** (1.5s debounce) — a burst of bookings triggers one refresh, not many.
   - **Skipped while the tab is hidden** — it defers and catches up when you look again, so it never runs the expensive render for a screen nobody's watching.

## Why this beats 10s polling
- **Idle cost ≈ zero** — nothing happens until something actually changes (vs. ~41 requests every 10s forever).
- **Faster** — updates appear ~1.5s after the booking, not up to 10s later.
- **Self-targeting** — only devices that receive the push (Admin/Manager/Owner + the session's instructor) refresh, which is exactly who has the calendar open.

## Two things to know
1. **Close and reopen the PWA once** on each device — the updated service worker needs to install/activate before the live-refresh kicks in. After that it's automatic.
2. It refreshes on **booking events** (which push). Session edits/blocks don't push — but those are done *by* the person looking at the calendar, who sees them instantly anyway.

Two optional follow-ups:
- **Add the same live-refresh to the instructor PWA schedule** (it currently only refreshes after the instructor's own actions) — quick to do.
- A subtle **"Updated just now" toast** on live refresh so staff notice it happened.

## The conditions that actually matter
1. **Each browser must have notifications enabled separately.** Push subscriptions are per-browser-per-device — enabling on the phone does **not** enable the desktop. Whoever wants live refresh on their laptop has to click **"enable notifications"** in that desktop browser once and grant permission.
2. **The calendar tab must be open.** The service worker only broadcasts the refresh to open tabs. (The notification banner still shows even if it's closed — but there's nothing to refresh.)
3. **The browser must be running.** If the calendar tab is open, it is — so this is automatic. Even if the tab is *backgrounded* (browser open, different tab focused), the push is delivered and the refresh **defers, then catches up** when you switch back to it.
4. HTTPS (you have it) and the updated service worker activated (one reload after the deploy).

## The one gotcha to watch
Because I set `userVisibleOnly: true` on the subscription (required by Chrome), **every refresh also shows a notification** — so on desktop, staff get a banner *and* the live refresh together. That's usually fine, but if reception has the calendar open on a desktop all day, they'll see a notification pop for every booking. If that's noisy, the cleaner fix is the **"pulse" approach** (poll a tiny cheap endpoint) which refreshes silently with no notification dependency at all.

So: **desktop works as long as that browser opted into notifications.** If you'd rather have silent desktop refresh that doesn't depend on each person enabling push, tell me and I'll add the lightweight pulse-poll as the desktop path.

Deployed. The **VAT (online only)** fee is now excluded from commissionable revenue everywhere it's calculated:

## What changed
| Commission path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Revenue-split** (% of monthly revenue) | summed `TotalNet` (incl. VAT) | sums `TotalNet − OnlineFeeAmount` |
| **Per-class payroll** (`ResolveAttendeeRevenueAsync`) | whole-invoice & amount-paid fallbacks included VAT | strips the attendee's apportioned VAT share |
| **Per-class display** (calendar/class panel) | same leak | same fix, so display matches payout |

## Important nuance
The VAT is stored **separately** as `Invoice.OnlineFeeAmount` — it was never inside an invoice *line*. So for online bookings whose paid invoice had a proper line for the attendee, commission was **already** on the base price (fee-free). The leak was only in the **fallback paths**:
- whole-invoice `TotalNet` (multi-line / missing-line invoices), and
- `att.AmountPaid` for online bookings where the payment amount bundled the VAT.

Those now subtract the fee, apportioned per attendee when an invoice covers multiple people.

## One thing to decide
Commission is **recomputed from source data** each payroll run, so this takes effect **going forward** and for any period you haven't finalized yet. But **already-finalized `PayrollRun` snapshots won't change retroactively** — they're frozen records.

So: if the **current/open period** had online bookings, its commission will now be correct on the next calculation. If a **past, already-run payroll** over-counted the VAT and you want it corrected, tell me the month and I can recompute/compare it.

124	    {
125	        var payments = await _payments
126	            .Find(Builders<Payment>.Filter.And(
127	                Builders<Payment>.Filter.Gte(p => p.PaymentDate, start),
128	                Builders<Payment>.Filter.Lt(p => p.PaymentDate, end)))
129	            .Project(p => new PaymentRevenueRow { InvoiceId = p.InvoiceId, AmountPaid = p.AmountPaid })

131	        if (payments.Count == 0) return 0m;
132	
133	        var invoiceIds = payments
134	            .Where(p => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(p.InvoiceId))
135	            .Select(p => p.InvoiceId!)
136	            .Distinct()
137	            .ToList();
138	
139	        var validInvoiceIds = (await _invoices
140	                .Find(Builders<Invoice>.Filter.And(
141	                    Builders<Invoice>.Filter.In(i => i.Id, invoiceIds),
142	                    Builders<Invoice>.Filter.Ne(i => i.Status, "VOIDED")))
143	                .Project(i => i.Id)
144	                .ToListAsync())

146	
147	        return payments
148	            .Where(p => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(p.InvoiceId) && validInvoiceIds.Contains(p.InvoiceId))

Deployed and healthy. Here's what's now live, system-wide:

## Revenue now excludes the online fee
The dashboard **Monthly Revenue** figure is now **net of the "VAT (online only)" fee** — the fee is treated as a pass-through, not studio earnings. This is exact for fully-paid invoices and apportioned for partial payments, and it's computed from source each time, so **past months recompute net too** (delta % compares net-to-net).

## Invoices unchanged (as you asked)
No invoice data was touched — Kerry's SP-INV-260706-0020 still shows the ₫42,500 VAT, receipts still print the "VAT (online only)" line. Only the *revenue reporting* excludes it.

## New "fees received" analytic
The Revenue widget now shows a sub-line:
> **+ ₫X online fees collected (excl. from revenue)** — the total VAT collected this month.

(If it's zero it reads "Revenue is net of online (VAT) fees.")

## Commission
Already excludes the fee from the prior change — so revenue and commission are now consistent.

## ⚠️ One place I deliberately did NOT change yet
The **accounting P&L statement** (`AccountingService`) still sums the fee into its "Total Sales / Earned Revenue." I left it because netting it there cleanly needs matching adjustments to the **revenue-by-method** and **revenue-by-category** breakdowns so the statement still balances — that's a careful, separate change rather than a quick patch. Your **dashboard** total revenue is correct now; the **P&L** total will still be ~fee higher until I do that pass.

Want me to do the **P&L pass** next (net the fee out of Total Revenue there and add a "VAT/online fees collected" line to the statement so it balances)? Let me record the rule so it's consistent going forward:

questions.question: What database should the new Studio Nexis project start with?

options.label: Fresh empty database (Recommended)
options.description: New project starts clean — no clients, bookings, or invoices. Safest: no real customer PII copied into an experimental project. You seed/test data yourself.

options.label: Copy of the current live data
options.description: Clone all current clients, bookings, packages, invoices into the new DB. Realistic data to work with, but duplicates real customer personal + financial data into a separate project.

questions.question: How should external integrations (Stripe, Meta Pixel, Brevo/SMTP email) be set up in the new project?

options.label: Disabled / clean slate (Recommended)
options.description: New project gets its own env with payment, ad-tracking, and email integrations OFF (blank keys). Prevents the fork from charging cards, sending real emails, or polluting Meta/analytics. You add test keys when ready.

options.label: Reuse the original's keys
options.description: Copy the same Stripe/Meta/Brevo keys. Risky: the fork could take real payments, send real emails to customers, and mix ad/analytics data with the live studio.

content.text: Fresh DB + clean integrations — the safe path, and it means no live data or secrets get copied. Let me study the original compose so I can produce a fully isolated variant (distinct names, ports, data dirs). This only reads the original — doesn't modify it:

# Soul Pilates — PRODUCTION Stack
#
#  Assumes you've copied soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz and
#  soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz onto the host and loaded them with:
#    docker load < soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz
#    docker load < soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz
#
#  Then:
#    cp prod.env.sample prod.env  # edit secrets
#    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
#
#  External access (mongosh / redis-cli from your dev machine):
#    MongoDB → host:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 27117)
#    Redis   → host:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 6479)
#    Both are auth-protected. Restrict access at the firewall to trusted IPs:
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 27117
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 6479
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port so the operator can run mongosh
      # from a dev machine. Auth is mandatory (MONGO_USER / MONGO_PASSWORD).
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27117}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port for direct redis-cli access.
      # Protected by REDIS_PASSWORD via --requirepass.
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6479}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6324:9000"      # S3 API — exposed so the public can fetch images
      - "127.0.0.1:6325:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s

  # One-shot that creates the soulpilates-public bucket (idempotent).
  # Runs after rustfs is healthy so it never races the S3 API startup.
  # Sets anonymous download policy so the frontend can fetch images directly.
  rustfs-bucket-init:
    image: minio/mc:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-bucket-init
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 $$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY $$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY &&
        mc mb --ignore-existing rustfs/soulpilates-public &&
        mc anonymous set download rustfs/soulpilates-public &&
        echo 'Bucket soulpilates-public ready.'
      "
    depends_on:
      rustfs:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    image: soulpilates/backend:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8391:8080"
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Production
      ASPNETCORE_URLS: http://+:8080
      MongoDbSettings__ConnectionString: "mongodb://${MONGO_USER}:${MONGO_PASSWORD}@mongo:27017/?authSource=admin"
      MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName: soulpilates
      JwtSettings__Secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
      # P4-S12 — optional previous-key slot for the rotation grace window.
      # Empty string is interpreted by Program.cs as "no previous key" (single-key mode).
      JwtSettings__PreviousSecret: ${JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET:-}
      StorageSettings__Endpoint: "http://rustfs:9000"
      StorageSettings__AccessKey: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      StorageSettings__SecretKey: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      StorageSettings__PublicBucket: soulpilates-public
      StorageSettings__PublicUrlBase: ${PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE}
      StorageSettings__ForcePathStyle: "true"
      StripeSettings__SecretKey: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}
      StripeSettings__PublishableKey: ${STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY}
      StripeSettings__WebhookSecret: ${STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET}
      StripeSettings__Enabled: ${STRIPE_ENABLED}
      # ───── SMTP / Email ─────
      SmtpSettings__Host: ${SMTP_HOST}
      SmtpSettings__Port: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      SmtpSettings__Username: ${SMTP_USERNAME}
      SmtpSettings__Password: ${SMTP_PASSWORD}
      SmtpSettings__FromEmail: ${SMTP_FROM_EMAIL}
      SmtpSettings__FromName: ${SMTP_FROM_NAME:-Soul Pilates Da Nang}
      SmtpSettings__Enabled: ${SMTP_ENABLED:-true}
      SmtpSettings__EmailRegisterVerificationEnabled: ${SMTP_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ENABLED:-true}
      # Email test-mode safety net: when TestMode=true, real customers never get
      # mail — everything is redirected to TestRedirectTo (or dropped), except
      # addresses in TestAllowlist which still receive the real email.
      SmtpSettings__TestMode: ${SMTP_TEST_MODE:-false}
      SmtpSettings__TestRedirectTo: ${SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO:-}
      SmtpSettings__TestAllowlist: ${SMTP_TEST_ALLOWLIST:-}
      # ───── Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel + Conversions API ─────
      MetaTracking__PixelId: ${META_PIXEL_ID:-}
      MetaTracking__AccessToken: ${META_CAPI_TOKEN:-}
      MetaTracking__TestEventCode: ${META_CAPI_TEST_CODE:-}
      MetaTracking__Enabled: ${META_TRACKING_ENABLED:-true}
      # ───── Web Push (VAPID) ─────
      WebPush__Enabled: ${WEBPUSH_ENABLED:-true}
      WebPush__Subject: ${WEBPUSH_SUBJECT:-mailto:admin@soulpilates.com.vn}
      WebPush__PublicKey: ${WEBPUSH_PUBLIC_KEY}
      WebPush__PrivateKey: ${WEBPUSH_PRIVATE_KEY}
      # ───── Seed & CORS ─────
      AdminSeed__Enabled: "true"
      AdminSeed__Email: ${ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL}
      AdminSeed__Password: ${ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD}
      AdminSeed__Name: "Soul Pilates Admin"
      # CORS — single origin in path-split deployment
      CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      # ───── Public site (customer-facing absolute URLs in emails) ─────
      # EmailService builds verify-email, reset-password and "view account"
      # links against this base. Must match the host VestaCP serves publicly.
      PublicSite__BaseUrl: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      # ───── Timezone ─────
      TZ: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
      # ───── Observability ─────
      SentrySettings__Dsn: ${SENTRY_DSN}
    volumes:
      - ./data/soulpilates-api-logs:/var/log/soulpilates-api
    depends_on:
      mongo:
        condition: service_started
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      rustfs-bucket-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]

  frontend:
    image: soulpilates/frontend:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3719:80"
    networks: [public]

input.content:
# Studio Nexis — ISOLATED fork of the Soul Pilates stack.
# Fully separate from the live project: own containers, ports, data dirs,
# database ("studionexis"), media bucket, and network. GlitchTip omitted.
#
#   cd /opt/studionexis
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d
name: studionexis

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: studionexis-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27118}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: studionexis-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6480}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6326:9000"
      - "127.0.0.1:6327:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s

  rustfs-bucket-init:
    image: minio/mc:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-bucket-init
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 $$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY $$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY &&
        mc mb --ignore-existing rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        mc anonymous set download rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        echo 'Bucket studionexis-public ready.'
      "
    depends_on:
      rustfs:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    image: studionexis/backend:latest
    container_name: studionexis-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8392:8080"
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Production
      ASPNETCORE_URLS: http://+:8080
      MongoDbSettings__ConnectionString: "mongodb://${MONGO_USER}:${MONGO_PASSWORD}@mongo:27017/?authSource=admin"
      MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName: studionexis
      JwtSettings__Secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
      JwtSettings__PreviousSecret: ${JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET:-}
      StorageSettings__Endpoint: "http://rustfs:9000"
      StorageSettings__AccessKey: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      StorageSettings__SecretKey: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      StorageSettings__PublicBucket: studionexis-public
      StorageSettings__PublicUrlBase: ${PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE}
      StorageSettings__ForcePathStyle: "true"
      # ── Integrations DISABLED for the fork (clean slate) ──
      StripeSettings__SecretKey: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__PublishableKey: ${STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__WebhookSecret: ${STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET:-}
      StripeSettings__Enabled: ${STRIPE_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__Host: ${SMTP_HOST:-}
      SmtpSettings__Port: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      SmtpSettings__Username: ${SMTP_USERNAME:-}
      SmtpSettings__Password: ${SMTP_PASSWORD:-}
      SmtpSettings__FromEmail: ${SMTP_FROM_EMAIL:-noreply@studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn}
      SmtpSettings__FromName: ${SMTP_FROM_NAME:-Studio Nexis}
      SmtpSettings__Enabled: ${SMTP_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__EmailRegisterVerificationEnabled: ${SMTP_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__TestMode: ${SMTP_TEST_MODE:-true}
      SmtpSettings__TestRedirectTo: ${SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO:-}
      SmtpSettings__TestAllowlist: ${SMTP_TEST_ALLOWLIST:-}
      MetaTracking__PixelId: ${META_PIXEL_ID:-}
      MetaTracking__AccessToken: ${META_CAPI_TOKEN:-}
      MetaTracking__TestEventCode: ${META_CAPI_TEST_CODE:-}
      MetaTracking__Enabled: ${META_TRACKING_ENABLED:-false}
      WebPush__Enabled: ${WEBPUSH_ENABLED:-false}
      WebPush__Subject: ${WEBPUSH_SUBJECT:-mailto:admin@studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn}
      WebPush__PublicKey: ${WEBPUSH_PUBLIC_KEY:-}
      WebPush__PrivateKey: ${WEBPUSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}
      AdminSeed__Enabled: "true"
      AdminSeed__Email: ${ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL}
      AdminSeed__Password: ${ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD}
      AdminSeed__Name: "Studio Nexis Admin"
      CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      PublicSite__BaseUrl: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      TZ: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
      SentrySettings__Dsn: ${SENTRY_DSN:-}
    volumes:
      - ./data/api-logs:/var/log/soulpilates-api
    depends_on:
      mongo:
        condition: service_started
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      rustfs-bucket-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]

  frontend:
    image: studionexis/frontend:latest
    container_name: studionexis-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3720:80"
    networks: [public]

networks:
  internal:
    driver: bridge
  public:
    driver: bridge

content.text: Now a helper script so you generate the secrets yourself (I don't write secret values):

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fills the __SET_ME__ secret placeholders in prod.env with fresh random values.
# Run once, on the host:  bash generate-secrets.sh
# ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD is set to a random value too — change it to something you
# can remember, or reset it later, since it's your first admin login.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if ! grep -q '__SET_ME__' prod.env; then
  echo "No __SET_ME__ placeholders left — secrets already set. Nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

gen() { openssl rand -hex 32; }

# Replace each secret's placeholder with an independent random value.
for key in MONGO_PASSWORD REDIS_PASSWORD JWT_SECRET RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD; do
  val="$(gen)"
  # Only replace the placeholder on that exact key's line.
  sed -i "s|^${key}=__SET_ME__$|${key}=${val}|" prod.env
done

echo "Secrets generated in prod.env."
echo "→ Your initial admin login:"
grep -E '^ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL=|^ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD=' prod.env
echo "  (change ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD in prod.env now if you want a memorable one, BEFORE first boot)"

message.content: I would now like to recreate this system for studionexis to be a saas product that we license to studios. there will need to be a complete restructure to the way it works, will doing this be potentially harmful to the live studio system?

content.text:
Good question to ask *before* diving in. The honest answer has two parts, and the distinction matters a lot.

## Will the SaaS restructure harm the live studio? — Not the code or data, but watch the shared infrastructure.

Because I already isolated the fork, the **restructure itself is safe at the logical level**:
- Separate codebase (`/opt/studionexis`) — editing/rewriting it can't touch `/opt/soulpilates`.
- Separate database, containers, ports, media, secrets — no data crossover.
- Integrations off — the fork can't email customers or charge cards.

So a "complete restructure" of *how Studio Nexis works* won't corrupt or expose the live studio's data or break its code.

**But** both systems share the same physical box, and that's where the real risk lives:

| Shared surface | Risk during a SaaS build | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Host RAM/CPU/disk** (7.8 GB, no swap) | Multi-tenant work — many tenant DBs, migrations, load tests, seeding — can starve the live containers → live studio slows or OOM-crashes | The biggest risk. Cap the fork's resources, or move it off-box |
| **Shared nginx** | Wildcard/per-tenant subdomain routing means frequent nginx edits; one bad reload breaks the live vhost | Always `nginx -t` before reload (already my habit) |
| **Shared Docker daemon** | A `docker system prune` or a runaway build can affect live images/containers | Never prune broadly; tag carefully |
| **Shared DNS zone** (`soulpilates.com.vn`) | Adding tenant subdomains is fine; a careless edit to apex/`www` records isn't | Only touch new records |
| **Reusing live secrets/accounts** | If SaaS billing/email reuses the studio's Stripe/Brevo/Meta keys → cross-charges, mixed data | Use brand-new, separate accounts |

## My real recommendation
For **isolated experimentation**, the current fork is perfect. But a **true multi-tenant SaaS you license to other businesses** is a large, long-lived product that will get heavy (tenant provisioning, per-tenant data isolation strong enough for *unrelated* companies, billing, plan tiers, subdomain/custom-domain routing, onboarding, per-tenant backups, CI/CD, load). Running that build **on the same server as a paying live studio is a liability purely from co-location** — even with perfect logical isolation, resource contention and shared-nginx/Docker mistakes are operational risks to a business that's actively taking bookings and payments.

**So: build the SaaS on a separate server/VPS.** Keep this box for the live studio only. Clone the `/opt/studionexis` fork over to a fresh host and do the restructure there. That drops the "could this hurt the live studio?" risk to essentially zero.

## One more thing worth flagging
This is the **multi-tenancy** problem from our earlier franchise conversation, but bigger — franchises were *one* business with multiple locations; SaaS is *many unrelated* businesses. The data-isolation bar is much higher (a bug leaking Studio A's clients to Studio B is a serious breach, not just an annoyance). That reinforces doing it on separate infrastructure with a proper tenant-isolation design from day one.

**How I can help next:**
1. **Write the SaaS architecture plan** — tenancy model (DB-per-tenant vs shared-schema + `TenantId`), provisioning, subdomain routing, licensing/billing, super-admin vs tenant-admin — sized in phases.
2. **Help you stand up a separate server** and migrate the fork there cleanly.
3. Both.

Which direction do you want to go — and do you already have a separate server/VPS in mind, or should the plan include provisioning one?

message.content: what if i just want to build it here and then when im ready to make it public, migrate it. would that be safe?

content.text:
Yes — that's a sensible plan, and it's genuinely safe **as long as you keep it a *build*, not a *launch*, on this box.** The distinction is everything:

## Why it's safe
Development work is **light** — editing code, rebuilding images, running a few test tenants, clicking around. That's a fraction of the resources a live production system uses. The fork is already fully isolated (own DB, containers, ports, secrets, integrations off), so nothing you *build* can reach the live studio's code or data.

And because I set it up isolated from day one, **migration later is a lift-and-shift, not a rewrite** — copy `/opt/studionexis` to the new server, move its Mongo dump, rebuild the images, point DNS. It's designed to move.

## The guardrails that keep "build here" safe
Stay on the green side of this line:

| ✅ Safe to do here (building) | ⚠️ Don't do here (migrate first) |
|---|---|
| Edit/restructure code, rebuild images | **Onboard real paying tenants** |
| Run 2–5 **fake** test tenants | Take **real payments** / send real customer email |
| Design tenancy, routing, billing logic | **Load/stress testing** (spins up many DBs, eats RAM) |
| Small seed data | Bulk-importing large real datasets |
| Edit only the `studionexis` nginx vhost (with `nginx -t`) | Broad `docker system prune`, touching soulpilates containers |

The one hard rule: **don't go public *from* this box.** Build and test with fake studios here; flip to real customers only *after* you've migrated. The moment real money and unrelated businesses' data land on it, co-location risk becomes real.

## The practical risk to actually watch
**RAM.** You've got ~4 GB reclaimable and no swap. As the SaaS build grows and you run a few test tenants, keep an eye on `free -h` and `docker stats`. If the fork's footprint starts creeping toward crowding the live containers, that's your early signal to migrate — not a crisis, just a heads-up.

## Bottom line
Build here, migrate before launch: **safe**, and the way I isolated the fork makes the eventual migration low-risk to the live studio (it's copying *out*, never modifying the live system).

Two things I can do to de-risk it further right now, if you want:
1. **Add a small resource cap** to the studionexis containers (mem limits in its compose) so the fork *can't* starve the live studio even by accident — a cheap insurance policy while you build here.
2. **Write a migration runbook + script** now (while it's simple) so moving to a dedicated server later is a checklist, not a scramble.

Want either of those — and shall we start on the actual SaaS restructure (beginning with the tenancy-model decision)?

# Studio Nexis — ISOLATED fork of the Soul Pilates stack.
# Fully separate from the live project: own containers, ports, data dirs,
# database ("studionexis"), media bucket, and network. GlitchTip omitted.
#
#   cd /opt/studionexis
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d
name: studionexis

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: studionexis-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27118}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: studionexis-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6480}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6326:9000"
      - "127.0.0.1:6327:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s

  rustfs-bucket-init:
    image: minio/mc:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-bucket-init
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 $$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY $$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY &&
        mc mb --ignore-existing rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        mc anonymous set download rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        echo 'Bucket studionexis-public ready.'
      "
    depends_on:
      rustfs:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    image: studionexis/backend:latest
    container_name: studionexis-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8392:8080"
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Production
      ASPNETCORE_URLS: http://+:8080
      MongoDbSettings__ConnectionString: "mongodb://${MONGO_USER}:${MONGO_PASSWORD}@mongo:27017/?authSource=admin"
      MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName: studionexis
      JwtSettings__Secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
      JwtSettings__PreviousSecret: ${JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET:-}
      StorageSettings__Endpoint: "http://rustfs:9000"
      StorageSettings__AccessKey: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      StorageSettings__SecretKey: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      StorageSettings__PublicBucket: studionexis-public
      StorageSettings__PublicUrlBase: ${PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE}
      StorageSettings__ForcePathStyle: "true"
      # ── Integrations DISABLED for the fork (clean slate) ──
      StripeSettings__SecretKey: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__PublishableKey: ${STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__WebhookSecret: ${STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET:-}
      StripeSettings__Enabled: ${STRIPE_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__Host: ${SMTP_HOST:-}
      SmtpSettings__Port: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      SmtpSettings__Username: ${SMTP_USERNAME:-}
      SmtpSettings__Password: ${SMTP_PASSWORD:-}
      SmtpSettings__FromEmail: ${SMTP_FROM_EMAIL:-noreply@studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn}
      SmtpSettings__FromName: ${SMTP_FROM_NAME:-Studio Nexis}
      SmtpSettings__Enabled: ${SMTP_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__EmailRegisterVerificationEnabled: ${SMTP_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ENABLED:-false}
      SmtpSettings__TestMode: ${SMTP_TEST_MODE:-true}
      SmtpSettings__TestRedirectTo: ${SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO:-}
      SmtpSettings__TestAllowlist: ${SMTP_TEST_ALLOWLIST:-}
      MetaTracking__PixelId: ${META_PIXEL_ID:-}
      MetaTracking__AccessToken: ${META_CAPI_TOKEN:-}
      MetaTracking__TestEventCode: ${META_CAPI_TEST_CODE:-}
      MetaTracking__Enabled: ${META_TRACKING_ENABLED:-false}
      WebPush__Enabled: ${WEBPUSH_ENABLED:-false}
      WebPush__Subject: ${WEBPUSH_SUBJECT:-mailto:admin@studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn}
      WebPush__PublicKey: ${WEBPUSH_PUBLIC_KEY:-}
      WebPush__PrivateKey: ${WEBPUSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}
      AdminSeed__Enabled: "true"
      AdminSeed__Email: ${ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL}
      AdminSeed__Password: ${ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD}
      AdminSeed__Name: "Studio Nexis Admin"
      CorsSettings__AllowedOrigins__0: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      PublicSite__BaseUrl: ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      TZ: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
      SentrySettings__Dsn: ${SENTRY_DSN:-}
    volumes:
      - ./data/api-logs:/var/log/soulpilates-api
    depends_on:
      mongo:
        condition: service_started
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      rustfs-bucket-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]

  frontend:
    image: studionexis/frontend:latest
    container_name: studionexis-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3720:80"
    networks: [public]

networks:
  internal:
    driver: bridge
  public:
    driver: bridge

Caps are live — the fork now has hard ceilings (backend 640 MB, mongo 768 MB, etc.) and is sitting way under them (~320 MB total). The live studio is completely untouched. It **cannot** starve the live system now, even if a test goes wrong.

Now the foundational decision that shapes the entire restructure: **the tenancy model** — how each studio's data is isolated. This is the fork in the road; everything else (routing, provisioning, billing, backups) hangs off it.

One thing strongly in your favor: your app **already reads the database name from config** (`MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName`), which makes one of these options far cheaper to build than the others.

questions.question: Which tenancy model should the SaaS use to isolate each studio's data?

options.label: Database-per-tenant (Recommended)
options.description: Each studio gets its own Mongo database on the shared cluster. Strong isolation (a query bug can't leak across studios), trivial per-studio backup/export/delete, and LEAST invasive here — the app already picks DB by config, so it's mostly a 'resolve tenant → pick DB' middleware. Cross-studio reporting is harder; not for tens-of-thousands of tenants (fine for studios).

options.label: Shared DB + TenantId column
options.description: One database, every record tagged with a TenantId, every query filtered by it. Cheapest per tenant and best for huge scale, BUT isolation is only as good as your query discipline (one missed filter = a data breach between businesses), and it's a big invasive change — stamping + filtering ~40 collections.

options.label: Full silo per tenant
options.description: Each studio gets its own complete container stack + DB (like this fork). Maximum isolation, but heavy ops/cost per studio — only worth it for a few high-value enterprise clients, not a scalable SaaS.

Now I can see the whole shape of the restructure. The key finding: **`MongoDbContext` is a singleton bound to one database, and all ~40 services just call `GetCollection<T>(...)` through it.** That's actually great news — if I make that context *tenant-aware* while keeping its API identical, the ~40 services need **zero changes**. That's the heart of the plan.

## The database-per-tenant architecture

```
Request → [Tenant Resolution] → picks tenant "studio-a" → MongoDbContext binds to DB "tenant_studio-a"
                                                            ↓
Control plane DB "studionexis_control"  ← Tenant registry (slug, DB name, plan, status)
Tenant DBs: tenant_studio-a, tenant_studio-b, …  ← each studio's isolated data
```

## Phased roadmap

| Phase | What | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Tenant foundation** | Control-plane `Tenant` registry + `TenantContext` + make `MongoDbContext` resolve the current tenant's DB (services unchanged) + resolution middleware | Core plumbing |
| **2. Provisioning & super-admin** | Create/suspend/delete a tenant → spins up its DB + seeds its admin; a super-admin plane above the studios | Medium |
| **3. Auth & routing** | JWT carries tenant; subdomain-per-studio routing (`studio-a.studionexis…`) + wildcard cert | Medium |
| **4. Background jobs** | Birthday/VIP/reminder jobs must loop over *all* tenants, not one DB | Careful |
| **5. Billing & licensing** | Plans, subscription state, license enforcement | New surface |
| **6. Onboarding UX** | Studio signup → provisioned instance | Product polish |

**Phase 1 is done and verified** — the hardest architectural piece is in place, and it's non-breaking.

## What now exists (database-per-tenant foundation)
- **`Tenant`** control-plane entity + **`ControlPlaneContext`** (registry lives in a separate `studionexis_control` DB)
- **`ITenantContext`** (scoped) — holds the resolved tenant's DB for the request
- **`ITenantRegistry` / `TenantRegistry`** — resolves subdomain slug → tenant, cached
- **`TenantResolutionMiddleware`** — `studio-a.studionexis…` → binds the request to `tenant_studio-a`; unknown slug → 404; bare domain → default DB
- **`MongoDbContext` is now tenant-aware and scoped** — and crucially, **its API is unchanged, so all ~40 services need zero modification**. One shared Mongo connection pool (singleton); only the DB selection is per-request.

## Verified
✅ Compiles ✅ Boots cleanly (no DI/scope errors) ✅ Still serves the fork on the default DB (no tenant subdomain yet) ✅ Live studio untouched, fork within its resource caps.

So a request to a tenant subdomain will now transparently read/write that tenant's isolated database — the core of the whole SaaS model.

## Next up — Phase 2: provisioning & super-admin
- A **super-admin plane** (above the studios) to create/list/suspend tenants
- **Provisioning**: create tenant → create its DB → seed its admin/settings/notification rules
- Then Phase 3 (JWT carries tenant + wildcard subdomain routing & cert), Phase 4 (background jobs loop all tenants), Phase 5 (billing/licensing).

- **nginx:** `/etc/nginx/sites-available/studionexis` (enabled). Proxies /api/→8392, /studionexis-public/→6326, /→3720. LE cert via certbot --nginx (auto-renew), expires ~Oct 5 2026.

## Where we are
- ✅ **Phase 1** — database-per-tenant foundation (services unchanged)

- ✅ **Phase 3** — wildcard subdomain routing + TLS (end-to-end proven)

## Remaining phases
- **Phase 4** — background jobs (birthday/VIP/reminder emails) loop over *all* tenants instead of one DB
- **Phase 5** — billing & licensing (plans, subscription state, enforcement)
- **Phase 6** — self-serve signup so a studio can provision itself from the landing page's "Start free trial"

## One thing I flagged in memory to tighten later
Right now tenant auth is resolved purely by subdomain (the DB binding). Before you take real customers, we should also **stamp the tenant into the JWT** so a token issued for one studio is cryptographically scoped to it — a defense-in-depth layer. I'd fold that into Phase 3.5 or alongside Phase 5.

Want to keep going — **Phase 6 (self-serve signup)** would make the "Start free trial" button actually create a studio, which is the most demo-able next step — or pick another phase?

**Studio Nexis** is a fully isolated fork of the Soul Pilates codebase (created 2026-07-07) so the user can make changes without touching the live studio. Live at **https://studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn**. Related: [[project_soul_pilates]], [[soul-pilates-deploy]].

- **Location:** `/opt/studionexis` (separate from `/opt/soulpilates`).
- **Compose:** `docker-compose.prod.yml` (top-level `name: studionexis`). Containers `studionexis-*`. GlitchTip dropped.
- **Ports (host):** backend 8392, frontend 3720, mongo 27118, redis 6480, rustfs 6326/6327 (all vs soulpilates 8391/3719/27117/6479/6324/6325).
- **DB:** database name `studionexis` (fresh/empty). Media bucket `studionexis-public`.
- **Images:** `studionexis/backend:latest`, `studionexis/frontend:latest` (frontend built with `PUBLIC_API_URL=https://studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn`).
- **Env:** `/opt/studionexis/prod.env` — own secrets (generated via `generate-secrets.sh`). ALL integrations OFF (Stripe/Meta/SMTP/WebPush = false, blank keys).
- **Admin seed:** admin@studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn (password in prod.env `ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD`).
- **nginx:** `/etc/nginx/sites-available/studionexis` (enabled). Proxies /api/→8392, /studionexis-public/→6326, /→3720. LE cert via certbot --nginx (auto-renew), expires ~Oct 5 2026.
- **DNS:** studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn → 72.62.240.50 (DNS-only / grey cloud, needed for HTTP-01).

**Redeploy:** build with studionexis tags then `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d` (see [[soul-pilates-deploy]] for the analogous live flow). Do NOT confuse with the live soulpilates stack.

**Resource caps (2026-07-07):** studionexis compose has mem_limit/cpus on every service (backend 640m, mongo 768m, redis 128m, rustfs 256m, frontend 96m) so the fork can't starve the live studio while co-located.

**SaaS restructure IN PROGRESS (started 2026-07-07).** Turning studionexis into a multi-tenant SaaS licensed to studios. Decision: **database-per-tenant** (each studio = its own Mongo DB `tenant_<slug>`; control-plane DB `studionexis_control` holds the Tenant registry). Plan is to build ON this box then MIGRATE to a dedicated server before going public (build ≠ launch here). Phased: 1 tenant foundation ✅, 2 provisioning+super-admin, 3 JWT-tenant+wildcard subdomain routing/cert, 4 background jobs loop all tenants, 5 billing/licensing, 6 onboarding UX.

**Phase 2 DONE (verified end-to-end):** `ITenantProvisioningService`/`TenantProvisioningService` (Services) — `CreateTenantAsync` validates slug (regex + reserved list), inserts Tenant into control DB, opens a scope, `ITenantContext.SetDatabase(tenant_<slug>)` BEFORE resolving MongoDbContext, seeds the tenant DB with an admin `User` (PasswordHasher.Hash), rolls back control record on seed failure; also ListTenantsAsync + SetStatusAsync (suspend/activate). `SaasController` (`/api/saas/tenants` POST/GET + `/{slug}/status` PATCH) — `[Authorize(Roles=Admin)]` + control-plane-only guard (`ITenantContext.IsResolved==false`, so tenant admins can't manage tenants; the DEFAULT-DB apex admin is the super-admin — no new secret). Smoke-tested: super-admin login → provisioned "demo-studio" → verified 3 separate DBs (studionexis / studionexis_control / tenant_demo-studio) with the tenant admin ONLY in the tenant DB. (A test `demo-studio` tenant exists; not reachable until Phase 3 subdomain routing.)

**Phase 3 DONE (2026-07-07, verified end-to-end):** wildcard subdomain routing + TLS. Wildcard DNS `*.studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn → 72.62.240.50` (user added). Wildcard cert via certbot DNS-01 (Cloudflare, `/root/.secrets/cloudflare.ini`) at `/etc/letsencrypt/live/studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn-0001/` (CN `*.studionexis…`, auto-renew). Wildcard tenant vhost `/etc/nginx/sites-available/studionexis-tenants` (server_name `*.studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn`) serves the FULL studio app (booking NOT hidden) → proxies /api/→8392, /studionexis-public/→6326, /→3720; nginx prefers the exact apex vhost over the wildcard. PROVEN: demo-studio.studionexis…/booking/ = 200; login as admin@demo-studio.com SUCCEEDS on its subdomain (200, tenant DB) but FAILS on apex (401, default DB) — same creds, different DB = routing-based tenant isolation works. Tenant auth resolution is via subdomain host (no JWT tenant claim yet — a token is currently accepted on any host that resolves the same tenant DB; tighten in a later pass). Remaining: Phase 4 background jobs per-tenant, Phase 5 billing/licensing, Phase 6 self-serve signup/onboarding.

**Apex hides the studio app (2026-07-07):** the booking system + customer app is per-tenant, NOT for the Studio Nexis marketing site. The apex nginx vhost (`/etc/nginx/sites-available/studionexis`) has a regex `location ~ ^/(booking|packages|checkout|account|my-bookings|my-package|onboarding|register|verify-email|reset-password|forgot-password)(/|$) { return 302 /; }` so those routes redirect to the landing page on the apex. Live at apex. The studio app pages (booking/admin/login) remain for tenants.

content.text:
**Phase 5 works — full license lifecycle enforced.** Verified live:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Fresh studio | 14-day trial, `licenseValid: true` |
| **Expire the trial** (super-admin) | `licenseValid: false` |
| App API (`/api/booking/schedule`) | **402 — blocked** ✅ |
| Login (`/api/auth/login`) | **200 — still open** (so the owner can reach billing) ✅ |
| **Reactivate on STUDIO plan** | `licenseValid: true`, trial cleared ✅ |
| App API again | **200 — restored** ✅ |

So a studio's access is now gated by its subscription: trials expire and lock the app (but never lock the owner out of login), and the super-admin can suspend, extend a trial, or move a studio onto a paid plan — all via `/api/saas/tenants/{slug}/subscription`.

## Honest scope note
This is the **licensing state machine + enforcement** — the part that decides *who can use the product*. What it does **not** yet include is **actual payment collection**: wiring Stripe subscriptions + webhooks so paying flips `SubscriptionStatus` to `ACTIVE` automatically, and a frontend **"renew / subscribe"** page that shows when a studio hits the 402. Those are the remaining billing pieces.

content.text:
Recorded. Studio Nexis now has a real licensing spine: studios get a 14-day trial, expiry locks the app (not login), and the super-admin controls plans/subscriptions.

## Full build status
- ✅ Phase 1 — tenant foundation (DB-per-tenant)
- ✅ Phase 2 — provisioning + super-admin
- ✅ Phase 3 — wildcard routing + TLS
- ✅ Phase 5 — **licensing & enforcement**
- ✅ Phase 6 — self-serve signup
- ✅ Premium site redesign · booking hidden on apex
- Live Soul Pilates untouched; fork within caps

## What's left for a real launch
1. **Payment collection** — Stripe subscriptions + webhooks to auto-flip `SubscriptionStatus`, and a frontend **"renew/subscribe"** page for the 402 state (completes Phase 5)
2. **Phase 4** — background jobs (emails/reminders) loop over all tenant DBs, not just the default
3. **Signup hardening** — email verification + captcha before public
4. **JWT tenant claim** — cryptographically scope tokens to their tenant
5. **Migrate to a dedicated server** before onboarding real paying studios

My recommendation for the next push: **Phase 4 (per-tenant background jobs)** — right now automated emails/reminders only run against the default DB, so tenant studios silently get none, which is a correctness gap. Want me to keep going with that, or tackle the Stripe payment collection to finish billing?

content.text:
Full wizard lifecycle verified: fresh studio → `setupCompleted: false` → completes → `true`. Here's the complete flow now:

## Fixed: owner onboarding
1. **Signup success** → "Go to my studio" now points to **`/admin/login`** (the admin portal), not the client booking login.
2. **On admin login**, `AdminLayout` checks the studio's settings — if setup isn't complete, it **redirects to `/admin/setup`**, so the **first thing a new owner sees is the setup wizard**.
3. **The wizard** (on-brand, 3 steps): Welcome → a get-started checklist (add your team, create class types, studio settings & schedule — each linking into the admin) → Finish → marks setup complete → lands on the dashboard.
4. **Afterward**, `setupCompleted: true` → straight to the dashboard, wizard never reappears. ("Skip for now" also marks it done so it won't nag.)

Backend: added `GlobalSettings.SetupCompleted` + a lightweight `POST /api/settings/complete-setup` (avoids the heavy full-settings validation), and surfaced the flag in the settings GET.

input.command:
source /tmp/nexis-migrate-vars
cat > "$STAGE/MIGRATION-RUNBOOK.md" <<'EOF'
# Studio Nexis — migration to a new server

This bundle is a complete, self-contained copy of the Studio Nexis SaaS.
It contains ZERO from the live Soul Pilates system. Restoring it does not touch
the old server; when you're ready you just repoint DNS and shut the old fork down.

## Contents
- source/           full app source + docker-compose.prod.yml + prod.env (REAL secrets) + generate-secrets.sh
- mongodump/dump/   all databases: studionexis (default), studionexis_control (tenant registry), tenant_* (each studio)
- media/            object-storage (rustfs) media
- nginx/            the apex + wildcard-tenant vhosts

Secrets are reused as-is so existing tenant logins/JWTs keep working. Keep this bundle private.

## On the NEW server
Prereqs: Docker + docker compose, nginx, certbot + python3-certbot-dns-cloudflare.

1) Put the project in place:
     mkdir -p /opt/studionexis && cp -a source/. /opt/studionexis/
     cd /opt/studionexis

2) Build images (or copy them over with `docker save`/`docker load`):
     docker build -q -t studionexis/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .
     docker build -q --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn \
       -t studionexis/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro

3) Start the stack (creates empty DBs):
     docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d

4) Restore the databases:
     docker cp ../mongodump/dump studionexis-mongo:/tmp/dump
     PW=$(grep '^MONGO_PASSWORD=' prod.env | cut -d= -f2)
     docker exec studionexis-mongo mongorestore -u admin -p "$PW" --authenticationDatabase admin --drop /tmp/dump

5) Restore media:
     cp -a ../media/. /opt/studionexis/data/rustfs/
     docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env restart rustfs

6) nginx: copy nginx/studionexis.conf and nginx/studionexis-tenants.conf into
   /etc/nginx/sites-available/, symlink into sites-enabled/, then `nginx -t`.
   (Fix cert paths after step 7.)

7) TLS certs on the NEW box:
     certbot --nginx -d studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn
     certbot certonly --dns-cloudflare --dns-cloudflare-credentials /root/.secrets/cloudflare.ini \
       -d "*.studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn" --dns-cloudflare-propagation-seconds 30
   Point the wildcard vhost's ssl_certificate at the new *.studionexis live path, then reload nginx.

## Cut-over (DNS)
- In Cloudflare, repoint BOTH records to the NEW server IP (DNS-only / grey cloud):
    studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn   A  <NEW_IP>
    *.studionexis.soulpilates.com.vn A  <NEW_IP>
- After it resolves + HTTPS works on the new box, on the OLD server stop ONLY the fork:
    cd /opt/studionexis && docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
    rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/studionexis /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/studionexis-tenants && systemctl reload nginx
  DO NOT touch /opt/soulpilates or any soulpilates-prod-* container — that's the live studio.
EOF

ZIP="/root/studionexis-MIGRATION-$TS.zip"
cd "$STAGE" && zip -rq "$ZIP" . && echo "=== $ZIP ===" && ls -lh "$ZIP"
unzip -tq "$ZIP" >/dev/null && echo "integrity OK"
rm -rf "$STAGE"

# Studio Nexis — ISOLATED fork of the Soul Pilates stack.
# Fully separate from the live project: own containers, ports, data dirs,
# database ("studionexis"), media bucket, and network. GlitchTip omitted.
#
#   cd /opt/studionexis
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d
name: studionexis

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: studionexis-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Resource ceilings so this fork can NEVER starve the live studio on the
    # shared host while it's still co-located during the build phase.
    mem_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27118}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: studionexis-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 128m
    cpus: 0.5
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6480}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 256m
    cpus: 0.5
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6326:9000"
      - "127.0.0.1:6327:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 10s

  rustfs-bucket-init:
    image: minio/mc:latest
    container_name: studionexis-rustfs-bucket-init
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 $$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY $$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY &&
        mc mb --ignore-existing rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        mc anonymous set download rustfs/studionexis-public &&
        echo 'Bucket studionexis-public ready.'
      "
    depends_on:
      rustfs:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [internal]

      MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName: studionexis
      JwtSettings__Secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
      JwtSettings__PreviousSecret: ${JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET:-}
      StorageSettings__Endpoint: "http://rustfs:9000"
      StorageSettings__AccessKey: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      StorageSettings__SecretKey: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      StorageSettings__PublicBucket: studionexis-public
      StorageSettings__PublicUrlBase: ${PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL_BASE}
      StorageSettings__ForcePathStyle: "true"
      # ── Integrations DISABLED for the fork (clean slate) ──
      StripeSettings__SecretKey: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__PublishableKey: ${STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY:-}
      StripeSettings__WebhookSecret: ${STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET:-}
      StripeSettings__Enabled: ${STRIPE_ENABLED:-false}

      SmtpSettings__Port: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}

content.text:
Deployed to the live studio. Here's the definitive answer:

## It's not a deduction bug — it's a display bug (now fixed)

**The credits were always deducting correctly.** I verified the backend: the credit-settlement deducts `seats = Quantity` credits (one per person), which is exactly why yesterday's 2-person booking correctly showed **−2** in the ledger. Julez's next-day 2-person class **will deduct 2 credits** when you check her in — the system reads the booking's seat count, not the label.

**What was wrong:** the checkout modal **hard-coded the text "1 credit"** no matter how many people the booking was for. So it *said* 1 but would have *deducted* 2 — misleading, understandably alarming, but the actual charge was right.

## What I fixed (live now)
1. The checkout now shows the **real number**: for Julez it reads **"Class — package credit (2 people) · 2 credits"**.
2. Bonus fix from the same screen: the **"Note / reason (required)"** hint no longer appears when paying by **credit** — it only applies to custom cash amounts, so it was confusing there.

**Hard-refresh the calendar** (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) and reopen Julez's checkout — you'll now see "2 credits," and checking her in will correctly deduct 2 from her Group package (leaving 4).

Peace of mind: I also confirmed there's no other credit path that under-deducts — walk-in credit checkouts are always single-seat, and the multi-seat "add student" → credit checkout correctly deducts per seat.

content.text:
Deployed to the live studio. Here's the new option:

## "Attending" control in checkout
When you open the checkout for a **multi-seat booking**, there's now an **Attending: [ N ] of 3** field (defaults to the full booked count). For your situation — 3 booked, 2 showed — just **set it to 2**, and everything adjusts automatically:

- **Drop-in charge** → 2 × the price (not 3)
- **Package credits** → deducts **2 credits** (not 3)
- On check-in, the **booking shrinks to 2** and the **no-show seat is released** back to the class (so capacity and records are accurate)

It works for any combination — 2 of 3, 1 of 3, etc. — and for both cash/card and package-credit checkouts.

## Also fixed along the way
The "Note / reason (required)" prompt no longer falsely appears on normal multi-seat bookings — it now only shows for a genuinely custom (non-standard) amount.

**To use it:** hard-refresh the calendar (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R), open the 3-person booking's checkout, set **Attending to 2**, and check them in — 2 people charged, 2 credits (or 2× drop-in), and the third seat freed.

Since these folks are **new to the studio**, one thing to confirm: they were booked as a single 3-seat booking under one name, right? If instead each newcomer needs their **own** client record (for their own future history/packages), the **"Split into separate people"** button is the better tool — it makes each a separate attendee you check in individually. content.text:
Deployed to the live studio. There's now a **client quick-search** in the top bar (right side).

## What it does
- Type a name, phone, or email (2+ characters) → a dropdown shows **up to 4 matching clients**, each with:
  - **Avatar + name**
  - **Phone · email** (sub-line)
  - **🎟 available credits** (e.g. `6 Grp · 2 Pvt`) — only shown if they have any
- **Click a result** → jumps to that client's profile
- If there are more than 4 matches → **"View all N results →"** at the bottom, which opens the full Clients page **pre-filtered** to your search
- Closes on outside-click or Escape; searches are debounced so it's snappy

It reuses your existing client search API (which already returns name, phone, email, and per-format credits), so it's a single fast request per keystroke — no extra backend load.

**Hard-refresh** any admin page (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) and you'll see the search box next to the date/profile in the top bar.

One note: the search respects your existing access control — anyone whose role can view clients will get results; a staff role without client access simply won't see results (the box stays empty), which is the correct behavior. Want me to also make the results **keyboard-navigable** (arrow keys + Enter), or is click/tap enough for your front desk?

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs
```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata
```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout
```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
```

```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:

        tables = page.extract_tables()
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction
```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
```

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
```

########## project_soul_pilates.md ##########
---
name: project-soul-pilates
description: "Soul Pilates CRM system at /opt/soulpilates — architecture, tech stack, and domain overview"

Soul Pilates is a production CRM for a pilates studio, located at /opt/soulpilates.

**Why:** Full studio management — bookings, payroll, packages, payments, analytics.

**How to apply:** When working on this project, understand the Clean Architecture layering and that business logic lives exclusively in SoulPilates.Services/.

## Tech Stack
- Backend: .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core), C#
- Frontend: Astro 6 (TypeScript, Bootstrap 5, jQuery)
- Database: MongoDB 8
- Cache: Redis 7
- Object Storage: RustFS (S3-compatible)
- Payments: Stripe
- Email: SMTP (Hetzner srv1182755.hstgr.cloud:587)
- Push Notifications: VAPID web push
- Error Tracking: GlitchTip (self-hosted Sentry)
- Logging: Serilog (structured JSON)

## Project Structure
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/` — Controllers, middleware, DI, entry point (Program.cs)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/` — Entities, interfaces, DTOs (no business logic)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/` — All business logic
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Infrastructure/` — MongoDB data access (MongoDbContext.cs)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Migration/` — Data migration utilities
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Tests/` — xUnit test suite (20+ test projects)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/` — Astro frontend SPA
- `/opt/soulpilates/docker-compose.yml` — Local dev stack
- `/opt/soulpilates/docker-compose.prod.yml` — Production stack
- `/opt/soulpilates/prod.env.sample` — All production secrets template
- `/opt/soulpilates/deploy/RUNBOOK.md` — Deployment procedure

## Domain Areas
- **Scheduling:** ClassBlueprint → CalendarSession materialization (background service)
- **Bookings & Waitlist:** Attendance records, waitlist auto-promotion
- **Packages & Wallet:** Credit-based system with expiry (ClientPackage)
- **Payroll:** Complex tiered commission (PayrollService.cs)
- **Payments:** Stripe intents + idempotent webhook (StripeProcessedEvent dedup)
- **Accounting:** P&L, expenses, fund pools, owner loans/distributions
- **Analytics:** KPIs, retention cohorts, revenue breakdowns
- **RBAC:** 7 roles — SuperAdmin, Owner, Manager, Instructor, Receptionist, Customer, Freelance
- **Audit Logging:** All CRUD actions tracked with actor, IP, timestamp

## Key Service Files
- `SoulPilates.Services/PayrollService.cs` — Commission calculations
- `SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs` — Class materialization
- `SoulPilates.Services/WaitlistService.cs` — Overflow management
- `SoulPilates.Services/PaymentService.cs` — Stripe integration
- `SoulPilates.Services/AnalyticsService.cs` — Business intelligence
- `SoulPilates.Services/AuthService.cs` — JWT auth

## Running Locally
```bash
docker compose up -d                    # MongoDB :27117, Redis :6479, RustFS :7283
dotnet run --project SoulPilates.API   # API at :5000/:5001
cd SoulPilates.Astro && npm run dev    # Frontend at :4321
```

## API
- 35+ controllers at /api/*
- JWT Bearer auth (2hr TTL, key rotation support)
- Rate limiting on auth endpoints
- Swagger at /swagger (dev only)

## Background Jobs (12+)
PackageExpiryBackgroundService, BookingReminderBackgroundService, RetentionReminderBackgroundService, ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService, ReservationCleanupBackgroundService, PushDispatcherService, SessionCompletionBackgroundService, and more.

## Production Deployment
- VestaCP reverse proxy (TLS termination)
- `/` → Frontend :80, `/api/*` → Backend :8080, `/soulpilates-public/*` → RustFS :9000
- All services bind 127.0.0.1
- Backups encrypted with age, stored in Backblaze B2

########## soul-pilates-deploy.md ##########
---
name: soul-pilates-deploy
description: How to build + deploy Soul Pilates prod images directly on the VPS
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f1b1af7e-43da-44b8-92b2-51e4d240617b

Soul Pilates prod ([[project-soul-pilates]]) uses **prebuilt images** (`soulpilates/backend:latest`, `soulpilates/frontend:latest`) referenced in `docker-compose.prod.yml` with **no `build:` context** — so `docker compose build` does nothing. `build-images.bat` is Windows-only (has a MuscleMapJS junction dance), but the images build fine **directly on the Linux VPS** because `SoulPilates.Astro/src/lib/MuscleMapJS` is a real directory there, not a junction.

Deploy from `/opt/soulpilates`:
```bash
# Backend (context = repo root)
docker build -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .
# Frontend (context = SoulPilates.Astro, API URL baked in at build time)
docker build --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://new.soulpilates.com.vn \
  -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro
# Recreate the two app containers (also re-reads prod.env)
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend
```
Backend binds `:8080`; smoke test via `https://new.soulpilates.com.vn/api/settings` → expect **401** (up + routing). Frontend `/` → 200. No local `dotnet`/`npm` — everything builds inside Docker.

- **DB:** database name `studionexis` (fresh/empty). Media bucket `studionexis-public`.

New test-ground bundle `/root/nexis-revsports-20260707-2002.zip` for domain **nexis.revsports.ca** (prod.env PUBLIC_* + SAAS_BASE_DOMAIN set to nexis.revsports.ca, same secrets, all DBs, migrate-setup.sh DOMAIN=nexis.revsports.ca). User uploads this to their VPS + pastes a handoff prompt into a new Claude chat on that box. Wildcard cert needs revsports.ca DNS provider's API (Cloudflare token if applicable).

**Migration bundle (2026-07-07):** `/root/studionexis-MIGRATION-20260707-1949.zip` (5.6M) = full source + docker-compose + prod.env(real secrets) + mongodump of ALL DBs (studionexis, studionexis_control, all tenant_*) + media + both nginx vhosts + MIGRATION-RUNBOOK.md + `migrate-setup.sh` (one-shot: installs docker/nginx/certbot, copies to /opt/studionexis, builds images, up -d, mongorestore --drop, restores media, writes HTTP-first nginx vhosts). User has a target VPS w/ SSH; runs the script there, then does DNS (point studionexis + *.studionexis at new IP, DNS-only) + certbot (apex --nginx + wildcard DNS-01) + adds wildcard SSL to tenant vhost. Cut-over = verify new box then `docker compose down` the fork on THIS box (never touch soulpilates-prod-*/opt/soulpilates). Secrets reused so tenant logins survive. This env can't SSH to the new server — user executes, I troubleshoot from output.

**Resource caps (2026-07-07):** studionexis compose has mem_limit/cpus on every service (backend 640m, mongo 768m, redis 128m, rustfs 256m, frontend 96m) so the fork can't starve the live studio while co-located.

**SaaS restructure IN PROGRESS (started 2026-07-07).** Turning studionexis into a multi-tenant SaaS licensed to studios. Decision: **database-per-tenant** (each studio = its own Mongo DB `tenant_<slug>`; control-plane DB `studionexis_control` holds the Tenant registry). Plan is to build ON this box then MIGRATE to a dedicated server before going public (build ≠ launch here). Phased: 1 tenant foundation ✅, 2 provisioning+super-admin, 3 JWT-tenant+wildcard subdomain routing/cert, 4 background jobs loop all tenants, 5 billing/licensing, 6 onboarding UX.

**Phase 2 DONE (verified end-to-end):** `ITenantProvisioningService`/`TenantProvisioningService` (Services) — `CreateTenantAsync` validates slug (regex + reserved list), inserts Tenant into control DB, opens a scope, `ITenantContext.SetDatabase(tenant_<slug>)` BEFORE resolving MongoDbContext, seeds the tenant DB with an admin `User` (PasswordHasher.Hash), rolls back control record on seed failure; also ListTenantsAsync + SetStatusAsync (suspend/activate). `SaasController` (`/api/saas/tenants` POST/GET + `/{slug}/status` PATCH) — `[Authorize(Roles=Admin)]` + control-plane-only guard (`ITenantContext.IsResolved==false`, so tenant admins can't manage tenants; the DEFAULT-DB apex admin is the super-admin — no new secret). For instructor **% commission** on a class booking, the commission base depends on how the client paid:
- **Package-credit redemption** → base = the **per-class rate within the package** = (package sale price ÷ credits). Stored on `ClientPackage.FractionalValuePerClass`. NOT the full drop-in rate.
- **Regular drop-in** (client paid the full drop-in price) → base = the drop-in rate.

**Why:** a client on a 10 Group pack (₫4,250,000/10 = ₫425,000/class) did NOT pay the ₫500,000 drop-in rate, so commissioning on drop-in overpays instructors. The user has emphasized this repeatedly.

Per-class value MUST be the **actual amount the package sold for** (net of discounts), NOT the product list price — the user was explicit: some packages are discounted and list price would overpay commission.

**How to apply:** the base resolver is `PayrollService.ResolveAttendeeRevenueAsync` (2026-07-05: loads the `ClientPackage` via `Attendance.PackageInstanceId` and returns `FractionalValuePerClass × qty` for `PACKAGE_CREDIT`; falls back to `session.DropInPrice` only when the per-class value is unknown/0). Package creation sets `FractionalValuePerClass = line.LineTotal ÷ units ÷ credits` — the **actual net** — in `InvoiceService.ProvisionPackagesFromInvoiceAsync` (line ~534), so upcoming purchases are correct including discounts. WalletService comp-grants set 0. On 2026-07-05 backfilled 95 legacy packages by matching each to its **actual purchase invoice line** (same client + parsed "<credits> <Group|Private> Class Pack" description + nearest date), net÷credits — script at scratchpad `backfill-actual-perclass.js`. See [[project_soul_pilates]].

**Related rule (2026-07-05):** a class only counts toward an instructor's class total / tier count if ≥1 attendee actually CHECKED_IN/ARRIVED — empty, all-no-show, or booking-only classes don't count. `PayrollService` already skipped empty classes (arrivedAttendances==0 → continue); `SchedulingService` monthClassCount was fixed to drop `BOOKED` from the counting query. Two commission code paths exist and BOTH must carry these rules: `PayrollService.ResolveAttendeeRevenueAsync` (payroll + instructor earnings) and `SchedulingService` per-class commission snapshot (schedule Financials tab).

**Related rule (2026-07-07): "VAT (online only)" fee is NOT commissionable.** The online surcharge is a pass-through, stored separately as `Invoice.OnlineFeeAmount` (never inside an invoice line). Commission base must exclude it. Fixed in BOTH paths: revenue-split monthly base sums `TotalNet − OnlineFeeAmount`; per-class resolvers strip the attendee's apportioned fee share from the whole-invoice `TotalNet` fallback and the `att.AmountPaid` fallback (the per-line total was already fee-free, so line-matched bookings were already correct — the leak was only the fallbacks). Recomputed from source each run → applies going forward; finalized PayrollRun snapshots don't change retroactively.

**Open edge cases (flagged to user, undecided):** comp grants have `FractionalValuePerClass=0` → currently fall back to drop-in; 8 packages (non-standard credit counts GROUP 7/11/4/2/0, PRIVATE 4/2, + 1 PRIVATE/5 with no findable purchase) stayed 0 → also fall back to drop-in.

Soul Pilates is a production CRM for a pilates studio, located at /opt/soulpilates.

- Backend: .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core), C#
- Frontend: Astro 6 (TypeScript, Bootstrap 5, jQuery)
- Database: MongoDB 8
- Cache: Redis 7
- Object Storage: RustFS (S3-compatible)
- Payments: Stripe
- Email: SMTP (Hetzner srv1182755.hstgr.cloud:587)
- Push Notifications: VAPID web push
- Error Tracking: GlitchTip (self-hosted Sentry)
- Logging: Serilog (structured JSON)

## Project Structure
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/` — Controllers, middleware, DI, entry point (Program.cs)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/` — Entities, interfaces, DTOs (no business logic)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/` — All business logic
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Infrastructure/` — MongoDB data access (MongoDbContext.cs)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Migration/` — Data migration utilities
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Tests/` — xUnit test suite (20+ test projects)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/` — Astro frontend SPA
- `/opt/soulpilates/docker-compose.yml` — Local dev stack
- `/opt/soulpilates/docker-compose.prod.yml` — Production stack
- `/opt/soulpilates/prod.env.sample` — All production secrets template
- `/opt/soulpilates/deploy/RUNBOOK.md` — Deployment procedure

## Domain Areas
- **Scheduling:** ClassBlueprint → CalendarSession materialization (background service)
- **Bookings & Waitlist:** Attendance records, waitlist auto-promotion
- **Packages & Wallet:** Credit-based system with expiry (ClientPackage)
- **Payroll:** Complex tiered commission (PayrollService.cs)
- **Payments:** Stripe intents + idempotent webhook (StripeProcessedEvent dedup)
- **Accounting:** P&L, expenses, fund pools, owner loans/distributions
- **Analytics:** KPIs, retention cohorts, revenue breakdowns
- **RBAC:** 7 roles — SuperAdmin, Owner, Manager, Instructor, Receptionist, Customer, Freelance
- **Audit Logging:** All CRUD actions tracked with actor, IP, timestamp
