- `SoulPilates.Services/PayrollService.cs` — Commission calculations
- `SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs` — Class materialization
- `SoulPilates.Services/WaitlistService.cs` — Overflow management
- `SoulPilates.Services/PaymentService.cs` — Stripe integration
- `SoulPilates.Services/AnalyticsService.cs` — Business intelligence
- `SoulPilates.Services/AuthService.cs` — JWT auth

```bash
docker compose up -d                    # MongoDB :27117, Redis :6479, RustFS :7283

```

- 35+ controllers at /api/*

- Rate limiting on auth endpoints

PackageExpiryBackgroundService, BookingReminderBackgroundService, RetentionReminderBackgroundService, ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService, ReservationCleanupBackgroundService, PushDispatcherService, SessionCompletionBackgroundService, and more.

Soul Pilates prod ([[project-soul-pilates]]) uses **prebuilt images** (`soulpilates/backend:latest`, `soulpilates/frontend:latest`) referenced in `docker-compose.prod.yml` with **no `build:` context** — so `docker compose build` does nothing. `build-images.bat` is Windows-only (has a MuscleMapJS junction dance), but the images build fine **directly on the Linux VPS** because `SoulPilates.Astro/src/lib/MuscleMapJS` is a real directory there, not a junction.

Deploy from `/opt/soulpilates`:
```bash
# Backend (context = repo root)
docker build -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .
# Frontend (context = SoulPilates.Astro, API URL baked in at build time)
docker build --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://new.soulpilates.com.vn \
  -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro
# Recreate the two app containers (also re-reads prod.env)
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend
```
Backend binds `:8080`; smoke test via `https://new.soulpilates.com.vn/api/settings` → expect **401** (up + routing). Frontend `/` → 200. No local `dotnet`/`npm` — everything builds inside Docker.

Section 01

System Overview & Architecture

Soul Pilates is a production-grade, all-in-one management platform for a boutique pilates & yoga studio — everything from online booking to payroll runs in one connected system.

The platform replaces the usual patchwork of a booking app, a spreadsheet, a POS terminal and a payroll tool. Because every module shares one database, data flows automatically: a class booked deducts a credit in real time; a class completed feeds instructor commission; a payment taken updates revenue, the client's history and the P&L at once.

Clean Architecture

The backend follows a strict layered (Clean Architecture) design. Business rules live in exactly one place, which keeps the system predictable and testable.

LayerResponsibility
SoulPilates.APIHTTP controllers, middleware, authentication, dependency injection, the app entry point.
SoulPilates.CoreEntities, DTOs and interfaces only — no business logic. The shared contract.
SoulPilates.ServicesAll business logic — scheduling, payroll, payments, analytics, accounting.
SoulPilates.InfrastructureMongoDB data access (the MongoDbContext).
SoulPilates.Migration / .TestsData-migration utilities and an xUnit test suite.
SoulPilates.AstroThe web front end (admin portal, instructor portal, customer booking site).
At a glance 40+ API controllers · 69 data entities · 12+ background jobs · 7 user roles · one MongoDB database. Three front-end surfaces: the admin portal, the instructor portal, and the customer-facing booking site.
Section 02

Technology Stack

Backend

.NET 10 (ASP.NET Core), C#. JWT bearer auth with 2-hour tokens and key-rotation support. Rate limiting on auth endpoints. Serilog structured JSON logging.

Frontend

Astro 6 (TypeScript), Bootstrap 5, jQuery. Installable PWA with offline-aware service worker and web-push support.

Data & Cache

MongoDB 8 (primary store), Redis 7 (cache / reservation locks), RustFS (S3-compatible object storage for images & media).

Platform Services

Stripe (payments), VAPID Web Push (notifications), SMTP via Brevo relay (email), GlitchTip (self-hosted error tracking).

The whole stack runs as Docker containers behind an nginx reverse proxy that terminates TLS and routes / to the frontend, /api/* to the backend, and /…-public/* to object storage.

Section 03

Data Model & Roles

The domain is expressed in 69 entities. The most important ones and how they relate:

EntityRole in the system
ClassBlueprintA recurring class template (name, format, instructor, price, capacity, schedule). Materialised into concrete sessions.
CalendarSessionA concrete class on the calendar — snapshots price, instructor, equipment from the blueprint at materialisation.
ClientA studio customer — contact details, medical notes, tags, lifetime value, visit history.
CustomerAccountA client's login for the customer booking site (separate from staff User accounts).
AttendanceA booking on a session — status, seat quantity, payment method, amount paid/due. The heart of the booking system.
ClientPackageA purchased class pack / membership — remaining credits, expiry, per-class value.
Invoice / PaymentFinancial records. Invoices carry lines; payments record money actually received.
Staff / UserInstructors and staff, their rates, commission model and login.
PayrollRunA finalised monthly payroll snapshot per instructor.
GlobalSettingsStudio-wide configuration — pricing rules, fund splits, cancellation windows, VIP tiers, integrations.
One subtlety worth knowing IDs are stored as MongoDB ObjectId but modelled as strings in C#. Sessions snapshot price/instructor/equipment from their blueprint at creation time — editing a blueprint doesn't change already-scheduled sessions unless the "update future sessions" sync is used.

Roles & Access Control (RBAC)

Seven roles, each with a scoped view. Access is enforced in two layers — the backend [Authorize] attributes and front-end role checks.

RoleWhat they can do
SuperAdmin / OwnerEverything — including finance, payroll, owner loans & distributions.
ManagerOperations and most admin, class blocking/management.
ReceptionistFront desk — manage classes, check-in, complete, block/unblock, POS checkout, collect payment, add students.
InstructorOwn schedule & earnings; from the PWA can check people in, view attendee contact/limited profile, and remove attendees from their own classes.
CustomerThe booking site — book classes, view packages/credits, manage their bookings.
FreelanceStudio-rental / freelance sessions kept separate from the public booking flow.
Section 04

Scheduling & the Calendar

Classes begin life as blueprints. A background materialiser turns each recurring blueprint into concrete CalendarSessions across a rolling horizon, so the calendar always shows the weeks ahead without anyone creating each class by hand.

  • Formats: Group, Mat (a group sub-type), Private and Duo — each with its own pricing and capacity behaviour.
  • Live calendar: week / day / month views, colour-coded by format, difficulty, equipment or instructor.
  • Session management: edit a session, mark completed, block/unblock a class or a whole time slot, override (reschedule / swap instructor / change capacity), and cancel.
  • "Jump to next available day" and capacity guards that atomically claim seats to prevent overbooking.
  • Once a class has started it disappears from the public booking site and can no longer be booked — enforced both in the listing query and at the booking action.
Live-refresh, done efficiently Rather than polling, the admin calendar refreshes only when something actually changes — the service worker broadcasts a signal on every booking push, and the open calendar refreshes in place (coalesced, and paused while the tab is hidden). Near-zero idle load, and faster than a timer.
Section 05

Bookings, Waitlist & Reservations

Every booking is an Attendance record. Bookings can be made by a customer online, or by staff at the desk. A single booking can cover multiple people ("book for N" — one attendance with a seat quantity).

Reserve
A checkout reservation atomically claims the seat(s) so two people can't grab the last spot. Abandoned reservations are auto-cleaned.
Confirm / pay
The reservation becomes a confirmed booking on payment or credit redemption.
Waitlist
Full classes take a waitlist; a freed seat auto-promotes the next person.
Check-in & complete
Staff check attendees in; completing the class finalises attendance and feeds commission.

Reschedules, cancellations and no-shows are all handled with policy-aware rules (cancellation windows differ by format and payment type), and a booking that was rescheduled away is locked so it can't be double-charged.

Section 06

Client CRM

Every client has a single searchable profile: contact details, medical/health notes, tags, referral source, membership tier, full booking & package history, and lifetime value — no spreadsheets.

  • Global quick-search in the top bar: type a name, phone or email and up to four ranked results appear instantly, each showing name, phone, email and available Group/Private/Mat credits. Results are ranked so recently-active clients surface first.
  • VIP & Super-VIP tiers computed from lifetime spend and checked-in class count, with automatic congratulations emails on tier-up.
  • Account linking: a customer's booking-site login is kept in sync with their client record; a merge tool combines duplicate accounts (e.g. someone who signs up with a new email) without losing history or credits.
  • Retention: automatic reminder emails to lapsing clients, plus birthday and review-request automations.
Section 07

Packages, Memberships & Credits

Clients buy class packs and memberships that hold credits. Credits are tracked in real time — a class booked or checked in deducts the right number, one per seat.

ConceptHow it works
FormatsSeparate credit wallets per format — Group, Mat, Private.
Per-class valueEach package stores what one class actually cost = net sale price ÷ credits. Used for accurate commission (see §11).
LifecycleActivation, low-balance, freezes, expiry and renewals — all automated by background jobs.
LedgerEvery deduction/refund is written to a package ledger for a complete audit trail.
Multi-person credit bookings When one person books for several people and pays by credit, the system deducts one credit per attendee (e.g. a 2-person booking deducts 2). The checkout clearly shows the exact number of credits before you confirm.
Section 08

Point of Sale & Checkout

The calendar POS ("Checkout") is where the front desk takes payment and checks people in. It's a single, flexible flow that handles every situation.

Pay by credit or drop-in

One click swaps between settling with a package credit or charging the drop-in price. The status banner shows the client's available credits, or notes they'll be charged as a drop-in.

Partial attendance

Booked for 3 but only 2 showed? A "How many people are attending?" stepper charges & deducts only for the attendees, shrinks the booking and frees the no-show seat.

Split the bill

"Split into separate people" turns a multi-seat booking into individual attendees, each checked out and paid for separately (each can use their own credits).

Add-ons & adjustments

Add merchandise or a package to the same sale, apply a discount or promo code, choose a payment method, and add a note. Custom amounts require a reason for the audit trail.

Guardrails built in Every custom charge is checked against the expected price (per seat × attendees) so mistakes surface immediately; each sale produces a clean invoice & receipt; and credit settlements can't double-deduct or erase a prior cash payment.
Section 09

Payments & Stripe

Online payments run through Stripe with a fully idempotent webhook (processed-event de-duplication), so a booking is only ever confirmed once even if Stripe retries.

  • Deposit / partial / pay-at-studio options, configurable per studio.
  • Multiple desk payment methods: Cash, Bank Transfer, MoMo, ZaloPay, Credit Card, Wise, Stripe.
  • An online-payment "VAT (online only)" surcharge can be applied — but it is a pass-through fee, excluded from both revenue reporting and instructor commission (see §10–11), while still shown on the invoice and surfaced as a separate "fees collected" figure.
Section 10

Finance & Accounting

The finance module turns day-to-day activity into real accounting.

AreaWhat it covers
RevenueCash-basis — counts money actually received (not merely invoiced), net of the online-fee pass-through. Dashboard shows monthly revenue, month-over-month delta, and total online fees collected separately.
P&LProfit & loss with revenue by method and category, expenses, salaries and payroll.
Fund poolsNet profit is split into Marketing / Savings / Owners pools (a configurable triple that must sum to 100%).
Owner financesOwner loans, loan repayments and profit distributions.
Expenses & stockExpense tracking by category, merchandise SKUs, stock receipts and low-stock alerts.
Why cash-basis matters here Revenue only counts what's genuinely received, so unpaid packages or outstanding deposit balances never inflate the numbers. This was a deliberate correction to avoid over-stating income.
Section 11

Payroll & Commission

Instructor pay is the most nuanced part of the system, supporting several commission models plus bonuses, with one-click monthly payroll runs.

Commission models

  • Percentage / tiered — a % of class revenue, where the rate can step up with the instructor's monthly class count.
  • Fixed per-head — a fixed amount per attendee.
  • Revenue-split — a % of the studio's monthly revenue.
  • Flat private rate — for private sessions.

The rules that keep commission honest

RuleWhy
Package bookings commission on the package's per-class rate (net sale price ÷ credits), not the full drop-inA client on a discounted 10-pack didn't pay the drop-in price, so paying commission on the drop-in would over-pay the instructor.
A class only counts toward the class total / tier if ≥1 attendee actually checked inEmpty or all-no-show classes shouldn't advance an instructor's tier.
The online (VAT) fee is never commissionableIt's a pass-through surcharge, not studio earnings.
Partial attendance recomputes correctlyIf only 2 of 3 booked show up, revenue & commission reflect the 2 who attended.
Two code paths, one truth Commission is computed in two places — the finalised payroll run and the live per-class "Financials" view on the calendar. Both carry the identical rules so the number an instructor sees always matches what they're paid.
Section 12

Analytics & Notifications

Analytics

Dashboards focus on numbers that grow a studio, not vanity metrics: monthly revenue & delta, active clients (rolling 30 days), classes this week, class occupancy / fill rate, retention cohorts, revenue by client segment, and instructor performance. Class analytics only count completed classes with attendees, and the analytics page defaults to the current month.

Notifications

A unified notification system delivers by email and PWA web push:

  • Staff pushes: a "✨ New booking" alert to the class instructor and admins/managers — now firing for every booking source (customer online, reception, instructor, POS walk-in), not just customer bookings.
  • Customer automations: class reminders, review requests, birthdays, and VIP / Super-VIP milestone emails.
  • Editable templates: email templates are configurable in Settings, with correct branded links and a List-Unsubscribe header for deliverability.
Section 13

Integrations

Stripe

Card payments with idempotent webhooks and processed-event de-duplication.

Meta Pixel + Conversions API

Dual browser-pixel + server-side CAPI with a shared event ID for de-duplication and better match quality (fbp/fbc). Funnel events tracked; internal tags stripped from customer-facing content.

Email (Brevo SMTP)

Reliable bulk delivery via a Brevo relay, with SPF/DKIM/DMARC + reverse-DNS set up for inbox placement. A test-mode safety net can redirect all mail away from real customers.

Web Push (VAPID)

Installable-PWA push to staff and customers, respecting per-user notification preferences.

Section 14

Deployment & Infrastructure

The production stack runs as Docker containers on a single VPS, fronted by nginx for TLS and routing.

ComponentDetail
BackendASP.NET Core container on 127.0.0.1:8391 → :8080.
FrontendAstro static build served by nginx on 127.0.0.1:3719. The API base URL is baked in at build time.
MongoDB / Redis / RustFSAuth-protected, bound to localhost, on non-default host ports.
Routingnginx: /→frontend, /api/*→backend, /…-public/*→object storage; TLS via Let's Encrypt (auto-renew).
ObservabilitySerilog structured logs + self-hosted GlitchTip error tracking (tunnel-only).
BackupsFull system backups (database + media + source) captured as encrypted archives.
Deploy flow Images are built directly on the VPS (docker build … for backend and frontend), then the two app containers are recreated with docker compose … up -d backend frontend. A quick smoke test (/api/settings → 401, / → 200) confirms the routing is healthy.
Section 15

Studio Nexis — the Multi-Tenant SaaS

Studio Nexis takes the very same platform and turns it into a product you can license to other studios — each getting its own branded space, on its own subdomain, with its data fully walled off.

It began as an isolated fork of Soul Pilates (separate code, database, containers, ports and secrets, so building it can never touch the live studio) and was restructured into a database-per-tenant SaaS.

How isolation works — database-per-tenant

Request arrives
A studio's subdomain <studio>.studionexis… hits the server.
Tenant resolved
Middleware reads the subdomain, looks the studio up in a control-plane registry, and binds the request to that studio's own database — e.g. tenant_lotus-yoga.
App runs unchanged
The data context transparently points at the tenant's database, so all ~40 services work exactly as before — with zero changes — but on isolated data.
Proven isolation The same login succeeds on a studio's own subdomain (its database) and fails on any other — different studio, different database. A query bug can't leak one studio's clients into another's.

What's built

CapabilityDetail
Self-serve signupA studio signs up from the marketing site, picks a subdomain, and is provisioned instantly — its own database seeded with its own admin.
Owner onboardingFirst login lands in the admin portal and opens a 3-step setup wizard (team, class types, studio settings).
Super-admin planeCreate / list / suspend studios and manage their plan & subscription — restricted to the platform operator.
Licensing & trials14-day trials, plan tiers, and enforcement: an expired trial or lapsed subscription blocks the app (but never the login, so the owner can renew).
Wildcard routing + TLSEvery *.studionexis… subdomain is served and TLS-secured by one wildcard certificate.
Marketing siteA premium product landing page + pricing on the apex; the booking/studio app is hidden there (it belongs to each tenant's subdomain).

Safety while co-located

During development the SaaS runs on the same box as the live studio but is fenced off: separate everything, plus hard CPU/RAM caps so the fork can never starve the live system. The plan is to migrate it to a dedicated server before onboarding real paying studios — and a complete one-command migration bundle (all code, databases, media, nginx configs and a setup script) is ready for exactly that.

Section 16

Recent Enhancements & Roadmap

Recently shipped (live studio)

  • Multi-seat "book for N", split-into-separate-people, and partial-attendance checkout (charge only who showed).
  • Correct multi-person credit deduction and a fix for a phantom balance after partial check-in.
  • Online (VAT) fee excluded from revenue and commission, with a separate "fees collected" metric.
  • Commission fixes: package per-class rate, empty-class exclusion, partial-attendance recompute.
  • Full receptionist class-management permissions (mark completed, check-in, block/unblock).
  • Instructor PWA: notch-safe layout, attendee contact / limited profile, remove-attendee.
  • New-booking push for all booking sources; push-driven live calendar refresh.
  • Global client quick-search in the top bar, ranked by recency, redesigned to match spec.
  • Redesigned calendar checkout modal; SEO foundation for the public site.

On the roadmap

Studio Nexis → launch-ready

Stripe subscription billing + webhooks (auto-activate on payment) and a "renew/subscribe" page; per-tenant background jobs; signup hardening (email verify + captcha); JWT tenant claim; then migrate to a dedicated server.

Live studio

Continued refinements to POS, analytics and the customer experience, plus the P&L netting of the online-fee pass-through.

In one sentence Soul Pilates is a complete, connected studio-management platform running live for the Da Nang studio — and Studio Nexis is that same platform reborn as a multi-tenant SaaS, ready to give any studio its own isolated instance in minutes.

Soul Pilates & Studio Nexis · Complete System Breakdown · Generated July 2026

"Split into separate people" turns a multi-seat booking into individual attendees, each checked out and paid for separately (each can use their own credits).

Add-ons & adjustments

Add merchandise or a package to the same sale, apply a discount or promo code, choose a payment method, and add a note. Custom amounts require a reason for the audit trail.

Guardrails built in Every custom charge is checked against the expected price (per seat × attendees) so mistakes surface immediately; each sale produces a clean invoice & receipt; and credit settlements can't double-deduct or erase a prior cash payment.
Section 09

Payments & Stripe

Online payments run through Stripe with a fully idempotent webhook (processed-event de-duplication), so a booking is only ever confirmed once even if Stripe retries.

  • Deposit / partial / pay-at-studio options, configurable per studio.
  • Multiple desk payment methods: Cash, Bank Transfer, MoMo, ZaloPay, Credit Card, Wise, Stripe.
  • An online-payment "VAT (online only)" surcharge can be applied — but it is a pass-through fee, excluded from both revenue reporting and instructor commission (see §10–11), while still shown on the invoice and surfaced as a separate "fees collected" figure.
Section 10

Finance & Accounting

The finance module turns day-to-day activity into real accounting.

AreaWhat it covers
RevenueCash-basis — counts money actually received (not merely invoiced), net of the online-fee pass-through. Dashboard shows monthly revenue, month-over-month delta, and total online fees collected separately.
P&LProfit & loss with revenue by method and category, expenses, salaries and payroll.
Fund poolsNet profit is split into Marketing / Savings / Owners pools (a configurable triple that must sum to 100%).
Owner financesOwner loans, loan repayments and profit distributions.
Expenses & stockExpense tracking by category, merchandise SKUs, stock receipts and low-stock alerts.
Why cash-basis matters here Revenue only counts what's genuinely received, so unpaid packages or outstanding deposit balances never inflate the numbers. This was a deliberate correction to avoid over-stating income.
Section 11

Payroll & Commission

Instructor pay is the most nuanced part of the system, supporting several commission models plus bonuses, with one-click monthly payroll runs.

Commission models

  • Percentage / tiered — a % of class revenue, where the rate can step up with the instructor's monthly class count.
  • Fixed per-head — a fixed amount per attendee.
  • Revenue-split — a % of the studio's monthly revenue.
  • Flat private rate — for private sessions.

The rules that keep commission honest

RuleWhy
Package bookings commission on the package's per-class rate (net sale price ÷ credits), not the full drop-inA client on a discounted 10-pack didn't pay the drop-in price, so paying commission on the drop-in would over-pay the instructor.
A class only counts toward the class total / tier if ≥1 attendee actually checked inEmpty or all-no-show classes shouldn't advance an instructor's tier.
The online (VAT) fee is never commissionableIt's a pass-through surcharge, not studio earnings.
Partial attendance recomputes correctlyIf only 2 of 3 booked show up, revenue & commission reflect the 2 who attended.
Two code paths, one truth Commission is computed in two places — the finalised payroll run and the live per-class "Financials" view on the calendar. Both carry the identical rules so the number an instructor sees always matches what they're paid.
Section 12

Analytics & Notifications

Analytics

Dashboards focus on numbers that grow a studio, not vanity metrics: monthly revenue & delta, active clients (rolling 30 days), classes this week, class occupancy / fill rate, retention cohorts, revenue by client segment, and instructor performance. Class analytics only count completed classes with attendees, and the analytics page defaults to the current month.

Notifications

A unified notification system delivers by email and PWA web push:

  • Staff pushes: a "✨ New booking" alert to the class instructor and admins/managers — now firing for every booking source (customer online, reception, instructor, POS walk-in), not just customer bookings.
  • Customer automations: class reminders, review requests, birthdays, and VIP / Super-VIP milestone emails.
  • Editable templates: email templates are configurable in Settings, with correct branded links and a List-Unsubscribe header for deliverability.
Section 13

Integrations

Stripe

Card payments with idempotent webhooks and processed-event de-duplication.

Meta Pixel + Conversions API

Dual browser-pixel + server-side CAPI with a shared event ID for de-duplication and better match quality (fbp/fbc). Funnel events tracked; internal tags stripped from customer-facing content.

Email (Brevo SMTP)

Reliable bulk delivery via a Brevo relay, with SPF/DKIM/DMARC + reverse-DNS set up for inbox placement. A test-mode safety net can redirect all mail away from real customers.

Web Push (VAPID)

Installable-PWA push to staff and customers, respecting per-user notification preferences.

Section 14

Deployment & Infrastructure

The production stack runs as Docker containers on a single VPS, fronted by nginx for TLS and routing.

ComponentDetail
BackendASP.NET Core container on 127.0.0.1:8391 → :8080.
FrontendAstro static build served by nginx on 127.0.0.1:3719. The API base URL is baked in at build time.
MongoDB / Redis / RustFSAuth-protected, bound to localhost, on non-default host ports.
Routingnginx: /→frontend, /api/*→backend, /…-public/*→object storage; TLS via Let's Encrypt (auto-renew).
ObservabilitySerilog structured logs + self-hosted GlitchTip error tracking (tunnel-only).
BackupsFull system backups (database + media + source) captured as encrypted archives.
Deploy flow Images are built directly on the VPS (docker build … for backend and frontend), then the two app containers are recreated with docker compose … up -d backend frontend. A quick smoke test (/api/settings → 401, / → 200) confirms the routing is healthy.
Section 15

Studio Nexis — the Multi-Tenant SaaS

Studio Nexis takes the very same platform and turns it into a product you can license to other studios — each getting its own branded space, on its own subdomain, with its data fully walled off.

It began as an isolated fork of Soul Pilates (separate code, database, containers, ports and secrets, so building it can never touch the live studio) and was restructured into a database-per-tenant SaaS.

How isolation works — database-per-tenant

Request arrives
A studio's subdomain <studio>.studionexis… hits the server.
Tenant resolved
Middleware reads the subdomain, looks the studio up in a control-plane registry, and binds the request to that studio's own database — e.g. tenant_lotus-yoga.
App runs unchanged
The data context transparently points at the tenant's database, so all ~40 services work exactly as before — with zero changes — but on isolated data.
Proven isolation The same login succeeds on a studio's own subdomain (its database) and fails on any other — different studio, different database. A query bug can't leak one studio's clients into another's.

What's built

CapabilityDetail
Self-serve signupA studio signs up from the marketing site, picks a subdomain, and is provisioned instantly — its own database seeded with its own admin.
Owner onboardingFirst login lands in the admin portal and opens a 3-step setup wizard (team, class types, studio settings).
Super-admin planeCreate / list / suspend studios and manage their plan & subscription — restricted to the platform operator.
Licensing & trials14-day trials, plan tiers, and enforcement: an expired trial or lapsed subscription blocks the app (but never the login, so the owner can renew).
Wildcard routing + TLSEvery *.studionexis… subdomain is served and TLS-secured by one wildcard certificate.
Marketing siteA premium product landing page + pricing on the apex; the booking/studio app is hidden there (it belongs to each tenant's subdomain).

Safety while co-located

During development the SaaS runs on the same box as the live studio but is fenced off: separate everything, plus hard CPU/RAM caps so the fork can never starve the live system. The plan is to migrate it to a dedicated server before onboarding real paying studios — and a complete one-command migration bundle (all code, databases, media, nginx configs and a setup script) is ready for exactly that.

Section 16

Recent Enhancements & Roadmap

Recently shipped (live studio)

  • Multi-seat "book for N", split-into-separate-people, and partial-attendance checkout (charge only who showed).
  • Correct multi-person credit deduction and a fix for a phantom balance after partial check-in.
  • Online (VAT) fee excluded from revenue and commission, with a separate "fees collected" metric.
  • Commission fixes: package per-class rate, empty-class exclusion, partial-attendance recompute.
  • Full receptionist class-management permissions (mark completed, check-in, block/unblock).
  • Instructor PWA: notch-safe layout, attendee contact / limited profile, remove-attendee.
  • New-booking push for all booking sources; push-driven live calendar refresh.
  • Global client quick-search in the top bar, ranked by recency, redesigned to match spec.
  • Redesigned calendar checkout modal; SEO foundation for the public site.

On the roadmap

Studio Nexis → launch-ready

Stripe subscription billing + webhooks (auto-activate on payment) and a "renew/subscribe" page; per-tenant background jobs; signup hardening (email verify + captcha); JWT tenant claim; then migrate to a dedicated server.

Live studio

Continued refinements to POS, analytics and the customer experience, plus the P&L netting of the online-fee pass-through.

In one sentence Soul Pilates is a complete, connected studio-management platform running live for the Da Nang studio — and Studio Nexis is that same platform reborn as a multi-tenant SaaS, ready to give any studio its own isolated instance in minutes.

content.text:
Fixed and verified. The metric now reflects **classes actually taught** — the real numbers for Nakko:

| Metric | Before (wrong) | Now |
|---|---|---|
| This month | ~200 | **43** |
| This week | — | 27 |
| Today | 10 | 2–3 (as completed) |

## What was wrong
It was counting **every session** assigned to the instructor — including the ~131 future/empty sessions the calendar pre-creates for the rest of the month. That's why the month showed 200.

## The fix
It now counts only classes she's **actually taught** — sessions that are **completed with at least one checked-in attendee** — bucketed by studio-local day / week / month. This is the exact same definition your **commission** uses, so the "This month" number will line up with the group + private class counts already shown on the earnings page.

## One thing to know
Because it counts **completed** classes, a class shows up once it's been marked completed (with attendees checked in) — so "today" reflects classes done *so far*, and ticks up through the day as each class wraps. If she taught 3 but one isn't marked completed yet (or nobody was checked in), it'll read 2 until that's done — which is the same rule that governs her pay, so they stay consistent.

Have her refresh the earnings page to see the corrected counts.

content.text:
I dug through the funnel data, and the picture is clearer than "accounts but no bookings" suggests — there are a few real friction points. Here's what the data actually says:

## What's really happening
| Signal | Number | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Accounts created **in the last 7 days** | **240 of 242** | The "flood of accounts" is your **activation-email campaign** — you created accounts *for* existing clients, they're not organic self-signups |
| Accounts **activated** (chose a password) | **29 (12%)** | 88% never completed activation → **can't log in → can't book online** |
| Bookings by source | **ADMIN 1,331 · WALK-IN 50 · ONLINE 36** | **Only ~2.5% of all bookings are customer self-service.** The studio runs almost entirely on desk bookings |
| Activated users who booked online | **13 of 29** | The ones who *do* activate convert fine (~45%) — so the wall is **before** booking, not the booking itself |
| Abandoned checkouts (stale reservations) | **0** | People aren't dropping *mid-checkout* — most never reach it |

So it's **not** that lots of customers sign up and abandon a booking. It's that **almost nobody reaches the online booking flow at all**, for three structural reasons:

## The friction points (in priority order)

**1. Guest checkout is OFF — you must have an account *and be logged in* to book.**
`AllowGuestCheckout: false`. I confirmed in the booking code: a customer who browses classes and clicks "Book" hits a **"please log in"** wall and gets redirected to `/login`. Combined with 88% not activated, this is the single biggest leak — the customer is ready to book and gets stopped by a login gate.

**2. Activation is a multi-step barrier (12% completion).**
Open email → click the *right* link → choose a password. We already saw the "superseded link" confusion (each new email kills the previous link) bites people here. Most of your client base simply can't log in.

**3. Online booking usually demands a 30% card deposit.**
`DepositPercentage: 30`, and the most common online path is `STRIPE_DEPOSIT` (15 of 36). A first-timer has to enter a card to book — friction vs. just showing up. (Pay-at-studio *is* enabled, but the deposit path dominates.)

## What I'd change (biggest impact first)
1. **Turn on guest checkout** — let people book with just name / phone / email, no account or login required. This removes the wall the ready-to-book customer hits. They can be offered an account *after*. I'd expect this alone to materially lift online bookings.
2. **Make activation painless** — fix the superseded-link issue (accept any unexpired token) and consider **passwordless / magic-link** login instead of "choose a password."
3. **Default online bookings to pay-at-studio** (make deposit optional or off) so a new customer can book without a card.

Want me to **enable guest checkout** and turn the mandatory deposit off (both are settings changes — quick and reversible), then tackle the activation flow? That's the fastest path to reducing the drop-off, and I can measure the online-booking rate again after a week to confirm it moved.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The immediate/current request (in-progress): "our no show rate is too high right now, so i prefer to have deposits on, but lets have just deposits for right now, no full payment (option to disable this if its not in settings already), and then lets have guest checkout (name, number, email)." Interpretation confirmed by data analysis: online payment should be **deposit-only** (STRIPE_DEPOSIT), disable pay-in-full (STRIPE_FULL) and pay-at-studio ("just deposits" for no-show reduction), and enable guest checkout (name/phone/email, no account required). Deposit percentage stays 30%. Package credit remains available for members.

   Immediately prior request: "are you able to take a look at the data and see if there are any friction points between the system and the end user when it comes to making bookings. We seem to have a lot of people making accounts but not actually making the bookings." (Completed as analysis — findings below.)

   Other recent completed requests (in reverse chronological order): per-day class calendar heatmap on instructor earnings page for the selected month; instructor earnings today/week/month class metrics (then corrected); instructor PWA add-multiple-quantity to class; instructor block-class from PWA; comprehensive system-breakdown PDF; (rejected) 5 website templates for Studio Nexis; Studio Nexis migration to nexis.revsports.ca; Studio Nexis SaaS full build.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Clean Architecture: SoulPilates.API (controllers/DI/Program.cs), .Core (entities/DTOs/interfaces), .Services (ALL business logic), .Infrastructure (MongoDbContext).
   - Tech: .NET 10 / ASP.NET Core, Astro 6 frontend, MongoDB 8, Redis 7, RustFS (S3), Stripe, Brevo SMTP, VAPID web push, GlitchTip.
   - IDs are `string` in C# with `[BsonRepresentation(ObjectId)]`, stored as ObjectId in Mongo — mongosh queries must use `ObjectId()`.
   - Two studios on one VPS (72.62.240.50): live soulpilates (backend 8391, frontend 3719, mongo container soulpilates-prod-mongo) and studionexis fork (backend 8392, frontend 3720, mongo studionexis-mongo, DB-per-tenant SaaS).
   - Settings: `GlobalSettings` is a single Mongo doc; `SettingsService.GetAsync` does lazy backfills with `ReplaceOneAsync`. The admin GET `/api/settings` returns an **explicit anonymous projection** (new fields must be added there to serialize). Public `/api/payment/checkout-settings` [AllowAnonymous] feeds checkout.astro; `/api/customer/cancel-policy` (CustomerAuthController) feeds booking.astro and returns `allowGuestCheckout`.
   - Deploy: build images on VPS, `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend`. Cloudflare-proxied apex.
   - Studio-local time is Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh = UTC+7 (no DST); sessions stored UTC.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **SoulPilates.Core/Entities/GlobalSettings.cs** — Added `AllowFullPayment` (bool, default true) after `AllowPartialPayment`:
     ```csharp
     /// <summary>Whether the pay-in-full online option is shown at checkout. Default true.
     /// Set false to make the deposit the only online payment option (e.g. to force a
     /// deposit for no-show reduction).
     public bool AllowFullPayment { get; set; } = true;
     ```
   - **SoulPilates.API/Controllers/PaymentController.cs** — checkout-settings endpoint (line ~110), added `allowFullPayment = s.AllowFullPayment,` between allowPartialPayment and allowPayAtStudio.
   - **SoulPilates.API/Controllers/SettingsController.cs** — GET projection, added `settings.AllowFullPayment,` after `settings.AllowPartialPayment,`.
   - **SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/checkout.astro** (line ~1616) — gated STRIPE_FULL:
     ```js
     const methods = ["PACKAGE_CREDIT"];
     if (checkoutSettings.allowOnlinePayment) {
       if (checkoutSettings.allowPartialPayment)
         methods.push("STRIPE_DEPOSIT");
       // Pay-in-full can be disabled (e.g. deposit-only for no-show reduction).
       if (checkoutSettings.allowFullPayment !== false)
         methods.push("STRIPE_FULL");
     }
     if (checkoutSettings.allowPayAtStudio) methods.push("PAY_AT_STUDIO");
     ```
     Note: checkout.astro loads settings from `/api/payment/checkout-settings` (line 1389, merged at 1411 via `...(await settingsRes.json())`). Handles guest checkout at line 1454 (`if (!token && checkoutSettings.allowGuestCheckout === false)`) and 2034.
   - **SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/booking.astro** — line 1673-1675 ALREADY respects guest: `if (!token && cancelPolicy.allowGuestCheckout === false) showBookingLoginPrompt(currentSessionId);`. cancelPolicy loaded from `/api/customer/cancel-policy` (line 446, default `allowGuestCheckout: true` at 444). `showBookingLoginPrompt` (line 1724) shows the "Login required to book" gate.
   - **SoulPilates.Services/SettingsService.cs** — `GetAsync` (line 87) reads the single doc, then runs multiple backfill blocks (ExpenseCategories, cancel windows, OwnersSplitPercentage) each doing `await _settings.ReplaceOneAsync(s => s.Id == existing.Id, existing, ...)`. Was reading this to find why `AllowFullPayment`/`AllowGuestCheckout` return wrong values.
   - **SoulPilates.API/Controllers/CustomerAuthController.cs** — cancel-policy endpoint (line 169) returns `allowGuestCheckout = settings.AllowGuestCheckout` (line 198). Confirmed.

   Earlier this session (all deployed to live):
   - **SoulPilates.Services/InstructorService.cs** — `GetClassDaysAsync(staffId, year, month)` returns `Dictionary<int,int>` (day→count) of COMPLETED classes with ≥1 CHECKED_IN/ARRIVED attendee, bucketed by studio-local day (UTC+7). Replaced the earlier `GetClassCountsAsync` (which wrongly counted ALL non-blocked/cancelled sessions incl. 131 future scheduled → showed 200; correct=43).
   - **SoulPilates.API/Controllers/InstructorController.cs** — `[HttpGet("class-days")]` returns `{year, month, total, counts}`; `[HttpPatch("session/{id}/block-status")]` (SetMySessionBlockStatus, ownership-checked) with `InstructorBlockStatusRequest {bool Blocked}`; `AddStudentToMySession` already passes `request.Quantity` (InstructorAddStudentRequest has Quantity=1 default).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Instructor class-counts inflated (200 vs ~43)**: was counting all sessions incl. 131 future SCHEDULED. Fixed to count COMPLETED sessions with ≥1 CHECKED_IN/ARRIVED attendee (mirrors commission rule). User feedback: "the stats are wrong, says nakko has done 200 classes this month... today it says 10 but she only did 3."
   - **Partial-attendance phantom balance**: after shrinking booking quantity, AmountDueAtStudio wasn't re-based → left phantom balance.    - **CURRENT UNRESOLVED**: checkout-settings endpoint returns `allowFullPayment:true` (should be false) and `allowGuestCheckout:false` (should be true) even though DB has correct values (single doc: AllowPartialPayment=true, AllowPayAtStudio=false, AllowGuestCheckout=true, AllowFullPayment=false) and localhost (bypassing Cloudflare) returns same wrong values. `allowPartialPayment=true` and `allowPayAtStudio=false` ARE correct.    - **Studio Nexis domain hardcoded**: made configurable (SaasController reads `Saas:BaseDomain`, signup.astro derives from PUBLIC_API_URL host).

5. Problem Solving:
   Booking-friction analysis findings: 242 customer accounts (240 created in last 7 days = the activation campaign, not organic); only 29 activated (12%); 225 have ≥1 booking but bookings are ADMIN 1331 / WALK_IN 50 / ONLINE 36 (only ~2.5% self-service); 0 abandoned reservations; of 29 activated, 13 booked online. Identified friction: (1) guest checkout OFF (must log in to book), (2) low activation, (3) deposit/full-payment. Recommended enabling guest checkout + deposits; user chose deposit-only + guest checkout.

   - "come up with a way to display classes for everyday of the month for each month that is selected in the month drop down instead of doing today, this week, and this month."

content.text:
Both endpoints now return the correct values. The deposit-only + guest-checkout change is live and working.

## Resolved

The root cause of the long-running mystery: **I'd been writing settings to the wrong collection.** The app's `SettingsService` reads from a collection literally named `Settings` (`CollectionName = "Settings"`), but a stray `GlobalSettings` collection also existed, and all my earlier `mongosh` edits landed there. Every other layer (binary, connection, deserialization) was correct the whole time — a probe using the app's own compiled `GlobalSettings` type deserialized the doc perfectly, which is what finally pointed me at the collection-name mismatch.

**What's now live** (verified on `127.0.0.1:8391`, bypassing Cloudflare):

`/api/payment/checkout-settings` → `allowOnlinePayment:true, allowPartialPayment:true, allowFullPayment:false, allowPayAtStudio:false, allowGuestCheckout:true` (deposit 30%)
`/api/customer/cancel-policy` → `allowGuestCheckout:true`

So checkout now offers **deposit-only** (STRIPE_DEPOSIT) + package credit for members, with **pay-in-full and pay-at-studio both hidden**, and **guests can book** with name/phone/email — no account required. The code changes (`AllowFullPayment` field + `checkout.astro` gating) were already built and deployed; they just needed the data on the correct collection.

Two follow-ups worth noting:
- The stray `GlobalSettings` collection (1 doc, unused by the app) is still there — I left it since dropping production data wasn't authorized. Harmless, but if you'd like it cleaned up, run in `mongosh`: `db.GlobalSettings.drop()`.
- Turning **pay-at-studio off** was my read of "just deposits" — it's now off. If you actually want to keep pay-at-studio available alongside deposits, say the word and I'll flip `AllowPayAtStudio` back to true.

Want me to save a memory note about the `Settings` vs `GlobalSettings` collection-name gotcha so this doesn't cost hours again next time?

The "Network error" was a **regression I introduced**. My two earlier frontend rebuilds (for the "Deposit for Drop-In Class" label and the guest-checkout changes) ran `docker build` **without** `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL`. The Dockerfile defaults that arg to `http://localhost:5000`, so Astro baked `localhost:5000` into the browser bundle. Every client-side API call — registration, and also the booking/checkout fetches — was pointed at the user's own machine, which has nothing on port 5000, so `fetch` threw → "Network error."

I rebuilt with `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn` and redeployed. Verified:
- The register bundle now calls `https://soulpilates.com.vn`
- No `localhost:5000` anywhere in the served build

Mystery solved — and it's **working as designed, not a bug**. Here's exactly what happened:

**The timeline**
- **July 4**: a CRM Client record named **"Nicholas Albanese"** was created (phone `3653365989`, email `haxkodid@gmail.com`) and made **4 group bookings** with Nakko (deposit method) — all later **cancelled**, marked "due at studio."
- **Today**: Nicholas registered a new login (`nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com`) using the **same phone number** `3653365989`.

**Why the bookings appeared**
`RegisterAsync` in [CustomerAuthService.cs:98](SoulPilates.Services/CustomerAuthService.cs:98) **auto-links a new account to an existing Client — by phone first, then email.** His phone matched the July-4 "Nicholas Albanese" client, so his new account was tied to `ClientId 6a48c40172398e9b80641779`, and that client's 4 cancelled bookings now show under his account. I confirmed all 4 references (`SP-260704-6472/9462/5397/5920`) belong to that client.

This is intentional: it means a walk-in/admin-created client who later signs up sees their real history instead of a blank slate. Since the name matches, this is genuinely *his* record — the link is correct.

**One data-quality wrinkle worth flagging:** there are actually **two** Client records with the national number `3653365989` but different country codes and emails:

content.text:
Yes — confirmed. **Guest bookings do create a Client profile in the backend.** There's no truly "anonymous" attendance; every reservation must be tied to a `ClientId` so it can appear on the calendar, get a booking reference, and be checked in.

## How it works

When a guest submits the checkout form, it hits `/api/booking/reserve` (`[AllowAnonymous]`, [BookingController.cs:266](SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs:266)), which:

1. **Looks for an existing client** via `FindByPhoneOrEmailAsync(phone, email)`:
   - Exact phone match → if the guest's number is already a client, **reuses** it (no duplicate)
   - If phone starts with `+`, also tries the split country-code + national form
   - Otherwise, exact **email** match
2. **If none found → auto-creates a new Client** (`FullName`, `PhoneNumber`, `Email`, `ContactPlatform="NONE"`, `CountryOfOrigin="Vietnam"`).
3. Creates a `RESERVED` attendance under that client. It shows on the calendar with the guest's name/phone/email.

So on the calendar, a guest booking looks like any other client booking. And because it's the same phone/email matching used at registration, **if that guest later signs up with the same phone or email, their account auto-links to this client** and they see the booking — exactly the mechanism behind the Nicholas situation.

## Two consistency gaps worth flagging

The guest dedup and the registration dedup don't behave identically:

| | Guest reserve | Registration |
|---|---|---|
| Placeholder-phone guard (e.g. `999999999`) | **No** — junk phones can collide unrelated guests | Yes (`IsPlaceholderPhone`) |
| Email matching | **Case-sensitive exact** (`c.Email == email`) | Case-insensitive regex |

Practical effects:
- A guest who types a filler phone number could get merged into another guest's client record (and see their bookings). Registration explicitly protects against this; guest reserve doesn't.
- A guest entering `Nick@Gmail.com` when a client exists as `nick@gmail.com` won't match → **duplicate client** created.

Want me to align the guest-reserve path with the registration logic (add the placeholder-phone guard + case-insensitive email match) so guest bookings dedup consistently and avoid both the collision and the duplicate-client cases?

Both deployed and backend is healthy. Here's everything that was implemented:

## Part 1 — "GUEST" tag on the calendar
- **[ListDtos.cs](SoulPilates.Core/DTOs/ListDtos.cs)** — added `IsGuest` to `ClassAttendeeDto`.
- **[SchedulingService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs)** — the roster builder now runs one `IN` query to find which client IDs have a `CustomerAccount`; anyone on the roster **without** an account is flagged `IsGuest = true`. (Definition of guest: a client who booked but never created an account.)
- **[ClassDetailPanel.astro](SoulPilates.Astro/src/components/admin/ClassDetailPanel.astro)** — renders a blue **GUEST** pill next to the name, right alongside the existing NEW / Recurring / ×qty tags.

- **[EmailService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/EmailService.cs)** — new `SendGuestBookingConfirmationAsync`: same booking details + `.ics` invite as the normal confirmation, **plus** a highlighted CTA block ("Want to manage this booking? Create your free account to see history, cancel/reschedule, and buy packages") with a **"Finish creating my account"** button. Bilingual (EN + short VI line). Reuses the editable BookingConfirmation template body, so admins keep control of the details wording.
- **[PaymentService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/PaymentService.cs)** — at the RESERVED→BOOKED transition, it checks whether the client has an account: registered customers get the standard email; **guests get the CTA variant**.
- **[register.astro](SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/register.astro)** — the CTA link pre-fills the registration form from `?name=&email=&phone=&redirect=/my-bookings`, splitting the name into first/last and peeling a `+84`-style country code into the selector, so the guest only has to set a password.

One design note: "guest" is defined as *no linked account*. So if a guest later finishes registration, their existing bookings will correctly stop showing the GUEST tag (the account now links to that client). content.text:
That's the answer. A token signed with the **current** `JWT_SECRET` returns **200** on every endpoint — including `/api/scheduling/class` (my code change works fine, no 500). So:

## Diagnosis: your login session is stale, not a data/backend problem

- **Backend auth is healthy** — a freshly-signed token works everywhere (200).
- **My feature code is fine** — the class-detail endpoint returns 200 with a valid token; the GUEST-tag change didn't break anything.
- **Your browser's token is being rejected** (77 × 401 across the board). It was signed with a *previous* `JWT_SECRET`. When my deploy today recreated the backend container, it loaded the current `JWT_SECRET` from `prod.env` — and `JWT_PREVIOUS_SECRET` is empty, so tokens signed with the old key no longer validate.

In other words: at some earlier point the `JWT_SECRET` in `prod.env` was rotated, but the old backend process was still running in memory with the previous key (so your existing token kept working). Today's restart activated the new key, invalidating tokens issued under the old one.

## The fix (30 seconds)
**Log out and log back in** to the admin panel. That issues a fresh token signed with the current secret, and everything — calendar details, washout, owners — will load again. Any other staff/admin still logged in will need to re-login once too; after that it's stable (the 7-day token lifetime and stable key mean this won't recur).

## Why it *looked* like my change broke it

content.text:
Good question — and it's worth being opinionated here, because the "default" TikTok objective (Website Conversions) is usually the *wrong* first move for a studio your size. Here's how I'd think about it for Soul Pilates specifically.

## The core constraint: conversion volume
TikTok's conversion optimization needs roughly **50 conversion events per ad group per week** to exit the learning phase. A boutique Da Nang studio doing a few dozen online bookings a month won't feed that — so if you point TikTok straight at "optimize for bookings," it stays stuck in learning, spends inefficiently, and looks like TikTok "doesn't work." So match the objective to the volume you can actually generate.

## Recommended objective by goal

**1. Messages / Lead Gen → best starting point (your "messages" goal)**
For a local service in Vietnam, **intent capture beats direct booking**. People discover you on TikTok cold; they're not ready to pay a deposit in one tap.
- Use **Lead Generation (Instant Form)** or **Messages** with a concrete offer ("First class + posture assessment — book your trial") .
- Instant Forms fill *inside* TikTok (no site friction), and you get name + phone + a lead volume high enough to optimize on.
- Then follow up on **Zalo/WhatsApp** (which you already flagged as your preferred channels) to close them into a booking. This is where Vietnamese local businesses convert.

**2. Website Conversions → phase two, once the pixel has data**
Once you're generating steady booking/deposit events, *then* run a Website Conversion campaign optimized for the deposit event. It'll work far better because the pixel has learned. Retarget your TikTok engagers + video-viewers here.

**3. Sales (packages) → retargeting only, not cold**
Nobody buys a class package from a cold TikTok. Sell packages to warm audiences: past bookers, IG/TikTok engagers, and — importantly — your **guests who booked but never bought a package** (you now have those records). Upload them as a Custom Audience.

## A concrete funnel for you
1. **Cold (Reach/Video Views + Lead Gen):** trial-class offer → capture phone → Zalo follow-up.
2. **Warm (Website Conversions):** retarget engagers → drive to the booking page (now deposit-only, low friction).
3. **Customer (Product Sales/Messages):** retarget bookers → package upsell.

## Two things that matter more than the objective
- **Creative is 80% of TikTok.** Native, phone-shot, founder/instructor-on-camera > polished ads. Winning angles for Pilates: posture/back-pain fixes, "what a private session actually looks like," transformation/consistency, studio vibe. Run 3–5 raw variations, kill losers weekly.
- **Tracking.** You already run Meta Pixel + Conversions API server-side. TikTok has the exact same setup (**TikTok Pixel + Events API**), and your deposit-only checkout gives a clean, meaningful conversion event to optimize on. Without it, TikTok is flying blind.

## Offer strategy — use your deposit flow as the hook
Your deposit-only checkout is a genuine advantage here: "**Reserve your trial with just a ₫150k deposit**" is a low-commitment CTA that still filters out no-shows. Lead with that.

---

If it's useful, I can do the technical side that ties into your system: **wire up TikTok Pixel + Events API** the same way the Meta integration works (fire deposit/booking events server-side), and/or add an **export of "guests who never bought a package"** to upload as a TikTok Custom Audience for the package-retargeting campaign. Want me to set either of those up?

One caveat: I can advise on the ad-account mechanics and the tracking integration, but I can't create campaigns, spend budget, or log into TikTok Ads Manager on your behalf — you'd drive those steps.

file.content:
<!--
  Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel + Conversions API loader.
  Include in every customer-facing page's <head>. Pages using CustomerLayout get
  it automatically; standalone pages (login/register/onboarding/…) include it too.

  Exposes window.spMetaTrack(eventName, customData, userData):
    • fires the browser Pixel with a fresh eventID, AND
    • relays the same event (same eventID) to /api/meta/event so the backend
      forwards it to Meta's Conversions API — de-duplicated by eventID.
  Safe no-op until a Pixel ID is configured (Events Manager → env).
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initMetaPixel() {
    // Default to a no-op so callers never crash before config resolves.
    window.spMetaTrack = window.spMetaTrack || function () {};

    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch (e) {}

    function getCookie(name) {
      var m = document.cookie.match('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;]*)');
      return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null;
    }

    function uuid() {
      try { if (crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {}
      return 'e-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(16).slice(2);
    }

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/config')
      .then(function (res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.enabled || !cfg.pixelId) return;
        var pixelId = cfg.pixelId;

        // ── Meta Pixel base code ──
        !(function (f, b, e, v, n, t, s) {
          if (f.fbq) return; n = f.fbq = function () {
            n.callMethod ? n.callMethod.apply(n, arguments) : n.queue.push(arguments);
          };
          if (!f._fbq) f._fbq = n; n.push = n; n.loaded = !0; n.version = '2.0';
          n.queue = []; t = b.createElement(e); t.async = !0; t.src = v;
          s = b.getElementsByTagName(e)[0]; s.parentNode.insertBefore(t, s);
        })(window, document, 'script', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js');

        fbq('init', pixelId);

        // ── Dual Pixel + CAPI tracker ──
        window.spMetaTrack = function (eventName, customData, userData) {
          customData = customData || {};
          userData = userData || {};
          var eventId = uuid();

          try { fbq('track', eventName, customData, { eventID: eventId }); } catch (e) {}

          // Synthesize fbc from an ?fbclid= param if the cookie isn't set yet.
          var fbc = getCookie('_fbc');
          if (!fbc) {
            try {
              var p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('fbclid');
              if (p) fbc = 'fb.1.' + Date.now() + '.' + p;
            } catch (e) {}
          }

          var payload = {
            eventName: eventName,
            eventId: eventId,
            eventSourceUrl: window.location.href,
            email: userData.email || null,
            phone: userData.phone || null,
            fbp: getCookie('_fbp'),
            fbc: fbc,
            value: (customData.value != null) ? customData.value : null,
            currency: customData.currency || null,
            contentName: customData.content_name || null,
            contentCategory: customData.content_category || null,
            contentIds: customData.content_ids || null,
          };

          try {
            fetch(API_URL + '/api/meta/event', {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify(payload),
              keepalive: true,
            }).catch(function () {});
          } catch (e) {}
        };

        // Fire the initial PageView through the dual path so it carries a shared
        // eventID (deduplicated with the server) AND is sent via the Conversions
        // API — not browser-pixel-only. Sends fbp/fbc for better match quality.
        try { window.spMetaTrack('PageView'); } catch (e) {}
      })
      .catch(function () {});
  })();
</script>

input.content:
<!--
  TikTok Pixel + Events API loader. Include alongside MetaPixel in every
  customer-facing page's <head>. Pages using CustomerLayout get it automatically;
  standalone pages (login/register/onboarding/…) include it too.

  Exposes window.spTiktokTrack(eventName, customData, userData):
    • fires the browser Pixel with a fresh event_id, AND
    • relays the same event (same event_id) to /api/tiktok/event so the backend
      forwards it to TikTok's Events API — de-duplicated by event_id.
  Callers pass the SAME (Meta-style) event names as spMetaTrack; this loader
  maps them to TikTok's standard event names. Safe no-op until a Pixel Code is
  configured (Events Manager → env).
-->
<script is:inline>
  (function initTiktokPixel() {
    // Default to a no-op so callers never crash before config resolves.
    window.spTiktokTrack = window.spTiktokTrack || function () {};

    var API_URL = '';
    try {
      var metaApi = document.querySelector('meta[name="api-url"]');
      API_URL = metaApi ? metaApi.content : '';
    } catch (e) {}

    // Map the shared (Meta-style) event names used across the app to TikTok's
    // standard web events so call sites stay identical to the Meta ones.
    var EVENT_MAP = {
      PageView: 'Pageview',
      ViewContent: 'ViewContent',
      InitiateCheckout: 'InitiateCheckout',
      Purchase: 'CompletePayment',
      CompleteRegistration: 'CompleteRegistration',
    };

    function getCookie(name) {
      var m = document.cookie.match('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;]*)');
      return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null;
    }

    function uuid() {
      try { if (crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID(); } catch (e) {}
      return 'e-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(16).slice(2);
    }

    fetch(API_URL + '/api/tiktok/config')
      .then(function (res) { return res.ok ? res.json() : null; })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (!cfg || !cfg.enabled || !cfg.pixelCode) return;
        var pixelCode = cfg.pixelCode;

        // ── TikTok Pixel base code ──
        !(function (w, d, t) {
          w.TiktokAnalyticsObject = t;
          var ttq = w[t] = w[t] || [];
          ttq.methods = ['page', 'track', 'identify', 'instances', 'debug', 'on', 'off', 'once', 'ready', 'alias', 'group', 'enableCookie', 'disableCookie', 'holdConsent', 'revokeConsent', 'grantConsent'];
          ttq.setAndDefer = function (t, e) { t[e] = function () { t.push([e].concat(Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments, 0))); }; };
          for (var i = 0; i < ttq.methods.length; i++) ttq.setAndDefer(ttq, ttq.methods[i]);
          ttq.instance = function (t) { for (var e = ttq._i[t] || [], n = 0; n < ttq.methods.length; n++) ttq.setAndDefer(e, ttq.methods[n]); return e; };
          ttq.load = function (e, n) {
            var r = 'https://analytics.tiktok.com/i18n/pixel/events.js', o = n && n.partner;
            ttq._i = ttq._i || {}; ttq._i[e] = []; ttq._i[e]._u = r;
            ttq._t = ttq._t || {}; ttq._t[e] = +new Date();
            ttq._o = ttq._o || {}; ttq._o[e] = n || {};
            n = d.createElement('script'); n.type = 'text/javascript'; n.async = !0; n.src = r + '?sdkid=' + e + '&lib=' + t;
            e = d.getElementsByTagName('script')[0]; e.parentNode.insertBefore(n, e);
          };
          ttq.load(pixelCode);
          ttq.page();
        })(window, document, 'ttq');

        // ── Dual Pixel + Events API tracker ──
        window.spTiktokTrack = function (eventName, customData, userData) {
          customData = customData || {};
          userData = userData || {};
          var ttEvent = EVENT_MAP[eventName] || eventName;
          var eventId = uuid();

          // TikTok pixel "contents" array format.
          var contents = null;
          if (customData.content_ids && customData.content_ids.length) {
            contents = customData.content_ids.map(function (id) {
              return { content_id: id, content_type: 'product', content_name: customData.content_name || '' };
            });
          }
          var props = {};
          if (customData.value != null) props.value = customData.value;
          if (customData.currency) props.currency = customData.currency;
          if (customData.content_name) props.content_name = customData.content_name;
          if (customData.content_category) props.content_category = customData.content_category;
          if (contents) props.contents = contents;

          // Advanced matching — TikTok's pixel hashes these client-side.
          try {
            if (userData.email || userData.phone) {
              ttq.identify({ email: userData.email || undefined, phone_number: userData.phone || undefined });
            }
          } catch (e) {}

          try { ttq.track(ttEvent, props, { event_id: eventId }); } catch (e) {}

          // Synthesize ttclid from a ?ttclid= param for click attribution.
          var ttclid = getCookie('ttclid');
          if (!ttclid) {
            try {
              var p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('ttclid');
              if (p) ttclid = p;
            } catch (e) {}
          }

          var payload = {
            eventName: ttEvent,
            eventId: eventId,
            eventSourceUrl: window.location.href,
            email: userData.email || null,
            phone: userData.phone || null,
            ttp: getCookie('_ttp'),
            ttclid: ttclid,
            value: (customData.value != null) ? customData.value : null,
            currency: customData.currency || null,
            contentName: customData.content_name || null,
            contentCategory: customData.content_category || null,
            contentIds: customData.content_ids || null,
          };

          try {
            fetch(API_URL + '/api/tiktok/event', {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify(payload),
              keepalive: true,
            }).catch(function () {});
          } catch (e) {}
        };

        // Fire the initial PageView through the dual path so it carries a shared
        // event_id (deduplicated with the server) AND is sent via the Events API.
        try { window.spTiktokTrack('PageView'); } catch (e) {}
      })
      .catch(function () {});
  })();
</script>

content.text:
TikTok Pixel + Events API is live and deployed — built as an exact mirror of your Meta setup (dual browser-pixel + server-side, deduplicated by `event_id`, so it survives ad-blockers/iOS just like Meta).

## What was built
**Backend** (mirrors `MetaConversionsService`):
- `TiktokEventsService` → posts to TikTok Events API v1.3, SHA-256-hashes email/phone, forwards IP + user-agent + `_ttp`/`ttclid`.
- `TiktokTrackingController` → `GET /api/tiktok/config` (public, never leaks the token) and `POST /api/tiktok/event`.

**Frontend** (`components/TikTokPixel.astro`, added next to `<MetaPixel />` on all 8 customer pages):
- Exposes `window.spTiktokTrack(...)`. Call sites run **in parallel** with the Meta ones, so both platforms get the same events with the same data:

| Funnel step | Meta | TikTok |
|---|---|---|
| Page load | PageView | Pageview |
| Viewing a class | ViewContent | ViewContent |
| Reached payment | InitiateCheckout | InitiateCheckout |
| **Booking confirmed** | Purchase | **CompletePayment** |
| New account | CompleteRegistration | CompleteRegistration |

Purchase/CompletePayment sends the full booking value + email/phone for match quality and ROAS optimization.

**It's dormant right now** — `/api/tiktok/config` returns `enabled:false` because no credentials are set, so the pixel is a no-op and nothing fires. Meta is unaffected.

## To activate (your steps — I can't access TikTok Ads Manager)
1. In **TikTok Events Manager**, create a Web pixel → copy the **Pixel Code** (looks like `C…`), and under Settings generate an **Events API Access Token**.
2. Paste them into `prod.env`:
   ```
   TIKTOK_PIXEL_CODE=<your pixel code>
   TIKTOK_EVENTS_TOKEN=<your access token>
   ```
   (`TIKTOK_TEST_EVENT_CODE` optional, only for the Test Events tab.)
3. Redeploy: `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend`
4. Verify `curl 127.0.0.1:8391/api/tiktok/config` shows `enabled:true`, then watch **Events Manager → Test Events** while you click through a booking to confirm ViewContent → InitiateCheckout → CompletePayment land (and show as deduplicated "Browser + Server").

I saved all of this to project memory so it's documented for later.

content.text:
I've found the cause, and it's serious enough that you should decide how to handle it rather than me just changing it.

## What's actually happening

Your booking system isn't down because of my changes or a normal bug. There's a **hidden remote kill-switch** built into the backend code, in a class called `UpdateCheckerService` ([UpdateCheckerService.cs](SoulPilates.Services/UpdateCheckerService.cs)):

- On **every startup** and then **every ~60 seconds**, the app phones home to a hardcoded external server: **`https://soulpilatescrm.badal.om`**.
- It expects that server to reply `{"active": true}`. If the reply is anything else — **or the server is simply unreachable** — the app **refuses to start and shuts itself down**.
- Right now that server (`57.129.94.127`) **resolves in DNS but isn't responding** (my probe timed out after 20s). So your entire backend is stuck in a crash loop, and every customer/admin page that needs the API is dead.

This was deliberately **obfuscated to hide it from you**: the URL is assembled from raw byte arrays "to avoid accidental plain-text matches during source-tree searches" (their own comment), the error messages are base64-encoded, and the user-facing message is disguised as a generic "infrastructure component unreachable" error. Whoever built your system (the `badal.om` domain — likely the original developer/agency) put in a switch that lets them, or an outage on their end, take your whole business offline. That's what just happened.

## What this means
- This is **your** system on **your** VPS. A third party's server outage should never be able to kill it — but as written, it can, and did.
- Removing it restores your service and makes you independent of their server. The only reason to hesitate is if you have a **contract/licensing relationship** with that developer where this is a (however unfair) enforcement mechanism you agreed to — that's a business call only you can make.

I can restore you in a few minutes by patching out the startup gate and the self-shutdown loop. But given the vendor/contract implications, I want your explicit go-ahead first.

content.text:
I've now tested the complete customer funnel end-to-end against the live site. Here's the verdict.

## ✅ Everything on the customer side works — verified live just now
I walked the entire funnel against `soulpilates.com.vn` and every step passed:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Schedule loads (class list) | ✅ 4 classes Jul 17, 28 over next 10 days, materialized to Oct 31 |
| Class detail | ✅ 200 |
| Price quote | ✅ deposit 30% = 157,500₫ (150k + 5% online fee) |
| Checkout settings | ✅ deposit-only, guest checkout ON |
| **Guest reservation** (name/phone/email) | ✅ created booking `SP-260711-2828` |
| **Stripe deposit payment intent** | ✅ clientSecret + publishable key returned, 157,500₫ |
| **Account creation** | ✅ "Account created successfully" |
| **Login** | ✅ token + clientId issued |
| Booking page renders | ✅ 200, correct API base, auto-advances past empty days |

(The recent `CANCELLED` online bookings in your data are my test reservations, which I released after — not real customers.)

So the funnel is **not** technically broken today. Which means the 99% drop was caused by things that were breaking it *before*, plus factors off the server.

## What actually caused the drop
1. **Chronic downtime from the hidden kill-switch (the big one).** That covert `badal.om` phone-home crash-looped your entire backend *every time* the vendor's server was unreachable — and it's been in the code since migration. Every customer who visited during an outage saw exactly the "Something went wrong — couldn't load the schedule" screen you screenshotted, and left. This alone could explain most of the drop. **Fixed today.**
2. **Guest checkout was OFF** until we turned it on — customers were forced to create an account before booking. Major abandonment. **Fixed.**
3. **Today's `localhost:5000` regression** (my build mistake earlier) broke *all* API calls for anyone who visited during that window. **Fixed.**
4. **The data pattern confirms it:** since June, bookings are 199 ADMIN / 52 WALK-IN / ~41 ONLINE (most of those ONLINE are test/released). Customers effectively haven't been able to self-book online — staff have been entering everything manually.

## The one thing I can't test from here — and it's likely significant
**Discoverability.** A 99% drop *exactly at migration* very often means customers can't *find* the new booking link. I can confirm people are reaching the page (126 hits/48h), but you should verify every place a customer clicks "Book" now points to `soulpilates.com.vn/booking`:
- **Google Business Profile** — the "Book" button / website link (this is huge for a local studio)
- **Instagram / Facebook bio links**
- **Any QR codes** in the studio or on flyers
- **Old SimplyBook** — is it still live and taking (or silently dropping) bookings? Old bookmarks/links should redirect to the new site.
- **Tell your existing customers** (Zalo/WhatsApp broadcast) the booking link changed.

Quick way to confirm which problem it is: check **GA4** for booking-page traffic since migration. Low traffic → discoverability. Normal traffic but no bookings → funnel (but the funnel works now, so I'd bet on traffic + the downtime).

## My recommendations
1. **It's stable now — but add uptime monitoring.** We just removed the kill-switch; there's nothing alerting you if the backend goes down again. I can set up a simple health-check + alert so you know within minutes, not when bookings vanish.
2. **Fix the booking links everywhere** (above) — likely your single biggest recovery lever.
3. **Reconsider deposit friction vs. no-shows.** Deposit-only is stricter than SimplyBook likely was. It's the right call for no-shows, but if bookings stay low, test allowing "reserve now / pay at studio" for a bit and compare.
4. **Today and tomorrow (Jul 11–12) have zero group classes** — verify that's intentional; gaps in the schedule mean nothing to book for someone visiting today.

Want me to **set up the uptime monitoring/alerting** now so you're never silently down again? Given what we just found, I'd strongly recommend it.

145	                .Find(Builders<Invoice>.Filter.And(

149	                .ToListAsync())
150	            .ToDictionary(

Clear answer: **No — these cancelled deposit bookings are not counted as revenue.** I verified it directly.

## Why
Your revenue figure is computed from **actual Payment records** (money genuinely collected), and only against invoices that aren't voided ([AnalyticsService.cs:127](SoulPilates.Services/AnalyticsService.cs:127)). It does **not** count projected or "due" amounts.

The cancelled rows you're looking at (Funnel Test, Guest Test, Hello tiktok, etc.) have:
- **No invoice** and **no payment record** — collected = ₫0.
- The `AmountPaid = 157,500` you might see is just a field on the booking from an **abandoned/test checkout** (a Stripe deposit *intent* was created but the payment was never actually completed). It's a projection, not collected cash.

So the "deposit" and "350,000 due" labels in that list are what the booking *would* have involved — not money in your account.

## I checked every cancelled booking, not just these
Across **all 39 cancelled / late-cancelled bookings**, the total actually-collected money is **₫0**. So cancelled bookings are contributing **nothing** to your revenue. Your revenue numbers are not inflated by any of this.

## The general rule (for when a real deposit *is* collected)
If a customer genuinely pays a deposit via Stripe and later cancels:
- A real Payment + Invoice would exist. Revenue counts collected cash on non-voided invoices, and cancellation **reduces** the linked invoice rather than always voiding it.
- Practically: a **kept** deposit (late cancel, no refund) *would* show as revenue — which is usually correct, since it's a cancellation fee you actually collected. A **refunded** deposit nets back out.
- Right now this is moot — you have zero cancelled bookings with collected money — but it's the policy question to be aware of once real deposit traffic starts.

## One housekeeping note
Most of those cancelled rows are **my test bookings** (Funnel Test, Guest Test, Hello tiktok, plus the SP-260711-xxxx ones I created while verifying the funnel earlier). They're harmless — ₫0 collected, no revenue impact — but they clutter your Bookings list. Want me to clean up the test bookings so your list only shows real customers?
